# Skills and evals review, 2026-11-28

Scope: all 173 skills in `packages/skills`, `packages/jj`, `packages/agents` and `packages/memory`, and their eval cases.
One reviewing agent per skill (`anthropic/claude-fable-5-2`, medium thinking). Evals ran on `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`;
`llm` graders were judged by Fable 5.2. No skill was edited: everything below under "Skill" is a recommendation.

## Result

- Eval cases: 418 before, 970 after, in all 173 skills (39 had none). All load with `--list`, 0 load errors.
- Case changes reported by the agents: 433 added, 53 fixed, 415 left failing on purpose, 219 removed (almost all are trial cases the agent wrote and dropped because they did not discriminate).
- Two cases that existed before were deleted and replaced: `accessibility-review/value-no-parsing-criterion` and `design-critique/value-unreadable-figma-link` (both scored 1.00 with and without the skill).
- Value cases: 241 in total. 115 of them, in 89 skills, discriminate on Haiku as reported by the agents (with the skill >= 0.8, without <= 0.5, 3 runs).
- Skill findings: 903 (184 high, 290 medium, 429 low). By area: accuracy 232, instructions 199, description 177, overlap 130, no-measurable-value 92, structure 73.

## How far to trust the numbers

The scores are the agents' own, from 3 runs per case. I re-ran a random sample of 10 "discriminating" value cases at 2 runs:
9 still scored higher with the skill (mean difference +0.52), 4 met the 0.8 / 0.5 bar again, and one inverted
(`godot-gdextension/value-load-and-compat-rules`: 0.33 with, 0.58 without). Treat a single case's score as noisy; 3 runs is too few for a gate.

Many cases fail on purpose. A trigger that a fair prompt does not route, or a value case that only works once the description
is rewritten, was left failing so the problem stays visible. Do not use the suite as a pass/fail gate until the skill fixes are in.

## Patterns across skills

- **Haiku often does not open a skill.** With all skills loaded and an empty workspace it looks for files, finds none and answers from memory. 177 description findings in total; most come with a replacement description, and each suggestion says whether it was tested on a copy and what it scored.
- **Much skill content adds nothing for Haiku.** 92 findings where rules scored the same with and without the skill. What does discriminate is mostly output contracts, project-specific defaults and facts newer than the model.
- **Dangling references.** Several dozen skills name sibling skills or agents that are not in this repo (leftovers from the claude-plugins layout, e.g. `plugin:skill` names).
- **Claude Code leftovers in evals.** Cases that used `/plugin:skill` commands, `scaffold.sh` or the Agent tool scored 0 in both arms under the pi runner; the agents rewrote them to `/skill:<name>` with files pasted into the prompt (doc-tidy, fact-check, fresh-eyes, pr-comments, privacy-review).
- **Overlap.** 130 findings where two skills claim the same job or their evals use the same prompt for different skills.

## Per skill

### accessibility-review

The skill is accurate (55-criteria reference and the 2.5.8 / 3.3.8 claims check out against W3C), but for Haiku its WCAG knowledge adds nothing measurable: three knowledge-based value ideas scored the same with and without it. The only measurable effect is the report format, and one fair explicit trigger prompt never routes (0/3, twice). Evals now hold 3 routing cases (2 pass, 1 left failing as a description problem) and 2 value cases (one discriminating on format only, one kept as a non-discriminating guard); all 5 load without errors.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs (--all-skills, Haiku); failing: route-checkout-mockup-before-handoff (0/3, same in the first run). route-implicit-keyboard-complaint 3/3 (2/3 in the first run), route-negative-game-accessibility-options 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-audit-report-contract`: 0.92 with, 0.25 without
- `value-target-size-24px`: 1.00 with, 0.92 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/accessibility-review/SKILL.md:3 - the description triggers on the words audit / a11y / WCAG but not on the user's situation. The case route-checkout-mockup-before-handoff (mockup values, 'problem for people with low vision or who can't use a mouse well', before dev handoff) scored 0/3 in two separate runs with --all-skills on Haiku: the event logs show no tool call at all, Haiku answered directly. The implicit case that mentions a compliance standard routed 2/3 then 3/3.
  - Suggested: Rewrite the description to: "Audits a design, mockup, spec or page for accessibility barriers against WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, focus visibility, target size, keyboard and dragging alternatives, labels, errors and authentication. Use whenever someone asks if a screen works for people with low vision, keyboard-only or motor-impaired users, shares colors, sizes or focus styles to check before handoff, or says \"audit accessibility\", \"check a11y\", \"is this accessible?\", \"does this meet WCAG / ADA / EAA\". Read it before answering even when the values are all in the prompt. Not for game accessibility options (game-ui) or a single rule lookup (uiux-lookup)."
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** On WCAG substance the skill changed nothing for Haiku. Tried at 3 runs each: (1) original value-no-parsing-criterion (do not cite 4.1.1): with 1.00 / without 1.00; (2) target size incl. 24px rule, spacing, equivalent-control and user-agent exceptions: with 0.92-1.00 / without 0.92-1.00; (3) contractor findings to validate (4.1.1 removed, 2.4.11 partly obscured is AAA, 3.3.8 object-recognition exception, paste blocked, 32px vs 44px): with 0.89 / without 1.00. SKILL.md:19-50 and :113-119 restate what the model already knows. The only discriminating effect is the output template (SKILL.md:63-109): value-audit-report-contract with 0.92 / without 0.25, and that difference is format; without the skill Haiku already computed the same contrast ratios and listed unverifiable items separately.
  - Suggested: Cut the criteria list in SKILL.md:23-50 down to the rules that are skill-specific decisions (procedure order, severity scale, open-items-not-passes, output template) and leave the criterion catalogue to references/wcag-22-aa.md. Judge the skill on the report contract, not on WCAG recall.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/accessibility-review/SKILL.md:15-16 delegate to `screen-reader-testing`, `web-development` and the `ui-critic` agent. None of them exists in this repo's four skills dirs or in packages/agents/agents (grep finds ui-critic only as a mention in other skills). On this machine `screen-reader-testing` exists only as a global skill in ~/.agents/skills and the web skill there is called `efficient-web-development`; no `web-development` and no `ui-critic` agent were found.
  - Suggested: Name only targets that ship with the package, or describe the hand-off without a name ("manual screen reader testing is out of scope; recommend it for ..."). Replace `web-development` with the actual skill name or drop it; drop `ui-critic` unless the agent is added.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/accessibility-review/SKILL.md:10 - "Target: the arguments given with the command" is a leftover from a slash-command template; a pi skill gets no arguments, so the line points at nothing.
  - Suggested: Delete the line, or replace with "Target: the design, page or files the user names."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/accessibility-review/SKILL.md:38 - the spacing exception is worded as the circle not overlapping "another target or its circle". In run value1 (with#0) Haiku with the skill loaded passed 20x20 targets with a 2 px gap: it checked only circle-vs-neighbouring-target (12 px reach, touching) and skipped circle-vs-circle (centres 22 px apart, overlapping). One run of three, so weak evidence.
  - Suggested: Add the shortcut the W3C example implies: "For a row of equal undersized targets this means centre-to-centre distance >= 24 px (20x20 with a 4 px gap passes, 20x20 with a 2 px gap fails)."
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/accessibility-review/SKILL.md:65-109 - the output template takes 45 of 119 lines and is always applied in full; in the with-skill runs Haiku emitted empty 'Keyboard and Focus' and 'Intended Screen Reader Output' tables for a static frame where nothing can be filled in.
  - Suggested: Add one line after the template: "Omit a section that has no rows for this material; for a quick question about one criterion answer directly without the template."

**Eval changes**

- added: `route-checkout-mockup-before-handoff`. Explicit positive trigger without skill name, 'audit', 'a11y' or 'WCAG': mockup values checked for low-vision and motor barriers before handoff. Fails 0/3 with --all-skills on Haiku in both runs (no skill read, direct answer). Left failing; it is a description problem.
- added: `route-implicit-keyboard-complaint`. Implicit positive trigger: keyboard user's complaint (sticky header hides focus, drag-only list) plus a procurement compliance question. 2/3 in the first run, 3/3 in the final run.
- added: `route-negative-game-accessibility-options`. Near-miss negative (min 0, max 0): accessibility options tab for a Godot game belongs to game-ui. 3/3 in both runs.
- removed: `value-no-parsing-criterion`. Did not discriminate: with 1.00 / without 1.00 at 3 runs; Haiku already avoids 4.1.1. A reworked variant (contractor findings incl. 4.1.1, 2.4.11 partial, 3.3.8 exceptions) also did not discriminate (0.89 / 1.00) and was not kept.
- added: `value-audit-report-contract`. Replaces the removed case. Free-form audit of a static mockup spec; 4 regex graders on the last message for the skill's report contract (principle headings, Critical/Major/Minor, contrast table with Ratio and Required, a section for unverifiable items). Final: with 0.92 / without 0.25. It measures format adherence, not knowledge; the unverifiable-items grader is lenient because the bare model does that too.
- left-failing: `value-target-size-24px`. Original scored with 0.95 / without 1.00. Hardened in place: boundary-ambiguous 20px/2px item replaced by the W3C example (20x20 with 4 px gap passes) and a clear fail (16x16 with 4 px gap), plus equivalent-control and user-agent-control exceptions; graders renamed to match. Still does not discriminate (final with 1.00 / without 0.92). Kept as a correctness guard, not as evidence of value; remove it if only discriminating cases should stay.

### android

The skill's content is accurate and clearly helps Haiku once it is read (targetSdk facts: 1.00 with vs 0.17 without), but with the current description Haiku rarely opens it. The implicit process-death trigger was never read in 9 runs against 170 competing skills, and neither new value case reaches the keep bar until the description is rewritten; a tested rewrite fixes both. Evals now hold 7 cases that all load: 2 positive triggers, 2 negatives (one new near-miss), 2 new value cases left failing on the description, and the old scaffold-based room-migration case, which I could not run.

**Routing:** Current description, --all-skills, Haiku, 3 runs (final run): 2/4 cases pass. Passing: not-android-swiftui 1.00, route-negative-minsdk-manifest-merger 1.00. Failing: trigger-android-1 0.67, trigger-android-2 0.00. Skill loaded alone: both triggers 1.00. Tested description rewrite with all skills: 4/4 at 1.00.

**Value cases:**

- `value-targetsdk-36-impact`: 0.50 with, 0.08 without
- `value-data-layer-review`: 0.40 with, 0.53 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/android/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded, Haiku does not open the skill for fair in-scope prompts. trigger-android-2 (form fields empty after the app is backgrounded) scored 0/9 over three all-skills runs; trigger-android-1 (the exact Room error string) was flaky at 0.33, 0.67 and 1.00. Loaded alone, both triggers score 1.00, so the skill is not losing to a sibling: it is simply not opened. The description opens with 'Writes and debugs Android app code', so question, review and impact-sheet prompts with no files do not read as a match. In the value runs with only this skill loaded, Haiku opened it in 1 of 6 with-arm runs.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: 'Android app architecture, lifecycle, persistence and platform behavior outside the UI toolkit. Read before answering, reviewing or writing anything about ViewModel state, SavedStateHandle and process death, repeatOnLifecycle, repositories and use cases, Hilt, Room migrations and DAOs, DataStore, WorkManager, foreground services, or what changes when targetSdk is raised to 35 or 36, even when no project files are present: it holds project defaults and version-specific facts that are easy to get wrong from memory. Typical symptoms: "A migration from 3 to 4 was required but not found", form input lost after the process is killed, a StateFlow that reloads on every rotation, "cannot be provided without an @Inject constructor".' Scores with this text, all skills, Haiku, 3 runs: trigger-android-1 1.00, trigger-android-2 1.00 (0.00 in a same-layout control with the original text), both negatives 1.00 (android-build was read instead on the near-miss). Value cases with it: targetsdk 1.00 vs 0.17, data-layer review 0.80 vs 0.47. Not tested: whether the broader text takes prompts away from kotlin, jetpack-compose or android-testing.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/android/references/architecture.md:9 holds the rule 'A use case that only forwards to a repository is noise', but SKILL.md never mentions use cases or the domain layer, and the table row at SKILL.md:38 ('Layers, modules, mappers, error types, where logic lives') gives no cue to open the reference for a review. In value-data-layer-review with the tested description, Haiku read SKILL.md in 3/3 runs, never opened architecture.md, and kept the forwarding use case every time (grader l1 0/3). The two rules that are in SKILL.md itself (line 25 one-shot events, line 31 no withContext around Room suspend DAOs) were applied 3/3.
  - Suggested: Add one bullet under '## Data layer' in SKILL.md: 'Add a use case only when logic is shared by several ViewModels or complex enough to test alone; one that only forwards to a repository is noise.' Also add 'use cases, domain layer' to the table row at SKILL.md:38.
- **low, structure.** The skill routes to skills that are in none of the four skills directories of this repo: `android-skills:android-intent-security`, `android-skills:android-permissions-security` and `android-skills:navigation-3` (SKILL.md:10), `android-skills:android-permissions-security` (references/background-work.md:27), `android-skills:edge-to-edge`, `android-skills:navigation-event` and `android-skills:adaptive` (references/behavior-changes.md:9, 23, 24). An agent without that external plugin is sent to a skill it cannot load. The in-repo names on SKILL.md:10 (jetpack-compose, android-build, android-testing, android-device, kotlin) all exist.
  - Suggested: Say once in SKILL.md that `android-skills:*` is an optional external plugin and what to do when it is absent (answer from the platform docs), or drop the names and describe the excluded topic only.
- **low, overlap.** SKILL.md:25 (one-shot events: a SharedFlow or Channel drops or buffers events when nobody collects) answers the same question as the kotlin skill's description trigger 'events lost from a MutableSharedFlow' and its case kotlin/trigger-kotlin-2 (a navigation event lost while the screen starts). SKILL.md:12 splits ownership as 'delivery semantics' to kotlin and 'lifecycle subscription' to android, but a lost UI event fits both and the line resolves it only with 'loads both'.
  - Suggested: State the tie-break in SKILL.md:12, for example: 'An event lost between a ViewModel and its screen is this skill; an event lost between two coroutines with no lifecycle involved is `kotlin`.'

**Eval changes**

- left-failing: `android/value-targetsdk-36-impact`. New value case. Four facts from references/behavior-changes.md (setInterruptionFilter becomes an app rule at 35; onBackPressed not dispatched, at most one missed scheduleAtFixedRate run and elegantTextHeight ignored at 36), each graded by a regex on a fixed final line. Current description: 0.50 with vs 0.08 without, because Haiku opened the skill in 1 of 3 runs. Tested description rewrite: 1.00 vs 0.17, with skill and reference read 3/3. Kept under the description exception.
- left-failing: `android/value-data-layer-review`. New value case. Five-line KEEP/CHANGE review: forwarding use case, withContext around a suspend Room DAO call and a Channel for a one-shot event should be CHANGE; entity mapping and WhileSubscribed(5_000) should be KEEP. Five regex graders on the final lines. Current description: 0.40 with vs 0.53 without (skill opened 0/3). Tested rewrite: 0.80 vs 0.47. The l1 grader (forwarding use case) fails even when the skill is read, because that rule is only in references/architecture.md:9; left failing as evidence for the instructions finding.
- added: `android/route-negative-minsdk-manifest-merger`. Near-miss negative: an Android app whose build fails with 'Manifest merger failed ... minSdkVersion' belongs to android-build. Grader requires zero reads of the android skill. All skills: 1.00 at 3 runs with both the current and the rewritten description. It scores 0.67 when android is the only skill loaded, which is expected and not the intended mode.
- left-failing: `android/trigger-android-2`. Unchanged. Fair implicit trigger (fields empty after backgrounding, values in a ViewModel StateFlow). All skills: 0.00 in all three runs (0/9); skill alone: 1.00; tested rewrite with all skills: 1.00. Description problem, not a case problem.
- left-failing: `android/trigger-android-1`. Unchanged. Flaky with all skills on the current description: 0.33, 0.67 (final run) and 1.00 (control); 1.00 alone and 1.00 with the rewrite. The prompt quotes the Room error string that the description also quotes verbatim; kept because it is the literal message a user would paste.
- left-failing: `android/room-migration`. Unchanged and not run: it needs --scaffold plus Write/Edit/Bash, which were off limits here. Graders read sound on inspection (file-targeted regex, llm grader with explicit PASS and FAIL). Its status is unverified, not confirmed failing.
- removed: `android/value-one-shot-event`. Candidate created and deleted in this session, never pre-existing. Multiple-choice on the one-shot event mechanism: Haiku picked the state-field answer 3/3 without the skill, so it measured nothing.

### android-build

The skill routes perfectly when loaded alone (3/3 on all three positive triggers) but is almost never opened by Haiku with all 173 skills loaded (1 of 9 positive runs); a tested description rewrite takes that to 9/9 without breaking either negative. The evals now have an implicit trigger, a near-miss negative and one discriminating regex-graded value case (1.00 with, 0.00 without); five other value ideas showed no difference on Haiku. The existing outcome case release-keep-rule was not run because it needs --scaffold and --allow-tools, which were off limits. The skill has one inverted rule (missingDimensionStrategy), a misleading keep-rule description and seven pointers to skills that do not exist in this repo.

**Routing:** 2/5 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (current description); passing: not-android-build-maven 3/3, route-negative-config-cache-convention-plugin 3/3; failing: trigger-android-build-1 1/3, trigger-android-build-2 0/3, route-implicit-qa-staging-build 0/3. Skill loaded alone: all three positives 3/3. With the tested description rewrite and --all-skills: 5/5 cases pass at 3 runs.

**Value cases:**

- `value-release-only-keep-file`: 1.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/android-build/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded Haiku does not open the skill on fair triggers: trigger-android-build-1 scored 0/3 and then 1/3, trigger-android-build-2 0/3 twice, route-implicit-qa-staging-build 0/3 twice. In those runs no SKILL.md of any skill was read; Haiku searched the empty workspace and answered from memory, so this is 'never opened', not a loss to a sibling. ### android-device

The skill is accurate and compact, but on Haiku it is rarely opened when all skills compete (2/6 routing cases pass; the four positives swing between 0/3 and 3/3 across identical runs, while all pass with the skill loaded alone), and a tested description rewrite brought the positives to 12/12 with both negatives still clean. No value case was kept: four different ideas all scored 1.00 without the skill, so for Haiku the skill showed no measurable value on what I tried. The evals now hold 4 positive triggers, 2 negatives (one a real near miss) and the pre-existing scaffold-based outcome case, which I could not run under the no --scaffold/--allow-tools rule.

**Routing:** 2/6 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run r7-routing-all): not-android-device-docker 1.00 and route-negative-compose-test-on-device 1.00 pass; failing: trigger-android-device-1 0.00, trigger-android-device-2 0.33, route-two-devices-install-error 0.33, route-implicit-link-opens-in-browser 0.00. Skill loaded alone: 6/6 at 1.00. Tested description rewrite with --all-skills: 6/6 at 1.00. --list loads all 7 cases with 0 load errors.

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/android-device/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded Haiku mostly answers adb questions from memory without opening the skill. Original description, --all-skills, 3 runs each: trigger-android-device-1 scored 0.00 / 1.00 / 0.00 over three invocations, trigger-android-device-2 0.67 / 0.00 / 0.33, route-two-devices-install-error 0.00 / 0.33, route-implicit-link-opens-in-browser 0.00 / 0.00. Event logs show no tool call at all in the failing runs (no sibling was read), and all four score 1.00 with the skill loaded alone, so this is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite (copy in /tmp/skill-evals/android-device/alt, --all-skills, 3 runs): all four positives 1.00 (12/12 runs), both negatives 1.00. Text: 'Finds why an Android app crashes or closes on a phone or emulator, and runs adb against one device safely. Read it before giving any adb or logcat command. Use for an app that closes on launch with no error, reading a "Caused by" chain or native tombstone off the device, INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE or other INSTALL_FAILED errors, "more than one device/emulator" with a phone and an emulator both attached, pm grant and revoke, and opening a URL or deep link in the app with am start. Pins one serial and asks before uninstall, pm clear or wiping data.' Only one invocation per case set was run against the rewrite, and the original is noisy, so treat 12/12 as strong but not final.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** Four value ideas were tried on Haiku at 3 runs and none discriminated; all were removed again. (1) SKILL.md:22, what ./gradlew installDebug does with two devices attached: with 1.00, without 1.00. (2) SKILL.md:32, reading a native crash on an unrooted phone via dumpsys dropbox data_app_native_crash: 1.00 / 1.00. (3) SKILL.md:45-53, an ASK/RUN table over uninstall -k, adb root, sdkmanager system image, force-stop, run-as: 1.00 / 1.00. (4) SKILL.md:30 and :57-59, free-form commands for a crash that already happened (crash buffer, no logcat -c, -d, no --pid, pinned serial): with 0.81, without 1.00. In (1) to (3) the with arm did read the skill, so the result is not a routing artefact. In (4) two of three with-arm runs did not open the skill even though it was the only one loaded.
  - Suggested: The rules Haiku already follows unaided (pin the serial, -b crash, -d, ask before uninstall, dropbox for native crashes) could be cut to a short checklist. Value for a small model would have to come from content it does not have: for example a decision table for process death without a crash (events buffer tags versus dumpsys activity exit-info), or OEM- and API-level-specific behaviour. The agentic procedure (the logcat-crash case with a fake adb) may still show value, but it needs Bash and was outside what I could run.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/android-device/SKILL.md:40 and references/adb.md:29. 'Single-quote the URI so the local shell does not split on &' is incomplete: adb shell joins its arguments and hands them to the device shell, which then sees a bare & and backgrounds the command, so the app receives the URL cut at the first &. Not verified on a device; a source search returned matching reports (superuser.com/questions/1755859, wix/Detox issue 2549) but no passages were retrieved.
  - Suggested: Change the example to quote for the device shell as well, e.g. adb -s <serial> shell "am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d 'https://example.com/item?id=1&x=2' <appId>", and reword the note to 'quote the whole remote command; the device shell also treats & as a control operator'.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/android-device/SKILL.md:30. The step says to read -b crash but not what the buffer holds; that is only in references/logcat.md:10. In the one free-form run where Haiku read SKILL.md (r3-value, with-1) it wrote that an uncaught Java exception 'is usually logged under AndroidRuntime in the main buffer, not the crash buffer' and added a second full logcat dump.
  - Suggested: Add half a sentence at SKILL.md:30: 'the crash buffer holds the FATAL EXCEPTION block of uncaught Java/Kotlin exceptions and native crash summaries, and survives after main has rolled over'.
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/android-device/SKILL.md:10 routes to android-skills:android-cli and android-skills:anr-audit-and-fix, which exist in none of the four skills directories of this repo. packages/skills/skills/android-performance/SKILL.md:10 explains that these names belong to the third-party android-skills plugin 'if installed'; android-device does not.
  - Suggested: Add the same qualifier as android-performance ('the android-skills: names are the third-party android-skills plugin, if installed'), so a model does not go looking for a skill that is not there.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/android-device/SKILL.md:22 says ./gradlew installDebug installs on every connected device and tells the reader to use assembleDebug plus adb install instead, while SKILL.md:15 recommends exporting ANDROID_SERIAL. To my knowledge the Android Gradle Plugin honours ANDROID_SERIAL for install tasks, which would make line 22 too absolute; I did not verify this against documentation.
  - Suggested: After checking the AGP behaviour, reword to 'installs on every connected device unless ANDROID_SERIAL is set'.

Routing is solid: all three routing cases (two positives, one near-miss negative) pass 3/3 on Haiku with all skills loaded. External facts in the skill (IETF draft revision 07 expired, RFC 9110 wording) were not checked against documentation.

**Routing:** 3/3 routing cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (route-idempotency-vs-webhooks, route-double-order-implicit, route-quiet-rate-limit-headers). The value case run the same way scores 0.48 because the skill is not read (0/3); with the suggested description all 4 cases score 1.00.

**Value cases:**

- `value-open-design-decisions`: 0.48 with, 0.52 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/api-idempotency/SKILL.md:3. Haiku does not open the skill when the user asks a short, self-contained idempotency question (pick A or B, or OK/FINDING on a pasted design). On value-open-design-decisions with the current description the skill was read in 0/3 runs loaded alone (with 0.48, without 0.52) and 0/3 with all skills (0.48). Over all exploratory value runs with the current description it was read in 2 of 15. Design-style prompts ('how do we change the endpoint') do open it (routing 9/9), so the description is found; it just does not tell the model that its own answer will be wrong. A milder rewrite that only added 'reviews ... reviewing an idempotency or retry design or its docs before it ships' opened it in 2 of 6 runs, so that alone is not enough.
  - Suggested: Tested text: "Designs and reviews idempotency keys and safe retries for HTTP APIs, server and client. Use when adding an Idempotency-Key header, fixing duplicate or double-submitted writes, reviewing an idempotency or retry design or settling its open questions, auditing a key implementation for races (atomic claim, in-flight state, replay window), or setting client retry policy, full-jitter backoff, retry budgets and SDK retry defaults. Read it before answering even a short either-or question on these, because several of its rules contradict the cautious default." Tested on a copy with only the description changed: skill alone, value-open-design-decisions read 3/3 and scored 1.00 (bare 0.52); a second review-style value prompt read 3/3 and scored 0.88 (bare about 0.4). With all 173 skills loaded: value case 1.00 (read 3/3), both positive routing cases 3/3, the rate-limit negative still 3/3 quiet.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/api-idempotency/SKILL.md:34 ('Decide explicitly whether a stored failure replays verbatim or may be re-attempted') and references/key-lifecycle.md:41. In an exploratory review case (removed to stay within the case cap) a design that stored a 500, replayed it verbatim, required a new key to try again and documented this was marked FINDING by Haiku in 4 of 5 runs where it had read SKILL.md. Its reasoning: a 500 on a card charge may hide an unknown vendor outcome, taken from the recovery-point paragraph at SKILL.md:61. The skill never says that replaying a stored 5xx is an acceptable choice, nor what makes it acceptable, so the model falls back to 'never cache a 500'.
  - Suggested: Extend SKILL.md:34: "Store both outcomes. Replaying a stored failure verbatim (the client must send a new key to try again) is a valid choice, and so is re-attempting; either is fine once it is decided and documented. Replay is only safe for a 5xx when the vendor outcome cannot be left unknown: the completer or the derived vendor key (section 3) resolves it. Leaving it undecided is the finding, not the replay."
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/api-idempotency/references/backoff-jitter.md:18 contradicts the default at references/backoff-jitter.md:9 and SKILL.md:76. The 'documented schedule integrators can copy' is `min(1000 * 2^attempt, 30000)` plus up to one second of random jitter, which is exponential backoff with small additive jitter (waits of about 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s stay nearly synchronized), not full jitter. The tenacity example on the same line, `wait_exponential_jitter(initial=1, max=10)`, is also exponential plus additive jitter (tenacity's full-jitter helper is `wait_random_exponential`; not checked against current tenacity docs).
  - Suggested: Rewrite the example as full jitter: "`random(0, min(30000, 1000 * 2^attempt))` milliseconds, so waits drawn from up to 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, capped at 30s", and use `wait_random_exponential(multiplier=1, max=30)` for the tenacity example after confirming it in the tenacity docs.
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/api-idempotency/SKILL.md:8 names a `postgres` skill and SKILL.md:80 names `python` and `coding`. None of the three exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills (only `mysql` and `codebase-design` are close). The 'if installed' hedge keeps it from being wrong, but line 80 sends the reader to 'the repo-wide retry policy' in a skill this repo does not ship.
  - Suggested: Drop the `python` and `coding` pointer from SKILL.md:80 (keep 'Use the language's retry library (tenacity, Resilience4j, or equivalent) before hand-rolling.') and either remove `postgres` from SKILL.md:8 or keep it only as a topic: 'Postgres locking and index details are out of scope'.

### api-keys

The skill routes well on Haiku with all skills loaded (explicit trigger 3/3, near-miss negative 3/3 quiet, implicit trigger 2/3), but it adds almost nothing Haiku does not already know: entropy maths, SHA-256 over argon2id, 401 vs 403, deactivate-before-delete, rate limits, CI federation and "rebuilding OAuth" were all answered correctly without it. The one rule that flips Haiku's answer (extend a routine rotation window while the old key still has traffic) sits only in the reference file, which Haiku does not open, so the single value case is left failing at 0.00/0.00 and scores 1.00/0.00 with a tested one-sentence addition to SKILL.md. The evals now hold 4 cases (1 pre-existing and untouched, 3 new), all loading without errors; 9 runner invocations were used.

**Routing:** 3 routing cases with --all-skills on Haiku at 3 runs: 2/3 pass fully (route-keys-vs-auth 3/3, route-negative-vendor-key-in-app 3/3 quiet); failing: route-implicit-departed-engineer at 2/3 (0.67), the miss opens no skill. The pre-existing route-keys-vs-auth was left unchanged.

**Value cases:**

- `value-rotation-traffic-at-window-end`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, instructions.** The rule 'if traffic persists near the window's end, extend the window rather than break a live consumer' exists only in packages/skills/skills/api-keys/references/storage-and-rotation.md:50. SKILL.md:55-58 says only 'watch last_used_at until traffic stops' and 'never delete a key before its traffic reads zero'. In value-rotation-traffic-at-window-end Haiku read SKILL.md in 3/3 with-skill runs, never opened the reference, and chose 'cut off on schedule' 3/3, the same as without the skill (0.00 vs 0.00). SKILL.md:12 tells the model to read the reference 'when implementing', so a design or review question does not trigger it; across the with-skill value runs the reference was opened in 1 of 15.
  - Suggested: Append to SKILL.md:55: 'If the old key still has traffic near the end of its window on a routine roll, extend the window and tell the customer which caller is still on it. Do not cut off a live consumer on schedule.' Tested on a copy of the skill with only this change: the case scored 1.00 with, 0.00 without (3 runs, Haiku). Also change SKILL.md:12 from 'Read it when implementing any of those' to 'Read it when designing, implementing or reviewing any of those'; that second change was not tested.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** For Haiku the skill changed nothing on most of what was tried. Without the skill Haiku was 3/3 correct on: counting only the non-stored body characters toward entropy (reference :32; 5-format case 1.00 vs 1.00), plain SHA-256 instead of argon2id or salt/pepper (SKILL.md:41), an empty scope list meaning no access (:46), 403 for a missing scope (:50), rate limiting validation despite 190-bit keys (:51), workload identity for CI (:21), not rebuilding OAuth on static keys (:20), coarse scopes at launch (:47), deactivate before delete (:55), and immediate revoke on a confirmed leak (:57). An 8-item keep/change review scored 0.92 with, 0.88 without.

- **medium, instructions.** The offboarding rule is stated three ways. SKILL.md:57 says revoke at once with no grace and accept the downtime; SKILL.md:63 says 'a revoke-and-rotate pass'; references/storage-and-rotation.md:60 says a production integration on a personal key is 'a standing defect to migrate to a service account'. None says what happens to a leaver's key that is carrying production traffic at the moment of removal. Results on that exact question were unstable: in a keep/change item ('revoke the leaver's keys at once even when production runs on one') Haiku with the skill read answered KEEP in 6 of 8 runs but CHANGE in 2 of 3 runs of one prompt variant, quoting the ownership rule against the revoke rule; without the skill it answered CHANGE 9/9 in that form and 'revoke immediately' 3/3 when asked as multiple choice. No stable case could be built on it, so none was kept.

Make references/storage-and-rotation.md:60 say the migration happens before departure, or by issuing a new key after the revoke. Not tested.

On the api-keys prompt Haiku read only api-keys in 3/3 runs with all skills loaded; the sibling's case was not run (out of budget scope).
  - Suggested: Give hashing and storage of issued keys to api-keys alone: drop 'or how issued API keys are hashed and stored' from the api-oauth-provider description and have it point to api-keys for that. Keep 'keys versus OAuth' in one of the two descriptions, or word the split (api-keys: the platform has no user-delegated access yet; api-oauth-provider: third-party apps act for users). The MCP 2026-07-28 security considerations are stricter: 'For public clients, authorization servers MUST rotate refresh tokens' (checked against modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations). The MCP bullet at SKILL.md:42 does not mention it.
  - Suggested: Add to SKILL.md:42 or :50: when serving MCP, rotation for public clients is a MUST, and sender-constraining is not offered as an alternative.
- **low, accuracy.** SKILL.md:8 and :100 say draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1 was at revision 16 when checked in October 2026. The datatracker now shows draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-17 dated 31 October 2026, still an Internet-Draft. The other MCP claims I checked against the 2026-07-28 spec are correct (iss SHOULD including error responses and expected to become MUST, DCR deprecated, CIMD SHOULD, RFC 9728 MUST, scope hierarchies MUST, hostname display MUST, localhost warning SHOULD). I did not recheck the RFC 9700 and RFC 6749 citations.
  - Suggested: Update both lines to revision 17 (31 October 2026), or drop the revision number and keep only 'still an Internet-Draft, recheck before calling it an RFC'.

### api-webhooks

The skill clearly helps Haiku on the provider side (response-classification value case: 1.00 with, 0.33 without, stable over two 3-run batches) and routes 3/3 on an explicit outbound-design prompt, but its receiving-side half is not found: an implicit Stripe handler prompt routes 0/3 with all skills and 1/3 with the skill alone. The signing guidance is out of date against the current Standard Webhooks spec (v1a is deprecated in favour of v2a). Evals now hold 3 routing cases (explicit, implicit, near-miss negative) and 1 value case; the pre-existing case is untouched.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (same result in two batches); failing: route-implicit-stripe-signature-mismatch (0/3 with all skills, 1/3 with the skill alone, 3/3 alone with the tested description rewrite)

**Value cases:**

- `value-endpoint-response-actions`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/api-webhooks/SKILL.md:42, references/signing.md:10 and :30-33 describe asymmetric signing as `v1a` with ed25519 over the same `{id}.{timestamp}.{body}` content. The spec on main (github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks spec/standard-webhooks.md, still labelled 1.0.0, fetched during this review) says `v1a` is deprecated in favour of `v2a`: signed content is `endpoint_id.msg_id.timestamp.payload`, ed25519 signs the raw SHA-256 hash of that content, and one key pair per environment may be shared across endpoints. SKILL.md:105 says the spec was rechecked 2026-10-17, so either that check missed it or the spec changed since. The rest I checked matches the spec: 20 KB payload, 24 to 64 byte secret, whsec_/whsk_/whpk_ prefixes, the 10-step schedule to 75:35:05, 3xx as failure, 410 disable, 15 to 30 s timeout, no tolerance number.
  - Suggested: Replace `v1a` with `v2a` in SKILL.md:42 and signing.md (header example, Keys table), add the asymmetric signed content `endpoint_id.msg_id.timestamp.payload` hashed with SHA-256 before ed25519, state that the unique-key-per-endpoint rule (signing.md:35) applies to symmetric secrets only while an asymmetric pair can be shared per environment, note that `v1a` is deprecated, and update the recheck date.
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/api-webhooks/SKILL.md:3: the receiving side is only the last clause ('verifying and acknowledging a webhook your app receives'). The implicit case route-implicit-stripe-signature-mismatch (Stripe events rejected after a body-parser change, handler timing out) is read 1/3 with the skill loaded alone and 0/3 with --all-skills (two batches). In the failing runs Haiku runs ls/find, finds nothing and answers from memory, opening no skill at all, so this is 'never opened', not a loss to a sibling.
  - Suggested: Tested text: "Designs outbound webhooks (provider side) and fixes or reviews handlers that receive events from a third party (Stripe, GitHub, Slack). Use when adding webhooks to an API, defining the event catalog and payloads, implementing Standard Webhooks signing and secret rotation, reviewing a sender's retry, dead-letter or SSRF defenses, writing the delivery contract, delivery log, replay and test-event surface customers see, or when an endpoint that receives provider events fails signature verification or times out and needs raw-body verification and a fast acknowledgement. Not for deduplicating redelivered events by ID (api-idempotency)." Scores: skill alone, implicit case 3/3 (was 1/3) and negative 3/3; with --all-skills the implicit case stays 0/3, negative 3/3, explicit 3/3. So it fixes routing when the skill is a candidate but not the empty-workspace baseline. Do not add 'gets the same event re-sent' to the description: that variant was tested and made the dedup negative fire 2/3 with --all-skills.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/api-webhooks/SKILL.md:8 sends 'API key issuance' to `api-oauth-provider`, and SKILL.md:42 says key storage follows `api-oauth-provider`'s `references/api-key-storage.md`. The repo has a dedicated `api-keys` skill, and packages/skills/skills/api-keys/SKILL.md:34 says webhook signing secrets follow api-keys for storage and rotation. The two skills point to different owners. Also, api-key-storage.md:7 prescribes storing only a SHA-256 hash, which cannot work for an HMAC signing secret the sender must read back to sign; in one run Haiku wrote 'stored hashed or encrypted' from this pointer.
  - Suggested: SKILL.md:8: 'API key issuance (`api-keys`)'. SKILL.md:42: 'Storage and rotation of the secret follow `api-keys`, if installed, except that a symmetric signing secret must be stored encrypted and retrievable, not hash-only, because the sender needs it to sign.'
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/api-webhooks/SKILL.md:54 and references/delivery-and-lifecycle.md:38 say 'A persistent `4xx` other than `408` and `429` goes (straight) to the dead-letter queue', while the table at delivery-and-lifecycle.md:35 says other 4xx dead-letter with no qualifier. 'Persistent' and 'straight' pull in opposite directions (first response, or after repeats?). For 3xx (SKILL.md:54, delivery-and-lifecycle.md:29) the text says 'failure' without saying whether the event is retried or dead-lettered; Haiku chose RETRY in all 6 with-skill runs. Haiku answered dead-letter on the first 401/403/404 in 6/6 runs, so the ambiguity did not cost points here.
  - Suggested: Drop 'persistent': 'Any `4xx` other than `408` and `429` goes to the dead-letter queue on the first response.' For 3xx add the action: 'count as a failed attempt and retry on the schedule (or dead-letter), never follow the redirect'. Also mark the 4xx dead-letter rule as the skill's own rule, since the spec only says to treat other codes as failure.
- **low, description.** A second value idea, a KEEP/CHANGE review of six sender behaviours (per-attempt webhook-timestamp, redirects not followed, 5 s timeout, strict ordering that blocks the queue, disable-and-email, replay as a new event), scored 0.89 with and 0.89 without, so the skill adds nothing there for Haiku. In 2 of 3 with-skill runs Haiku did not open SKILL.md at all although the skill was the only one loaded and the prompt opened with 'review of our outbound webhook sender before GA' (description, SKILL.md:3, covers 'reviewing a sender's retry, dead-letter or SSRF defenses'). The case was dropped, not kept.
  - Suggested: Broaden the review trigger in the description from 'reviewing a sender's retry, dead-letter or SSRF defenses' to 'reviewing or auditing an existing webhook sender before launch'. Not tested.

**Eval changes**

Listed here only to record two weaknesses I left alone: the prompt repeats the description's own list (event catalog, payloads, signing, retries, delivery log), so it is an easy explicit trigger, and its frontmatter has runs: 1 and an ignored model: key.   - Suggested: Tested text (with git-flow, hubflow, trunk-based removed: all 4 positive triggers 3/3 and both negatives 3/3 under --all-skills on Haiku; with the duplicates still present only 1/4): description: 'Works in whichever branching model a repo already uses and says where a change belongs: which branch to cut from, where a production fix, hotfix or release has to be merged, tagged or cherry-picked, and what a `git flow` or `git hf` command will do before it runs. Covers git-flow (main + develop, feature/release/hotfix branches; git-flow-next, AVH or plain git), HubFlow (`git hf`, `[hubflow]` config) and trunk-based (short-lived branches, flags, release branches with cherry-picks). Use when a request mentions a develop branch, release/* or hotfix/* branches, "git flow feature start", "finish a release", "git flow init", "git hf", a fix for production while a release branch is open, patching an old release line, or asks which branching model a repo uses or whether to pick trunk-based or git-flow. Not for commit messages, rebasing or rewriting history (git-history), GitHub or Forgejo release notes (gh-release, forgejo-release) or opening a PR (gh-pr, forgejo-pr).'
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/branching-models/SKILL.md:3 and :32 name skills that do not exist in the repo's four skills directories: `git-commit` (only in the user's ~/.agents/skills) and `ship` (nowhere). PR work lives in gh-pr and forgejo-pr.

- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/branching-models/SKILL.md:3 claims "release branch cherry-pick" while packages/skills/skills/git-history/SKILL.md:3 claims 'cherry-pick backports' and 'backport a fix'. A plain 'backport this fix to release/1.4' has two owners. Not measured with an eval (new-case budget spent elsewhere).

SKILL.md:49 can drop '(per the README, unverified)' for winget: the README lists it.

### catchup

The skill's content measurably helps Haiku when it is read (briefing order, leaving out pre-gap facts, picking the phase change as the one next move), but Haiku opens it unreliably: with the current description it is skipped whenever the user pastes the state or names no repo, even when it is the only skill loaded. The eval set now has 8 cases (6 routing, 2 value), all loading cleanly; 4 are left failing on purpose because they pass only with the tested description rewrite. Nine runner invocations were used; one drafted near-miss negative (domain-modeling glossary prompt) was removed unrun to stay within the three-new-case limit.

**Routing:** 3/6 cases pass at 3 runs (--all-skills, Haiku): catchup-away 3/3, catchup-quiet-handoff 3/3, catchup-quiet-session-recover 3/3; failing: catchup-next 0.78 (skill fired 3/3, labelled Next move missing in one run), route-implicit-back-from-leave 1/3, catchup-term 0/3. With the tested description rewrite: 5/6 pass, only catchup-term fails at 1/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-briefing-order`: 0.44 with, 0.11 without
- `value-one-next-move`: 0.33 with, 0.00 without
- `catchup-next`: 0.67 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:3 - the description frames the skill as working 'from live project state' and lists four quoted phrases. Haiku only opens it when a prompt repeats those phrases. With the skill loaded ALONE, both new value prompts (owner back after a gap, state pasted in the prompt) opened it in 2 of 12 with-arm runs (runs r2/r3/r8). With all skills loaded, route-implicit-back-from-leave fired 1/3 and catchup-term 0/3 (Haiku searches for files, finds none, answers without any skill).
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite (alt copy, only the description changed): 'Briefs a human who lost the thread of a project after time away or a long agent run: what needs them first, what changed, what new terms mean, and one next move. Read this before answering whenever a user says they were away, are back, lost track or no longer recognise the project, or asks what happened, where things stand, what a coined term in a plan means or where to pick up, also when they paste the log, plan or status themselves instead of pointing at a repo. Read-only. Not for writing a handoff for a new agent session or recovering a crashed session (handoff).' Scores with this text: all-skills routing route-implicit-back-from-leave 1/3 -> 3/3, catchup-next 0.78 -> 1.00, catchup-term 0/3 -> 1/3, catchup-away 3/3 and both negatives 3/3 unchanged; value (skill alone) value-briefing-order 0.44 -> 1.00, value-one-next-move 0.33 -> 0.67 (1.00 in an earlier run), catchup-next 0.67 -> 1.00. The skill was opened in 9/9 value with-arm runs.
- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/references/catchup.md is a near-verbatim copy of catchup/SKILL.md (diff: title, one sentence in the intro, the missing 'Not for' block, 'skill' vs 'mode' at SKILL.md:35). handoff/SKILL.md:3 and :16 describe '--catchup' as a handoff mode, and evals/handoff/handoff-quiet-away says 'catchup was model-invocable before the merge', i.e. catchup was meant to be folded into handoff. Two copies of the same instructions will drift.
  - Suggested: Decide on one owner. Either delete the standalone catchup skill (and its evals) if the merge into handoff is final, or keep catchup as the model-invocable skill and have handoff --catchup point to it instead of carrying a copy. Note that handoff is disable-model-invocation, so removing catchup removes automatic routing for returning-human questions.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:13 sends crash recovery to a skill named `session-recover`. No such skill exists in the four skills directories; recovery is `handoff --recover` (handoff/SKILL.md:17, references/recover.md). SKILL.md:12 points to `handoff`, which is a manual command (disable-model-invocation) and cannot be auto-invoked.
  - Suggested: Replace lines 12-13 with: '- Writing a brief for a new agent session: the user runs `/handoff`.' and '- Recovering a session that died: the user runs `/handoff --recover`.'
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:17 says 'Read live state only' and gives no rule for when the repo is unreachable but the user pasted the log or plan. In catchup-next (r2, with-arm, 3/3 runs) Haiku read the skill, then set aside the four log lines and the red CI stated in the prompt, said it had 'no live state to cite', asked for a repo path, and searched /home/buck/Projects for the commit messages. In one run it gave no Next move at all although the user asked what to do next.
  - Suggested: Add to step 1: 'State the user pastes (log lines, a Status block, CI result) counts as live state: brief from it, cite it as "your pasted log", and say once that it was not checked against the repo. Do not search outside the working directory for the project. If there is no state at all, say so and make the Next move the one command that would produce it.'
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:23 ('Gloss each project-specific term inline at its first use') and :22 ('Skip terms they used themselves') pull in different directions: step 4 has no exemption for terms the human already uses. Not measured by an eval; a first value-case idea on this was dropped because the correct answer could not be pinned down from the text.
  - Suggested: Change line 23 to: 'Gloss each term coined or repurposed since their last touch inline at its first use, even when a New words section follows.'
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:18 ('Everything before it stays out') was followed in 6/7 runs that read the skill; in r8 value-briefing-order with-2 Haiku read the skill and still briefed the pre-gap fact (ORDER: E, A, B, D, C). The 'Before finishing' list (lines 39-43) has no check for it.
  - Suggested: Add a check to 'Before finishing': 'Nothing dated before the human's last touch is in the briefing.'

**Eval changes**

All skills loaded: 0/3, Haiku looks for docs/plans/paperthin-ports.md, finds nothing and answers without opening any skill. Skill loaded alone: 3/3. ### click-path-audit

On Haiku the skill is never opened with its current description: 0/6 positive routing runs with all skills loaded, and 0/3 reads even when it is the only skill loaded, so this is "never opened", not "loses to a sibling". A tested description rewrite fixes that (8/9 positive routing runs across three prompts, negative stays quiet) and makes the report-contract value case discriminate 1.00 with vs 0.00 without. The suite now has 4 cases (2 positive routing, 1 negative, 1 value) that all load cleanly; the 2 positive routing cases and the value case are left failing against the current skill on purpose.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run); failing: click-path-audit-vs-react (0/3), route-implicit-delete-toast-but-still-there (0/3); passing: route-negative-save-returns-422 (3/3 quiet). With the tested description rewrite the same cases scored 3/3, 2/3 and 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-report-names-pattern-and-evidence`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/click-path-audit/SKILL.md:3. Haiku never reads the skill when the handler code is in the prompt. With --all-skills: click-path-audit-vs-react 0/3 and route-implicit-delete-toast-but-still-there 0/3 (a third fair trigger, buttons that do nothing after a store refactor, also scored 0/3 before I dropped it for the case limit). With the skill loaded alone (with arm of the value cases, 9 runs) it was read 0 times, so no sibling is winning; the event logs show Haiku either searching the empty workspace or answering directly, with no skill read at all. The description opens with what the skill does internally and gives the model no reason to open it once it can see the code.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: "Use when a button, toggle or form submit does nothing, flips back, flickers, or shows success without the promised result even though each function and its tests pass; when someone asks what fires on a click; or to check every control on a page after a state or store refactor. Read it before answering, also when the handler code is pasted in the prompt: it gives the trace format, the six named bug patterns the report must use and the rule for labelling findings that were not run. Not for API or payload errors, styling or performance." Scored on Haiku with all 173 skills loaded, 3 runs each: click-path-audit-vs-react 3/3, store-refactor trigger 3/3, implicit delete-toast 2/3, negative (422 payload) 3/3 quiet; value case 1.00 with / 0.00 without. A first rewrite without the sentence "Read it before answering, also when the handler code is pasted..." (same symptoms, same exclusions) was also tested and scored 0/9, so that sentence is what does the work.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** Bug detection itself is not improved for Haiku. A seven-control case built on the skill's own patterns (two sequential undos, one effect interference through a store subscription, one missing transition, three clean traps where order makes a foreign reset harmless) scored 1.00 with and 1.00 without the skill at 3 runs each, and the with arm did not read the skill. I removed that case. The only measured value is the report contract (SKILL.md:42-49 pattern names, SKILL.md:54 `inferred` label): with the tested description 1.00 vs 0.00. Not tested: multi-file workspaces where the writers of a field must be found, which is where the side-effect map (SKILL.md:17-26) would be expected to matter; the eval rules here do not allow workspace files.
  - Suggested: Accept that for pasted, single-screen code the skill's value is the report format and evidence labelling, and say so in the description (the tested rewrite does). If detection value matters, it needs a scaffolded multi-file eval to show it.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/click-path-audit/SKILL.md:10 sends the reader to skills `react` and `problem-solving`. Neither exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills (problem-solving exists only under the user's own ~/.agents/skills, which does not count). The existing eval case name click-path-audit-vs-react assumes the same missing sibling.
  - Suggested: Reword line 10 without skill names: "Not for building or fixing components, API or data-shape bugs, styling, or performance profiling." If a pointer is wanted, name a skill that ships here (`vue` for Vue/Pinia component work).
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/click-path-audit/SKILL.md:12 claims Pinia actions as in scope, while packages/skills/skills/vue/SKILL.md:3 claims "debugging ... Pinia stores ... stale state". A Vue button that resets itself matches both descriptions and neither names the other. Not measured (no runs spent on the sibling).
  - Suggested: Add one boundary clause to line 10, for example: "A single Vue or Pinia reactivity bug goes to `vue`; use this skill when the fault is in the order of calls a control sets off."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/click-path-audit/SKILL.md:26 tells the agent to use "the codebase-memory MCP tools (`search_graph`, `trace_path`)" with only "when the repo is indexed" as the condition. Nothing in this package provides that server, and the skill gives no way to tell whether it is available.
  - Suggested: Make it conditional on the tool being present: "If `search_graph` and `trace_path` are available, use them to find every writer of a field; otherwise Grep for the field name and the setter names."

### codebase-design

The skill's content works on Haiku once it is opened, but with the current description it is never opened when all skills compete (0/6 reads on the two fair triggers) and only sometimes when loaded alone. The skill had no evals; there are now 5 cases in packages/skills/evals/codebase-design/ (3 routing, 2 value), all loading cleanly. Against the unmodified skill both positive routing cases and both value cases are left failing; against a tested description rewrite all five pass (routing 3/3 each with all skills, value 1.00 with vs 0.20 and 0.22 without).

**Routing:** Unmodified skill, --all-skills on Haiku: 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs; failing: route-forwarding-chain-reshape (0/3), route-implicit-brittle-mocked-tests (0/3). Loaded alone the same two score 3/3 and 2/3. With the tested description rewrite and --all-skills: 3/3 cases pass.

**Value cases:**

- `value-refactor-candidates-contract`: 0.47 with, 0.20 without
- `value-review-note-vocabulary`: 0.11 with, 0.11 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md:3 opens with "Shared vocabulary and method for designing deep modules" and lists triggers in the skill's own jargon (seam, deepening opportunities). With all skills loaded Haiku never read it on either positive trigger (0/3 and 0/3; the logs show only find/grep for the pasted class names, then an answer from memory). Loaded alone it was read 3/3 and 2/3 on the routing prompts, but 0/3 and 1/3 on the two value prompts, including one that says "find refactor candidates", a phrase that appears only in the body at SKILL.md:54.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite (only the description changed, in a copy under /tmp/skill-evals/codebase-design/alt): "Restructures code into fewer, deeper modules, each with a small interface. Decides which thin classes, wrappers or forwarding chains to merge, what callers should see, where an injected port is justified, and which tests to replace. Read it before answering, even when the code is pasted into the prompt, for \"how should I restructure this package\", \"what should the public surface be\", tests that need many mocks or break on internal renames, \"should this be an interface\", \"review the architecture\" or \"find refactor candidates\". Not for making one specific misuse impossible to write (mistake-proof), naming domain terms (domain-modeling) or enforcing import rules (ts-module-boundaries)." Scores with --all-skills on Haiku at 3 runs: both positive triggers 3/3, negative 3/3 (one run opened mistake-proof instead). Value cases with this text: 1.00 vs 0.20 and 1.00 vs 0.22. Caveat: I wrote the rewrite after the eval prompts, and its "many mocks" and "find refactor candidates" phrases are close to two of them, so expect somewhat lower numbers on unseen prompts.
- **medium, accuracy.** references/html-report.md:113 bans "layer, wrapper" as substitutes for module, but the same file's own examples use them (:52 "Delete 4 shallow wrappers", :122 "implementation absorbs the wrappers", :84 "6 thin layers"), and the glossary in SKILL.md:14-16 does not ban them at all. In the alt-description runs, Haiku read SKILL.md and still wrote "thin pass-through layers" in one of three findings.
  - Suggested: Pick one rule. Either drop "layer, wrapper" from html-report.md:113, or add them to the Avoid list at SKILL.md:16 and reword the examples at html-report.md:52, :84 and :122.
- **low, structure.** The candidate card is specified twice with different fields: references/architecture-review.md:43-48 lists Files, Problem, Solution, Benefits, Before/after diagram, Recommendation strength; references/html-report.md:48-55 lists Title, Badge row, Files, diagram, Problem, Solution, Wins, ADR callout. "Benefits" and "Wins" name the same field, and the dependency-category tag exists only in html-report.md:50.
  - Suggested: Keep the field list in html-report.md only and have architecture-review.md section 3 point to it, or use the same names (Wins) in both.
- **low, overlap.** Two named skills do not exist in the four skills directories of this repo: `adr-writing` (SKILL.md:10 and references/architecture-review.md:64 without an "if installed" hedge; :14 has one) and `planning` (references/architecture-review.md:58, hedged). `domain-modeling`, `api-rest-design` and `mistake-proof` do exist.
  - Suggested: Add "if installed" at SKILL.md:10 and architecture-review.md:64 for adr-writing, and replace the `planning` reference at architecture-review.md:58 with the questions themselves (they are already listed on that line).
- **low, instructions.** references/deepening.md:29 says a port needs "at least two adapters ... (typically production + test)". A test adapter can always be justified, so the rule as written never forbids a port, which undercuts SKILL.md:32 ("Don't add a seam unless something actually varies across it") and deepening.md:15 (no port for local-substitutable dependencies).

With the current description it rarely opens it: with all skills loaded two of three fair triggers never fire (0/6 each), and on the value case Haiku answers from the description alone and scores no better than without the skill (0.33 vs 0.41). The evals now hold 6 cases (3 positive routing, 2 negatives, 1 value); three are left failing as description problems, with a tested rewrite that lifts the value case to 1.00 vs 0.43 and the positive triggers to 15/18.

Loaded alone the positives score handoff 3/3, readme 2/3, implicit 3/3. With the tested description rewrite and all skills: 5/5 (15/15) for the first variant, 12/15 for the final suggested text (readme 1/3, implicit 2/3).

**Value cases:**

- `value-blind-brief-keep-drop`: 0.33 with, 0.41 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/cold-read/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded Haiku does not open the skill when the artifact is pasted into the request: cold-read-readme 0/6 and route-implicit-oncall-runbook 0/6 (runs r5-all, r15-final-all); it reads the pasted text itself and answers, which is exactly what line 28 forbids. No sibling was read instead, so this is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling': loaded alone the same cases score 2/3 and 3/3 (r6-alone). The same happens on the value case with only this skill loaded: SKILL.md opened in 2 of 12 with-runs, so the rule 'pass contents, never intent' (line 18, 29), which is not in the description, is never seen (with 0.33, without 0.41, r12-value).
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: "Checks whether a document, README, runbook, plan or other artifact makes sense to someone who was not there, by handing only its contents to a fresh subagent and reporting where a stranger would stall. Use for \"would someone new follow this?\", \"does this stand on its own?\", \"what will the next person trip over?\", \"I have looked at this too long to judge it\", or a fresh-eyes read before a handoff, publish or merge, also when the text is pasted into the request. Read this before judging the artifact yourself or writing the fresh reader's brief; the session that wrote or discussed it cannot do the read, and the brief has rules. Diagnoses only. Not for disproving a decision (doubt-review) or checking docs against code (docs-audit)." Scores on Haiku: value case 1.00 with / 0.43 without at 6 runs, skill opened 6/6 (r13-value-alt2). Routing with all skills: 12/15 (handoff 3/3, readme 1/3, implicit 2/3, both negatives 3/3; r14-alt2-all). Caveats: two of the quoted phrases are close to my own test prompts, so the gain may be partly overfit; I did not test whether the wider text steals prompts from readme or docs-audit beyond the two existing negatives.

In the eval harness (no Agent tool) Haiku noticed this and read the artifact itself anyway: r1-all/runs/cold-read/cold-read-readme/with-0.jsonl thinking says "the cold-read skill calls for a fresh subagent, and I don't have an agent tool ... I'll try to read it using only the file's contents"; in r5-all cold-read-handoff/with-0 it opened SKILL.md, then delivered its own review and told the user to run the fresh read later.

### debloat

debloat is a manual command (disable-model-invocation: true), so pi hides it from the model and it can only be loaded with /skill:debloat; when loaded it does change Haiku's behaviour on two of its rules (leave self-contradicting text alone and hand it to v0-rewrite; do not move a cross-file duplicate, hand it to docs-audit). It had no evals; it now has 5 cases (3 routing cases that assert it stays quiet, 2 value cases invoked through the slash command), all loading and passing. The main problems are in the skill: it is a near word-for-word duplicate of doc-tidy's --debloat mode, it names a skill that does not exist, and v0-rewrite hands work to it although no model can see it.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; all three assert the manual skill stays quiet (no positive trigger can pass while disable-model-invocation is set). Against the tested rewrite without the flag: both in-scope prompts fired 3/3, the near miss stayed quiet 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-leave-tight-and-drifted-alone`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without
- `value-cross-file-duplicate-not-moved`: 1.00 with, 0.13 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/debloat/SKILL.md:20-38 is the same content as the --debloat mode of doc-tidy (packages/skills/skills/doc-tidy/SKILL.md:29-31 and 35-36): same six bloat targets, same 'compress in place', same 'teaching prose earns its length', same MISS rule, same handoffs. Both are manual commands, so the user has two commands for one job and two texts to keep in sync. The same holds for the standalone reorder skill versus doc-tidy --reorder.
  - Suggested: Keep one. Either delete debloat and change packages/skills/skills/v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:13 to point at `doc-tidy --debloat`, or drop the --debloat mode from doc-tidy and have it point at debloat. Not tested; it is a packaging decision.
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/debloat/SKILL.md:3-4: with disable-model-invocation the skill is left out of pi's skill listing and out of skill-index, so no fair request can route to it. Confirmed: the in-scope prompts in route-quiet-wordy-contributing and route-quiet-implicit-accreted-qualifiers did not load it in 3/3 runs each with all skills on Haiku. Meanwhile packages/skills/skills/v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:13 tells the model 'Tightening wordy but current prose: use `debloat`', a handoff the model cannot follow. The description also has no 'Use when' or 'Not for' part.
  - Suggested: If it should be found by the model, remove line 4 and use: 'Tightens prose that is correct and current but has grown wordy (padding, stacked qualifiers and asides, fused sentences, walls of enumeration, a point restated nearby), cutting words and never a rule, fact or constraint. Use when asked to tighten, trim, shorten or cut down a doc, section or paragraph, or to make over-qualified sentences readable again. Not for docs that contradict themselves or read like a changelog (v0-rewrite), or docs that disagree with the code or repeat one fact across files (docs-audit).' Tested on a copy in /tmp/skill-evals/debloat/alt with all 173 skills on Haiku, 3 runs each: both in-scope prompts loaded debloat 3/3 and the drifted-doc near miss stayed quiet 3/3. If it should stay manual, keep the flag and fix v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:13 to say it is a command the user runs (/skill:debloat).

### dependency-vetting

The skill is accurate on every fact I checked against npm, pnpm and GitHub documentation, and it routes well on Haiku with all skills loaded. It had no evals; it now has four cases (two positive routing, one near-miss negative, one value case), all loading and passing, with the value case at 1.00 with the skill against 0.67 without in the final run (0.50 in the run before). Two other value ideas showed no difference on Haiku and were dropped, so the measurable value is narrow: the git-dependency gotcha.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku in the final run (first run: 2/3, route-implicit-lockfile-new-packages at 0.67). 10 runner invocations used in total. --list loads all 4 cases of this skill; the one load error printed belongs to devcontainer/value-waitfor-last-hook, not this skill.

**Value cases:**

- `value-fetch-without-executing`: 1.00 with, 0.67 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, no-measurable-value.** Two of three value ideas showed no effect on Haiku 5.5 at 3 runs. (1) Hardening facts at packages/skills/skills/dependency-vetting/SKILL.md:119-120 (pnpm minimumReleaseAge in minutes, npm min-release-age in days, pnpm 11 default 1440, npm 12 and pnpm 10 blocking install scripts): with 0.93, without 0.93; only the npm 12 default was missed, in one run of each arm. (2) Name-attack and verdict rules at references/name-attacks.md:203,246,248 and SKILL.md:108 (three strong signals means stop without downloading, uv first-index, pip --extra-index-url, PEP 503 normalization, MAL- advisory is malicious): with 1.00, without 1.00. Haiku already knows these. In both cases the with arm also mostly did not open the skill (it was read in 1 of 6 with-arm runs).
  - Suggested: No change needed for correctness. If the skill is trimmed, these sections are the ones a current model already knows; the commands, the fetch rules and the Gotchas section are where the skill adds something.
- **low, description.** packages/skills/skills/dependency-vetting/SKILL.md:3 routes task-shaped requests well (--all-skills on Haiku: direct trigger 3/3 in both runs, implicit lockfile trigger 2/3 then 3/3). It is not opened for a quiz-shaped question ('which of these fetch commands can execute package code'): with the skill loaded alone, 0 of 9 with-arm runs read it across three runs of two prompt wordings, so the model answered from memory and got the git-dependency case wrong.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite: "Checks whether an npm or PyPI package is safe to install (malware, typosquatting, dependency confusion, a compromised version). Fetches without running install code, scans with GuardDog and OSV, reads lifecycle scripts and build hooks. Use before adding or installing a package nobody on the team knows, when a lockfile diff or PR pulls in new packages, when an advisory names a bad version, or when deciding whether a command (npm pack, pip download, npm install --ignore-scripts) can execute an untrusted package's code." Result: routing with all skills 3/3 cases at 1.00 (original 0.67 on the implicit case in the first run, 1.00 in the final run, so the gain is within noise); on the quiz-shaped prompt the skill was read in only 1 of 6 with-arm runs, so the rewrite does not fix that. Optional; I would not change the description on this evidence alone.
- **low, instructions.** The one rule that measurably changed Haiku's answer sits last-but-four in the file: SKILL.md:125 (git dependency .npmrc can swap the git executable even with --ignore-scripts). Ground rule SKILL.md:14 and fetch step SKILL.md:70-73 list unsafe commands and safe fetches but say nothing about git or tarball URL dependencies. Haiku still applied it in 6 of 6 runs where it read the file, so this is about robustness, not a failure. The gotcha also does not name the control: per the GitHub changelog (2026-02-18 and 2026-06-09) npm 11.10+ has --allow-git (default all) and npm 12 defaults --allow-git and --allow-remote to none; SKILL.md:119 mentions only the script default of npm 12.
  - Suggested: Add to SKILL.md:14: "`npm install --ignore-scripts` of a git or tarball URL dependency (direct or transitive) on npm 11 and older". Add a line to step 5: "git or URL dependency: clone or curl it yourself into the empty directory; never let npm resolve it." In SKILL.md:119 or 125 add: "npm 11.10+: pass --allow-git=none (and --allow-remote=none on 11.15+); npm 12 defaults both to none."
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/nuget/SKILL.md:11 sends 'vetting whether a new third-party package is trustworthy' to dependency-vetting, but SKILL.md:3 and SKILL.md:10 cover npm and PyPI only; every command and both references are ecosystem-specific. A NuGet vetting request handed over this way lands in a skill with nothing for it.
  - Suggested: Add to SKILL.md:10: "Other ecosystems (NuGet, Maven, Go, crates): only the name check, OSV lookup and verdict table apply; the fetch and scan commands here do not." Or change the pointer in the nuget skill.
- **low, accuracy.** Not verified: SKILL.md:78-85 pins guarddog@3.2.0 and states that GuardDog runs in a kernel sandbox, fails when none is available, and should be run through `docker run --rm ghcr.io/datadog/guarddog` instead of --no-sandbox. I did not check this against GuardDog documentation. Verified as correct against docs: pnpm 11 minimumReleaseAge default 1440 (pnpm.io 11.0 release notes), npm min-release-age in days from 11.10.0 (npm config docs), npm 12 blocking dependency install scripts with approve-scripts writing allowScripts (docs.npmjs.com cli/v12), git dependency .npmrc code execution under --ignore-scripts (GitHub changelog).
  - Suggested: Check the GuardDog version pin, sandbox behaviour and image name against the GuardDog README before the next release of the skill.

### deprecation-migration

The skill content is sound and compact, and when Haiku reads it the one rule that contradicts its instinct (remove on zero measured usage, not on the announced date) is applied every time. The weak point is the description: with all skills loaded Haiku opens it for the "sunset the v1 API" prompt only (3/5 routing cases pass), and a tested rewrite brings routing to 5/5 and the value case from 0.83 to 1.00. The suite now has 6 cases (3 pre-existing left untouched, 3 added), all loading without errors; 13 runner invocations were used.

**Routing:** 3/5 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run r13); failing: depr-rename-column (0.00), route-implicit-orphaned-service (0.33). Both are 'never opened' (skill alone: 0.67 and 1.00). With the tested description rewrite: 5/5.

**Value cases:**

- `value-remove-on-usage-not-date`: 0.83 with, 0.50 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/deprecation-migration/SKILL.md:3. With --all-skills on Haiku the skill is not opened for fair in-scope prompts: depr-rename-column 0/3 in three separate runs (zero tool calls, answered from memory) and route-implicit-orphaned-service 0/3 and 1/3. Loaded alone the same prompts score 0.67 and 1.00, so it is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'. Even alone, the value prompt (libraries being retired, removal date arrived) opened the skill in only 1 of 3 runs.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite (copy in /tmp/skill-evals/deprecation-migration/alt, only the description changed): 'Plans retiring an API, service, library, feature or database column and moving its callers to the replacement: the keep-or-retire decision, who does the migration work, when to announce, when it is safe to delete, strangler/adapter/flag cutovers, and zero-downtime schema changes (rename, drop or retype a column) via expand/contract. Use for "sunset the v1 API", "get the other teams off the old library", "nobody owns this service but it is still called", "the removal date is here, can we delete it", "rename a column in production without downtime". Read it before answering such a question even when there is no code to look at: several rules here (remove on measured zero usage, the owner migrates the callers) differ from common practice. Not for the deploy plan itself (rollout-plan).' - **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/modernize/SKILL.md:3 claims the same trigger verbatim ("sunset the v1 API", 'plans a sunset ... move its consumers off it'), and packages/skills/skills/modernize/references/sunset.md is a near word-for-word copy of this skill's Principles, The decision and The process sections (SKILL.md:12-35).
