### design-critique

The skill is short and readable, but on Haiku its only measurable gain is the output contract; its stage-matching rule is overridden by its own template, and it points to an agent and a skill that do not exist. The eval set now has 3 routing cases (2 positive, 1 near-miss negative) and 2 value cases; all 5 load without errors. Two cases are left failing on purpose: the implicit routing trigger (description problem, tested rewrite lifts it from 0/3 to 2/3) and the early-wireframe value case (instructions problem, tested rewrite lifts it from 0.20-0.40 to 1.00).

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-implicit-onboarding-screen-feels-off (0/3; 1/3 with the skill alone; 2/3 with the tested description rewrite)

**Value cases:**

- `value-description-only-critique`: 0.83 with, 0.25 without
- `value-early-wireframe-stage`: 0.40 with, 0.20 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/design-critique/SKILL.md:26 ('Match the stage: early exploration gets questions about direction and structure') is one line, and the fixed Output template at SKILL.md:43-79 overrides it. In value-early-wireframe-stage Haiku read the skill and still filled the whole template for a gray-box wireframe: no questions asked in any with-skill run (asks-open-questions failed 6/6 across two runs of 3), the 12/14/12px spacing nit landed in the top three priorities with pixel values, and it gave '44pt' touch targets and contrast advice for undecided colours. Scores with/without: 0.20/0.20 in the first run, 0.40/0.20 in the final run.
  - Suggested: Replace SKILL.md:26 with a stage rule that overrides the template. Tested in a /tmp copy (only this change), with-skill arm only: value-early-wireframe-stage scored 1.00 at 3 runs. Text used: "Match the stage. This decides the shape of the answer, and it overrides the output template below: (a) Early exploration (sketch, gray-box wireframe, 'first pass', colours and type not chosen): do not fill in the template. Lead with at least three open questions about direction and structure (what the screen is for, grouping, order, what is missing), then up to three structural recommendations. Answer a polish question the user raises (spacing, alignment) in one sentence and defer it; it is never one of the top three points. Give no pixel values, colour values, contrast ratios or type sizes for things that are not decided yet, and skip the Consistency and Accessibility sections. (b) Refinement or final polish: use the full template; spacing, alignment and state details belong here."
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/design-critique/SKILL.md:3 lists only explicit phrasings ('critique this mockup', 'review this design') and only artefact types, not a screen described in words. route-implicit-onboarding-screen-feels-off ('something about the second onboarding screen in my figma file feels off... where does it go wrong?') scored 0/3 with all skills loaded (Haiku called no tool at all and answered from memory) and 1/3 with the skill loaded alone, so it is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'. route-pricing-comp-before-stakeholders scored 2/3 in the first all-skills run and 3/3 in the final one.
  - Suggested: Tested with all 173 skills loaded, 3 runs: implicit case 2/3 (from 0/3), pricing case 3/3, handoff negative still 3/3 quiet. Text tested: "Critiques a UI design that is not built yet: a mockup, wireframe, comp, Figma frame, screenshot, or a screen the user describes in words. Covers usability, visual hierarchy, consistency and obvious accessibility problems, matched to the stage of the design. Use whenever someone shares or describes a screen and asks for feedback, what is wrong with it, why it \"feels off\", or what to fix before a design review, even when they never say \"critique\" and attach no file. A rendered page or built UI goes to the ui-critic agent; a developer spec for an approved design goes to design-handoff." The ui-critic clause was kept for the test only; drop or repoint it per the accuracy finding (that variant is untested).
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/design-critique/SKILL.md:3 and :15 send rendered pages to a `ui-critic` agent. No such agent exists in the repo: packages/agents/agents holds only dependency-auditor, docs-lookup, research-analyst, reviewer, security-auditor, test-runner and test-writer, and a repo-wide grep finds `ui-critic` only in skill texts. ### docs-audit

The skill's content is sound, but on Haiku it is mostly not read: with 170 skills competing, 3 of 7 routing cases pass at 3 runs, and the two "one fact" cases go to the sibling ssot-consolidate, which claims the same job. I added an implicit trigger (passes 3/3), a README-polish near-miss negative (passes) and one value case that discriminates on the report contract (with 0.78, without 0.17). Five rule-based value ideas showed no difference, because Haiku either already gets the rule right or never opens SKILL.md when the material is pasted into the prompt.

**Routing:** 3/7 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (docs-audit-stale-setup-guide, docs-audit-quiet-imports, docs-audit-quiet-readme-polish). Failing: docs-audit-cli-drift (2/3 runs), docs-audit-docs-only-duplicates (0/3), docs-audit-one-fact-retry (0/3), docs-audit-one-fact-timeout (0/3). Baseline before my changes was 1/5, with all four positives at 0/3. --list loads all 8 cases with 0 load errors. 13 runner invocations used.

### domain-modeling

The skill is short and accurate, and when Haiku opens it, it follows it (glossary path, entry format, exclusions and the ADR rule all score 0.90 to 1.00). The weak point is the description: with all skills loaded the most literal trigger (the overloaded word "account") is never opened, and an ADR-or-glossary question does not open the skill even when it is the only one loaded. The skill had no evals; it now has 5 cases (3 routing, 2 value) in packages/skills/evals/domain-modeling/, all loading cleanly, with 2 left failing on the description, which a tested rewrite fixes. 12 runner invocations used.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (negative 3/3); failing: route-overloaded-account-word (0/3), route-implicit-cancelled-two-meanings (2/3 in the final run, 3/3 in the first). With the tested description rewrite: 3/3 cases pass.

- `value-glossary-file-and-entry-format`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without
- `value-adr-only-when-all-three-hold`: 0.52 with, 0.43 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded, Haiku never opens the skill for route-overloaded-account-word (0/3 in each of two runs), although the prompt is the description's own example. It greps the empty workspace for "account" and asks its questions from memory. With the skill loaded alone the same prompt routes 3/3, so the description is losing in the crowd rather than being unreadable. The implicit case routes 3/3 and 2/3 with the current text. The description opens with what the skill does and puts the trigger last.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement (3/3 on all three routing cases with --all-skills; value cases 1.00 vs 0.19 and 0.90-1.00 vs 0.43-0.57): "Use when a word in the project means different things to different people, teams or modules (\"account\", \"order\", \"cancelled\") and it has to be settled which is which and what each is called, when naming a new concept, when deciding whether a settled term also needs an ADR, or when creating or editing a GLOSSARY.md. Read it before asking the person clarifying questions about a term. Runs the conversation by challenging each term, proposing one canonical word, testing it on edge cases and against the code, and writing settled terms to GLOSSARY.md. Not for module interfaces (codebase-design) or button and error wording (ux-copy)." A first rewrite that kept the what-it-does sentence first and lacked the "Read it before asking" sentence still scored 0/3 on the explicit case, so the trigger-first order, that sentence, or both are what help; I did not separate the two.
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md:27 holds the skill's sharpest rule (propose an ADR only when the choice is hard to reverse, surprising and a real trade-off), but the description on line 3 never mentions ADRs. On value-adr-only-when-all-three-hold with the skill loaded alone, Haiku did not open SKILL.md in 9 of 9 with-arm runs across three runs and scored like the bare model (final 0.52 with, 0.43 without).

- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/domain-modeling/SKILL.md:10 and :18 point to an `adr-writing` skill that does not exist in any of the four skills directories of this repo. Line 10 hedges with "if installed"; line 18 opens with "ADRs follow the `adr-writing` skill" as if it were present and only then gives the fallback.

### dotnet-native-interop

The skill teaches three things that do not compile on the .NET 10 SDK (checked with `dotnet build` on 10.0.114), and when Haiku reads it, it copies the worst one into its answer. With the current description Haiku almost never opens the skill under competition: 1 of 4 routing-relevant cases pass with --all-skills at 3 runs, and every miss is "never opened", not a sibling winning. A tested description rewrite lifts routing to 3 of 5 cases passing; no value case discriminated in the skill's favour, and the one value case I kept is an accuracy regression that currently passes only because the skill goes unread.

**Routing:** 1/5 cases pass with --all-skills on Haiku at 3 runs (negative-interop-trim-json 1.00); failing: trigger-interop-crash 0.00, trigger-interop-header 0.33, trigger-interop-implicit-load-failure 0.00, trigger-interop-libraryimport 0.33. Skill loaded alone: 0.67 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00. Tested description rewrite with --all-skills: 3/5 pass (crash 0.33, header 1.00, implicit 0.67, libraryimport 1.00, negative 1.00).

**Value cases:**

- `value-libraryimport-setlasterror`: 1.00 with, 0.89 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, accuracy.** `SetLastPInvokeError = true` is not a property of LibraryImportAttribute; the named argument is still `SetLastError = true`. Wrong at packages/skills/skills/dotnet-native-interop/SKILL.md:33 (table), :83 (migration step 2), :94 (verify list); references/memory-and-callbacks.md:88 and :94; references/diagnostics.md:15. Verified: building the :88 snippet on SDK 10.0.114 gives CS0246, and it builds after changing to `SetLastError = true`. Eval evidence: with the skill read (tested description, 3/3 runs read SKILL.md) Haiku wrote `SetLastPInvokeError = true` in 3/3 runs, scoring 0.33 with vs 0.89 without on value-libraryimport-setlasterror.
  - Suggested: Use `SetLastError = true` for both attribute styles everywhere. Table row: `OS error code | SetLastError = true | SetLastError = true (read with Marshal.GetLastPInvokeError())`. Migration step 2: "`CharSet` to `StringMarshalling`; keep `SetLastError = true`". Keep `Marshal.GetLastPInvokeError()` as the read API; only the attribute argument is wrong.
- **high, accuracy.** The claim that `CLong`/`CULong` with LibraryImport fail with SYSLIB1051 until the assembly has `[assembly: DisableRuntimeMarshalling]` is false on net10.0. At SKILL.md:44 and :101, references/type-mapping.md:22, references/diagnostics.md:23. Verified on SDK 10.0.114: a LibraryImport method with a `CLong` parameter, plus one with `CULong` return, `out CLong`, `CULong[]` and a struct holding a `CLong` field, all build with no attribute and no diagnostic. Following the skill makes a user add an assembly-wide attribute that changes `bool` and `char` marshalling for nothing. I did not test .NET 7 or 8 SDKs, where the claim may once have held.
  - Suggested: Delete the DisableRuntimeMarshalling/SYSLIB1051 requirement from all four places and drop the gotcha at SKILL.md:101. If it is true for an older SDK, state the exact version after checking it there.
- **high, accuracy.** The "complete SafeHandle wrapper" does not compile: references/memory-and-callbacks.md:51-52 gives a private parameterless constructor with the comment "Used by the marshaller to create the handle". Verified on SDK 10.0.114: `CreateHandle` returning `MyLibHandle` fails with SYSLIB1051 (SafeHandleMarshaller does not support unmanaged-to-managed); it builds once the constructor is public.
  - Suggested: Make the constructor `public MyLibHandle() : base(ownsHandle: true) { }` and change the comment to say the LibraryImport generator needs a public parameterless constructor for a returned or `out` SafeHandle.
- **high, description.** SKILL.md:3. With --all-skills on Haiku the fair triggers are not opened: crash 0.00, header 0.33, libraryimport 0.33, implicit-load-failure 0.00 (final run, 3 runs each). The logs show no sibling skill read in any miss; Haiku answers from memory or searches the empty workspace. Loaded alone the same cases score 0.67 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00, so the description is recognised but does not win attention among 170 skills.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite, --all-skills, 3 runs: crash 0.33, header 1.00, libraryimport 1.00, implicit-load-failure 0.67, negative still 1.00. Text: "Read before writing, reviewing or debugging any C# code that calls a native (C, C++, Rust) library through [DllImport] or [LibraryImport]. Covers signatures from a C header, string and struct marshalling, memory ownership, SafeHandle, callbacks and library loading. Use for wrapping a C library, DllNotFoundException, EntryPointNotFoundException, an AccessViolationException or intermittent crash in or after a native call, SYSLIB1054, or converting DllImport to LibraryImport for Native AOT. Not for IL2026/IL3050 trim warnings in managed code (dotnet-upgrade-guide)." Fix the accuracy findings first: this rewrite makes Haiku read the skill and so copy its errors.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** No case showed the skill helping Haiku. Tried: `#if WINDOWS` on a portable TFM (SKILL.md:102) 1.00 with / 1.00 without; second SetDllImportResolver throws (references/loading-and-tooling.md:39) 1.00 / 1.00; review scope rule, no rewrite of a working DllImport (SKILL.md:21-23) 1.00 / 1.00 even with the skill read 3/3; C `long` under LibraryImport 0.56 / 0.56, then dropped because the skill's expected answer turned out to be wrong. Haiku already knows CLong, nuint, explicit bool MarshalAs and StringMarshalling.

'Zero tests, exit 0' is VSTest behavior, not MTP. The skill itself cites exit code 5 at lines 64 and 104, so the opening claim contradicts it.

### ef-core

The skill's content is accurate and helps Haiku when it is read, but Haiku rarely reads it: with all skills loaded it was opened in 0 of 12 positive routing runs, and on self-contained questions it was opened in 1 of 12 runs even when it was the only skill loaded. The evals now have 7 cases (4 existing untouched, 3 new: one implicit routing case and two value cases); both value cases discriminate only with a tested description rewrite (with 1.00 vs without about 0.5) and are left failing against the current description. The EF 10 facts used in the new cases were checked against the Microsoft Learn breaking-changes pages.

**Routing:** 1/5 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (ef-core-vs-schema-design 1.00); failing at 0.00: trigger-ef-core-1, trigger-ef-core-2, trigger-ef-core-3, route-implicit-pasted-slow-report. The negative passes weakly: Haiku made no tool calls at all in those runs. Skill loaded alone: trigger-1 0.67, trigger-2 1.00, trigger-3 1.00, route-implicit 0.33. With the tested description rewrite and all skills: route-implicit 0.67, the three triggers still 0.00.

**Value cases:**

- `value-ef10-upgrade-checks`: 0.33 with, 0.38 without
- `value-review-comment-addrange`: 0.50 with, 0.50 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/ef-core/SKILL.md:3. Haiku answers EF Core questions from memory instead of opening the skill. With only this skill loaded, the two self-contained value prompts opened it in 1 of 12 with-arm runs (runs r4, r6, r8), so with and without scored the same (final: 0.33 vs 0.38 and 0.50 vs 0.50). The pasted-code routing case opened it in 1 of 3 runs alone and 0 of 3 with all skills. The description lists topics but gives no reason to read it when the model thinks it already knows EF Core, and does not mention pasted code, review comments or EF 9/10 behavior changes.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: 'Writes, reviews and tunes EF Core data access: query shape, tracking, Include vs split queries, N+1, bulk ExecuteUpdate/Delete, DbContext lifetime, migrations, raw SQL parameters, EF Core 9 and 10 behavior changes, and Dapper code beside it. Use for any DbContext or LINQ-to-entities code or question, pasted in the chat or in the repo: a slow EF query, a review comment about tracking or SaveChanges, dotnet ef migrations, "what does EF Core 10 do here", or reviewing a repository or import job. Read it before answering from memory, even when the workspace has no code: EF Core 9 and 10 changed defaults.' Results with this text (copy in /tmp/skill-evals/ef-core/alt, only the description changed): skill loaded alone, it was opened in 12 of 12 value runs; value-ef10-upgrade-checks with 1.00 vs without 0.48, value-review-comment-addrange with 1.00 vs without 0.50. With all skills loaded, route-implicit-pasted-slow-report went from 0/3 to 2/3. It did not help the three existing triggers (still 0/9 with all skills).
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/ef-core/SKILL.md:3. The three existing triggers (trigger-ef-core-1/2/3) score 0/9 with all skills loaded, under both the current and the rewritten description, and 0.67/1.00/1.00 with the skill loaded alone. The logs show no skill of any kind was read in the all-skills runs: Haiku greps for the named class, finds an empty workspace and answers from memory. So this is 'never opened', not a loss to a sibling (aspnet-core, csharp, dotnet-performance were not read either). I found no description text that fixes it; the tested rewrite above did not.

- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/ef-core/SKILL.md:10 sends out-of-scope work to `db-schema-design` and `postgres`. With all skills loaded, the existing implicit trigger (pasted `Core 1 panic'ed (LoadProhibited)` / `Backtrace:` / `rst:0xc (SW_CPU_RESET)` log, no chip named) scored 0/3 in two separate runs: Haiku ran one `ls`, found no files and answered from memory. Loaded alone, the same case scored 3/3, so it is 'never opened', not 'lost to a sibling'. The explicit OTA trigger scored 2/3 and 3/3. Even loaded alone, Haiku skipped the skill in 2 of 6 with-arm runs of the kept value case and 4 of 6 runs of a discarded 'write a button ISR component' case.

Text: "Writes, reviews and debugs ESP-IDF firmware for ESP32-family chips (ESP32, S2, S3, C3, C6, H2), with confirmation gates before any flash, eFuse burn or partition change. Use for any ESP32 or ESP-IDF question, with or without project files: FreeRTOS tasks, drivers, Wi-Fi/BLE, OTA and rollback, partitions, sdkconfig, sleep and wakeup, Secure Boot, LVGL, idf.py build/flash/monitor. Also use when pasted serial output is an Espressif crash even if no chip is named: `Guru Meditation Error`, `Core N panic'ed (LoadProhibited, StoreProhibited, ...)`, a `Backtrace: 0x400...` line, an `rst:0x.. (..._RESET),boot:0x..` boot line, task watchdog or brownout resets. Not for STM32, nRF, RP2040 or other non-Espressif MCUs." ### experiment-loop

The skill content clearly helps Haiku: the one value case scores 1.00 with the skill and 0.50 without. Routing is the problem: with all skills loaded, both fair positive triggers score 0/3 because Haiku looks for project files in the empty workspace and never opens the skill, while they score 3/3 with the skill loaded alone. A rewritten description scored 3/3 on both positives and on the negative with all skills loaded; that text echoes some wording from my own prompts, so treat the result as optimistic. The suite now has 4 cases (2 positive routing, 1 negative, 1 value), all loading without errors, with the two positives left failing as a description finding.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: experiment-loop-vs-problem-solving (0/3), route-implicit-overnight-bundle-size (0/3). Both are 3/3 with the skill loaded alone and 3/3 with the tested description rewrite under --all-skills. The negative route-negative-single-hot-function passes 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-keep-or-revert-decisions`: 1.00 with, 0.50 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/experiment-loop/SKILL.md:3. The description is written in the skill's own mechanics ("bounded, unattended optimize-and-measure loop", "one hypothesis per commit", "keep-or-revert decisions") and is not opened for user-worded requests. With --all-skills on Haiku, experiment-loop-vs-problem-solving (rewritten prompt) scored 0/3 twice and route-implicit-overnight-bundle-size scored 0/3 twice; the event logs show only ls/find/read of package.json or Makefile, and no SKILL.md of any skill was read. With the skill loaded alone both score 3/3, so this is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'. The original prompt of the existing case, which repeated the description wording, scored 3/3 with all skills.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement, scored 3/3 on both positives with --all-skills (the negative was not run against this exact text): "Runs many optimization attempts unattended against a number that a command prints (benchmark time, startup time, bundle size, memory, test pass rate). Tries one idea at a time on a dedicated git branch, measures, keeps only what improves the number, reverts the rest and logs every attempt. Use when the user wants the agent to keep trying ideas on its own (overnight, without babysitting, 'go through these ideas and keep what helps') toward a target or 'as low as it will go'. Not for one targeted optimization or a single benchmark run." A variant with the extra sentence "Read it before looking for the project files, because setup starts with questions to the user." also scored 3/3 on both positives and 3/3 on the negative. Caveat: the quoted trigger phrases overlap with the wording of my two eval prompts, so the score is likely optimistic for other phrasings.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/experiment-loop/SKILL.md:10 sends the reader to skills `coding`, `problem-solving` and `planning`. None of them exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills. The same line, SKILL.md:81 (through the reference) and references/loop-design.md:12 and :14 point to `/loop` and `/schedule` "built-ins"; these look like Claude Code commands, and I could not verify that pi has them.
  - Suggested: Describe the exclusions without skill names ("Not for a single optimization, for planning the surrounding work, or for pure polling or scheduling"), or name skills that exist in this repo. Remove the `/loop` and `/schedule` references or replace them with whatever pi actually offers for scheduling.
- **medium, instructions.** Contradictions in the keep rule. packages/skills/skills/experiment-loop/SKILL.md:57 says a metric that is the "Same" is reverted, while :68 says "Try removing code now and then. If the metric holds, the simpler version wins" (keep). SKILL.md:56 says "Improved beyond noise, boundary intact: keep", while :32 sets the default that a small gain is not worth added complexity. Haiku resolved the second conflict as revert in 6/6 runs with the skill loaded (grader e3), so it did not cost score; the first conflict was deliberately left out of the case because the skill gives no single right answer.

### fact-check

fact-check is a 30-line manual skill (disable-model-invocation: true), so it can never route in pi and its routing cases are all quiet negatives, which pass 3/3. When invoked with /skill:fact-check it measurably helps Haiku on two new deterministic cases (memory cannot confirm an external fact: 1.00 vs 0.43; fixed verdict words: 1.00 vs 0.00). The four older value cases show no measurable value: two need --scaffold, which I was not allowed to pass, and score 0 in an empty workspace, and the two -invoked ones, now fixed to run, are passed by bare Haiku too.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (fact-check-quiet-doubt, fact-check-quiet-trivia, route-quiet-in-scope-prove-it). All three are must-not-load cases; no positive trigger exists because the skill has disable-model-invocation: true. --list loads all 9 cases with 0 load errors. 5 runner invocations used.

- `value-memory-cannot-confirm`: 1.00 with, 0.43 without
- `value-verdict-words`: 1.00 with, 0.00 without
- `value-readme-claims-invoked`: 0.93 with, 0.87 without
- `value-earlier-answer-recheck-invoked`: 1.00 with, 1.00 without
- `value-readme-claims`: 0.00 with, 0.33 without
- `value-earlier-answer-recheck`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/fact-check/SKILL.md:10 sends new questions to a `research` skill. No skill of that name exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills.
  - Suggested: Drop the skill reference: "Not for reconsidering a decision or plan (that is `doubt-review`) or for researching a new question."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/fact-check/SKILL.md:12 says "The trigger is a feeling, not a request: when you are about to assert a checkable fact from a feeling ... check it before writing it". This contradicts line 4 (disable-model-invocation: true) and the description at line 3 ("Manual command"): the model never sees the skill unless the user types the command, so a self-trigger rule inside it cannot fire. Evidence: 0 SKILL.md reads in 9 routing runs, and 0 reads in the 6 no-slash-command value runs with the skill loaded.
  - Suggested: Delete line 12, or move that sentence to an always-loaded place (AGENTS.md). If self-triggering is really wanted, the flag has to go and the description needs a rewrite. Dropping the flag alone is not enough: with the flag removed in a /tmp copy and all 173 skills loaded, the in-scope prompt route-quiet-in-scope-prove-it still loaded the skill 0/3 times on Haiku. - **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/fact-check/SKILL.md:16 reads "Take the passage from `the arguments given with the command`". The backticked phrase looks like a converted $ARGUMENTS placeholder and reads as a literal identifier. Haiku coped with it in all 12 invoked runs.

- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/fact-check/SKILL.md:20-22 and :30 imply, but never state, what to do when the right source cannot be reached (no web access, file not available). Haiku inferred Unverified 3/3 in value-memory-cannot-confirm, so this is a robustness gap rather than an observed failure.
  - Suggested: Add to step 3: "If the right source cannot be reached in this session, the claim is Unverified, however sure you are from memory."
- **low, no-measurable-value.** On the two scenarios the original evals were built around (README lines against repo files; an earlier answer whose delete advice rests on a false claim), bare Haiku does as well as Haiku with the skill once the files are in reach: value-earlier-answer-recheck-invoked 1.00 vs 1.00, value-readme-claims-invoked 0.93 vs 0.87. The skill's measurable effect on Haiku is limited to the memory-cannot-confirm rule (SKILL.md:30) and the verdict vocabulary (SKILL.md:24-27).

### flag-hygiene

flag-hygiene had no evals; it now has 5 cases (3 routing, 2 value) under packages/skills/evals/flag-hygiene, all loading cleanly. Routing is good on Haiku with all skills loaded (explicit trigger 3/3, near-miss negative 3/3, implicit trigger 2/3), and one value case discriminates (1.00 with, 0.40 without). The second value case is left failing because Haiku never opens the skill when the audit findings are already in the prompt; a tested description rewrite takes it from 0.00 to 1.00 and every case to 3/3.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (8/9 runs correct); failing: route-implicit-toggle-sprawl at 0.67 (2/3 fires, same in both runs). With the tested description rewrite: 3/3 cases at 1.00.

**Value cases:**

- `value-long-lived-90-day-threshold`: 1.00 with, 0.40 without
- `value-removal-order`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/flag-hygiene/SKILL.md:3 describes only a whole-codebase audit. When the user already has the findings and asks to rank removals or fill a registry row, Haiku does not open the skill even when it is the only one loaded: 0 SKILL.md reads in 9 with-arm runs of value-removal-order across three prompt wordings ("flag cleanup", "stale flag audit ... prioritized removal list", "flag debt review"), and 0 in 9 runs of a dropped registry-row case. It then answers from memory and gets the order wrong (D,A,C,B or A,C,D,B instead of D,C,A,B) and writes the commit author as owner.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite: 'Audits feature flag debt across a codebase (stale, orphaned, duplicate, ownerless, nested, long-lived flags), builds the flag registry and ranks flags for removal. Use for "flag debt", "stale flags", "flag audit", "flag inventory", "which flags can we remove and in what order", or a cleanup of LaunchDarkly, Unleash, flagd, env-var or home-grown toggles. Read it also when the findings are already in hand and the task is only to classify them, fill a registry row or order the removals: the finding classes, registry fields (unknown owner rule) and removal ranking are defined here and differ from common practice. Not for adding or removing one flag (feature-flags), rollout plans (rollout-plan) or deprecating an API (modernize).' Scores with this text: skill alone, value-removal-order 1.00 (was 0.00) and the registry-row case 0.94 (was 0.17); with all 173 skills loaded, all five cases 1.00 at 3 runs, including the implicit trigger (was 0.67) and the negative.
- **high, overlap.** The feature-flags skill claims the same job. packages/skills/skills/feature-flags/SKILL.md:3 says it "audits a codebase for stale flags and flag debt" and triggers on "audit flags or build a flag registry"; its section 5 (SKILL.md:56) sends the reader to feature-flags/references/flag-hygiene.md, an 85-line copy of this skill's method (same 90-day rule at line 56, same removal ranking at line 79). flag-hygiene/SKILL.md:3 meanwhile says single-flag work belongs to feature-flags, and goff's description also routes "stale-flag audits" to feature-flags. Routing still picked flag-hygiene in my cases (8/9 runs), but two copies of the rules will drift (they already differ in wording: "house default" vs "this repo's own extension").
  - Suggested: Keep the audit in one place. Either delete feature-flags/references/flag-hygiene.md and section 5, and change the feature-flags description to "Not for a whole-codebase flag audit or registry (flag-hygiene)", or drop the flag-hygiene skill and keep the reference. Update goff's description to match.
- **medium, instructions.** The long-lived rule at SKILL.md:45 works once read (with arm 1.00 in every run), but the boundary to "Stale" at SKILL.md:40 is loose: "untouched in git for a long time" has no number, and the bare model files a flag past its expiry under stale instead of long-lived. A reader has to guess what "a long time" is.
  - Suggested: Give the stale class a threshold or a rule, for example "no commit touching the key or its definition in 180 days (this repo's default)", and add "a flag past its expiry is long-lived, not stale".
- **low, accuracy.** Flag type names differ between files: SKILL.md:20 says "ops and entitlement flags may live on", references/registry-template.md:8 and :11 list the types as "release, experiment, ops (kill switch), permission". In the dropped registry-row case one run wrote `type: release?` after reading the template, guessing a type the evidence did not support.
  - Suggested: Use one term in both files ("permission/entitlement" as feature-flags/SKILL.md:25 does) and add to the template: "type `?` when no document states it; do not infer it from the default value".
- **low, accuracy.** SKILL.md:3 sends API deprecation to modernize, while feature-flags/SKILL.md:3 sends the same thing to deprecation-migration. Both skills exist and both list "sunset the v1 API" as a trigger, so the two flag skills disagree on the neighbour.
  - Suggested: Pick one target in both descriptions (modernize, if deprecation-migration is the older skill).
- **low, structure.** SKILL.md:28 and references/search-recipe.md:3 point to "the feature-flags skill's platform notes" without a path. The file is packages/skills/skills/feature-flags/references/platforms.md, which a model with only flag-hygiene loaded cannot find from that wording.
  - Suggested: Name the file: "feature-flags skill, references/platforms.md (detection hints)", or copy the five lines of detection hints into search-recipe.md.

### forgejo-actions

The skill routes well and measurably helps Haiku: all 4 routing cases pass with all skills loaded in the final run, and the new value case scores 1.00 with the skill against 0.30 without. I added 3 cases (implicit trigger, GitHub near-miss negative, value) and left the 2 existing routing cases untouched; 6 runner invocations used. The facts I checked against the Forgejo docs and source hold; the findings are a wrong MCP tool prefix for pi, a pointer to a skill that does not exist, and small wording gaps.

**Routing:** 4/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run); failing: none. The implicit case scored 2/3 in an earlier all-skills run and 3/3 with the skill loaded alone.

**Value cases:**

- `value-github-habits-on-forgejo`: 1.00 with, 0.30 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-actions/references/failed-run.md:9 gates the preferred log-reading path on `mcp__plugin_forgejo-mcp_forgejo__*` tools. That is the Claude Code plugin prefix. In this repo packages/forgejo-mcp/src/index.ts:54 registers the server as "forgejo", so pi exposes the tools as `mcp__forgejo__*`. An agent matching the prefix literally will conclude the tools are absent and fall back to asking the user to paste the log. Not measured by an eval (cases have no MCP tools). The same prefix is in forgejo-cli/SKILL.md:54, forgejo-cli/references/commands.md:40 and forgejo-pr-comments/SKILL.md:23.
  - Suggested: Name the tools without a host-specific prefix: "Preferred, when the forgejo-mcp tools are present (`list_workflow_runs`, `list_action_run_jobs`, `get_action_job_logs`; the prefix is `mcp__forgejo__` in pi and `mcp__plugin_forgejo-mcp_forgejo__` in Claude Code)".
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-actions/SKILL.md:3 (description: "Not for GitHub-hosted Actions (`gh-actions`)") and SKILL.md:16 ("point to `gh-actions` if installed") name a skill that exists in none of the four skills directories. Line 16 hedges with "if installed"; the description does not. Routing was not harmed: the github.com near-miss negative stayed quiet 6/6 runs with all skills loaded.
  - Suggested: In the description drop the backticked name: "Not for workflows on github.com or GitHub Enterprise." Keep the hedged mention on line 16, or drop it until a gh-actions skill exists.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-actions/SKILL.md:18 and references/differences.md:7 say a higher-priority workflow directory wins "even if that directory is empty". Git does not track empty directories, so the real case is a directory holding only non-workflow files (README, .gitkeep). The rule itself is correct: I checked ListWorkflows in modules/actions/workflows.go on the forgejo branch ("We have found a valid source that we will use, no matter whether it contains workflows or not").
  - Suggested: Reword to "even if that directory contains no workflow files (for example only a README or .gitkeep)".
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-actions/references/differences.md:29 says older push and pull_request runs "of the same workflow" are cancelled when no `concurrency` is set. The reference page scopes this to "any previous invocation of the same workflow with the same branch", and for pull_request only to synchronize events. As written, a reader can conclude a push to one branch cancels a run on another.
  - Suggested: "automatic cancellation of older `push` and `pull_request` (synchronize) runs of the same workflow on the same branch when no `concurrency` is set; set `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: false` to keep them".
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-actions/references/failed-run.md:5 leaves the meaning of the trailing `/jobs/<j>` URL segment as a guess ("as far as we know ... hedge: confirm against the job list"). I could not verify it either. A hedge inside the instruction costs the model a decision on every failed-run task.
  - Suggested: Either verify against a live instance and state it, or turn it into a step: "Ignore the trailing job number for lookup; list the run's jobs and pick the failed one."

**Eval changes**

- left-failing: `forgejo-actions-run-url-routing`. Not changed and not failing: 3/3 with all skills on Haiku in two separate runs. Listed only because the schema has no 'unchanged' action. Frontmatter still carries an ignored `model:` key and `runs: 1`; harmless, left alone.
- left-failing: `forgejo-actions-workflow-routing`. Not changed and not failing: 3/3 with all skills on Haiku in two separate runs. The prompt names `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`, which is description wording, so it is an explicit trigger; the new implicit case covers the other side.
- added: `route-implicit-job-stuck-waiting`. Implicit positive: job stuck 'waiting' after moving from GitHub to Codeberg with runs-on: ubuntu-latest; no path, URL or skill wording. All skills: 2/3 in the first run, 3/3 in the final run; skill alone: 3/3. The one miss was Haiku listing the empty workspace and answering from memory, not a loss to a sibling.
- added: `route-negative-github-hosted-workflow`. Near-miss negative (min 0, max 0): a failing run URL on github.com. Skill stayed unread in 6/6 runs with all skills loaded.
- added: `value-github-habits-on-forgejo`. Six TRUE/FALSE assumptions about a migrated workflow, regex-graded on the last message: directory precedence with a workflow-less .gitea/workflows, ignored permissions, ignored job-level continue-on-error, default action host, auto-cancel without concurrency, github context alias. First run 0.93 with / 0.26 without; one with-run answered A5 FALSE because 'ci.yml never runs here', a coupling flaw in my prompt. I added one sentence telling the model to judge A2-A6 independently of A1; after that 1.00 with / 0.30 without. Expected answers were checked against the Forgejo docs (github-actions and reference pages) and workflows.go.

### forgejo-pr-comments

The skill had no evals; it now has 5 cases (3 routing, 2 value) under packages/skills/evals/forgejo-pr-comments/, all loading without errors. The skill clearly helps Haiku once invoked (fj command syntax 1.00 vs 0.00; triage contract 0.67 vs 0.00), but it can never be found by the model because `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps it out of pi's skill list, so both positive routing cases are left failing at 0/3. One triage rule (PR-description drift is `clarify`) lives only in a conditionally read reference and Haiku misses it in most runs; a one-line move into SKILL.md fixed it in a tested copy. The fj commands in the skill were checked against the installed fj v0.7.0 and are correct.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: routing-codeberg-review-feedback (0/3), routing-implicit-changes-requested (0/3), both because disable-model-invocation hides the skill. Against the tested copy (flag removed, description rewritten): 3/3 cases pass, alone and with --all-skills.

**Value cases:**

- `value-fj-fetch-commands-invoked`: 1.00 with, 0.00 without
- `value-triage-ids-and-description-drift-invoked`: 0.67 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-pr-comments/SKILL.md:4 sets `disable-model-invocation: true`. pi 1.7.0 drops such skills from the model-facing list (dist/core/skills.js:279) and packages/skill-index does the same (src/plan.ts:26), so no natural request can reach it. Evidence: routing-codeberg-review-feedback and routing-implicit-changes-requested score 0/3 each with --all-skills on Haiku (two separate runs). The description at SKILL.md:3 also has no 'Use when' clause, only 'Invoke as /forgejo-pr-comments', which is not pi's command form (pi expands `/skill:forgejo-pr-comments`, agent-session.js _expandSkillCommand).
  - Suggested: If the skill is meant to be found, remove line 4 and use this description: "Triages the review feedback on a Forgejo or Codeberg pull request (inline review comments, review summaries, a Request changes review) and fixes only the rows the user picks, with draft replies for the rest. Read-only on the forge: never posts, resolves or pushes. Use when a PR on codeberg.org or a self-hosted Forgejo (a URL ending /pulls/<n>) has reviewer comments to go through, address or push back on. Not for opening or writing a PR (`forgejo-pr`) or for github.com PRs (`pr-comments`)." Tested on a copy with line 4 removed and this text: all three routing cases 3/3 with the skill alone and 3/3 with --all-skills (173 skills), including the forgejo-pr near-miss negative. If manual-only is intended, keep the flag, say `/skill:forgejo-pr-comments` in the description, and accept that the two positive routing cases stay at 0.
- **medium, instructions.** The rule that a request to fix the PR description is `clarify` (editing it is a forge write) exists only in references/triage.md:31, and SKILL.md:55 tells the model to open that file only 'when the right action isn't obvious'. In value-triage-ids-and-description-drift-invoked Haiku skipped the reference in 5 of 6 with-skill runs after the prompt was made unambiguous and answered `R1: fix` ("you edit it on Codeberg") in those 5 (with-skill score 0.50 and 0.67). It only read the reference in the first draft of the case, where another row was ambiguous.
  - Suggested: Add a bullet to SKILL.md step 2 after line 53: "A request to change the PR title or description is `clarify`, never `fix`: editing it is a write on the forge. Put the corrected text in the report for the user to paste." Tested on a copy with only this bullet added (plus the description change above): the case scored 1.00 with, 0.00 without, 3 runs.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/pr-comments already covers Forgejo and Codeberg: its description (pr-comments/SKILL.md:3) says 'GitHub (gh) or Forgejo and Codeberg (fj)', it ships references/forgejo.md, and its references/triage.md differs from this skill's triage.md in only four lines. forgejo-pr-comments/SKILL.md:3 says 'Not for github.com PRs (`pr-comments`)' as if the two were split by forge, and forgejo-pr/SKILL.md:9 sends review feedback to `/pr-comments`, not to this skill. Both are manual-only, so nothing decides between them.
  - Suggested: Pick one owner for Forgejo review feedback. Either drop the Forgejo branch and references/forgejo.md from pr-comments and point forgejo-pr/SKILL.md:9 at forgejo-pr-comments, or remove forgejo-pr-comments. If both stay, share one triage.md instead of two near-identical copies.
- **low, accuracy.** SKILL.md:19 and SKILL.md:23 name MCP tools with the Claude Code plugin prefix `mcp__plugin_forgejo-mcp_forgejo__`. Under pi with packages/forgejo-mcp the server shows up as `mcp__forgejo` (seen in this session's server list; I did not list its tool names), so the literal names will not match. SKILL.md:19 also has a leftover placeholder substitution in code formatting: "Resolve the PR from `the arguments given with the command`".
  - Suggested: Name the tools without a host-specific prefix ("the forgejo MCP tools `list_pull_reviews`, `list_pull_review_comments`, `list_issue_comments`, `list_repo_pull_requests`, whatever prefix the host gives them") and rewrite line 19 as plain prose: "Resolve the PR from the argument the user gave: a number, or a URL ending `/pulls/<n>`".

### forgejo-release

The skill routes reliably on Haiku with all 170 skills loaded (3/3 cases at 3 runs each) and its fj command reference matches fj v0.7.0 --help on every flag I checked, so there are only low-severity findings. The evals went from one routing case to four: an implicit trigger, a near-miss negative, and one value case that discriminates (with 1.00, without 0.47). Runner caveat: the without arm is not isolated from the machine; in two earlier value attempts bare Haiku read the installed skill copy under ~/.pi/agent/npm/.../forgejo-release/SKILL.md, a claude-tools checkout and /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/fj, which inflated the baseline to 0.79-0.86 until the prompt told it not to search the disk.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs each with --all-skills on Haiku (forgejo-release-routing 1.00, route-implicit-ship-merged-work 1.00, route-negative-release-workflow-red 1.00); failing: none. No description rewrite needed or tested.

**Value cases:**

- `value-fj-release-commands`: 1.00 with, 0.47 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-release/SKILL.md:62 says view and edit take the release name and that view and delete accept -t/--by-tag, but does not say that on `release edit` the same short flag -t means something else: `-t, --tag <TAG>  Corresponding tag for this release` (fj v0.7.0 `fj release edit --help`). A model generalising from view/delete to `fj release edit -t v1.4.0 ...` would repoint the release's tag instead of selecting by tag. `fj release edit v1.4.0 --by-tag` is rejected by the parser (checked).
  - Suggested: Append to line 62: "`edit` has no --by-tag; its `-t <tag>` changes which tag the release points at, so never pass -t to edit to select a release."
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-release/SKILL.md:90 links references/notes.md only after the Errors table, while step 4 (line 43), where the bump and notes are drafted, does not point to it. Rules that exist only in the reference (references/notes.md:11 trust the diff over the commit message; :29 skip test/docs/lockfile/CI-only commits and keep an existing CHANGELOG.md in step) are easy to miss; in all 6 with-skill runs Haiku read SKILL.md only and never opened the reference (the tested tasks did not need it, so this is not measured as a failure).
  - Suggested: Move the pointer into step 4: "Bump table, note layout and the CHANGELOG.md rule: [notes](references/notes.md); read it before drafting." and drop line 90.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-release/SKILL.md:64 offers `fj release browse v1.4.0` as an equal alternative for showing the draft; it opens a browser, which does nothing useful in a non-interactive agent run (the same concern the skill raises for `-b` without a value at line 60).
  - Suggested: Use `fj release view v1.4.0` as the check and mention browse only as something the user can run themselves.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/forgejo-release/SKILL.md:8 states that Codeberg's terms restrict projects made mostly of generative-AI code. A source search found pages pointing that way (Codeberg/Community issue 2933 about an 'AI-generated' rule in the Terms of Use, a Codeberg blog post on LLMs) but I did not retrieve the terms text, so the exact wording is not verified.
  - Suggested: Link the clause (Codeberg Terms of Use section) next to the sentence so the claim can be checked and updated when the terms change.

**Eval changes**

- left-failing: `forgejo-release-routing`. Not failing and not changed: pre-existing explicit trigger, kept as is (fair prompt, grader pattern matches pi's synthetic Skill call). 3/3 with --all-skills on Haiku. Its prompt is not copied in any other skill's evals. It still carries an ignored `model:` key and `runs: 1`; harmless, left alone. (Listed here only to record that it was reviewed; the schema has no 'unchanged' action.)

### fresh-eyes

fresh-eyes is a manual command (disable-model-invocation) that works well once typed: both value cases now discriminate on Haiku (with 1.00 against 0.33 and 0.40 without). The two cases that existed could not run under the pi runner and were rewritten in place on the same point; three routing cases were added that pin the manual-only behaviour and a near miss. The main problem in the skill is that it restates four sibling skills (doubt-review, cold-read, lens-review, tunnel-check) and assumes a subagent tool and commands that pi does not guarantee.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (all three assert the skill stays unloaded). No positive trigger is possible: disable-model-invocation keeps fresh-eyes out of pi's skill listing, confirmed in the run logs. Experiment on a /tmp copy with the flag removed and the two in-scope prompts graded as positives: with all skills 0/3 and 0/3 (Haiku opened no skill at all, not a sibling either); skill loaded alone 3/3 for migration-claim and 0/3 for the implicit tunnel prompt.

**Value cases:**

- `value-disprove-invoked`: 1.00 with, 0.40 without
- `value-cold-invoked`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/fresh-eyes/SKILL.md:12-15 defines four modes that each restate a sibling skill in the same directory: --disprove repeats doubt-review (the adversarial prompt at fresh-eyes SKILL.md:35-48 is the one at doubt-review/SKILL.md:87, and the finding classes at :51 are those at doubt-review/SKILL.md:102), --cold repeats cold-read, --lens repeats lens-review, and references/tunnel.md repeats tunnel-check (same three classes, tunnel-check/SKILL.md:26). The description (SKILL.md:3) excludes /code-review, second-opinion and devils-advocate but says nothing about these four. Because of this the rewritten value cases test the same rules as doubt-review/value-verbatim-reviewer-prompt and cold-read/value-blind-brief-keep-drop, with different prompts.
  - Suggested: Decide which is canonical. Either drop fresh-eyes, or keep it as the single manual entry point and have each mode point at the sibling's SKILL.md instead of restating it; or remove the manual siblings lens-review and tunnel-check. At minimum, add to the description: "Model-invoked equivalents: doubt-review (disprove), cold-read (cold)." Not tested: it would not change routing for a manual command.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/fresh-eyes/SKILL.md:20-21 assumes a Claude Code subagent tool ("Agent tool, general-purpose, no worktree"). The only fallback covers running inside a subagent (:20); nothing covers a main session with no subagent tool, which is pi without a subagents extension and is what the eval runner provides. In the baseline run of the original cases Haiku never reached a brief. It produced a correct brief only when the prompt itself said the user would paste the brief into a clean session (3/3 in both value cases).
  - Suggested: Add to Core rules: "No subagent tool in this session: write the brief under the same rules and hand it to the user to paste into a clean session; do not review inline unless asked, and then label the result degraded: not fresh-context." Name the tool generically ("the subagent tool, e.g. Agent"). Not tested as a skill edit.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/fresh-eyes/SKILL.md:3, :50 and references/tunnel.md:7 send the user to `second-opinion`, and :3 to `/code-review`. Neither exists as a skill in the four skills directories of this repo, and /code-review is a Claude Code built-in, not a pi command. The siblings hedge this ("if installed" at devils-advocate/SKILL.md:15 and doubt-review/SKILL.md:13); fresh-eyes does not.
  - Suggested: Write "`second-opinion`, if installed" in all three places, and replace "(/code-review)" in the description with "(a code review)" or name it as Claude Code's built-in command.
- **low, accuracy.** The description (SKILL.md:3) says the command "has a fresh-context subagent review" the artifact and that --lens "judges through named lenses"; :15 repeats "named lenses". But :64 has the model choose the lenses fresh for each artifact, and :67 says to run them inline, with a subagent only when the user asks. So --lens is neither fresh-context by default nor based on lenses the user names, and :21 ("spawn the subagents below") contradicts :67 for this mode.
  - Suggested: Description: "--lens judges through 2 to 5 lenses it picks, one per failure mode (inline unless isolation is asked for)". At :21 add "(--lens runs inline, see below)".

The skill's content is sound and decisive when opened (loudness case: 1.00 whenever SKILL.md was read, 0.20 whenever it was not, 13 of 13 runs), but Haiku opens it unreliably: with all skills loaded the realistic triggers score 0.67 and the symptom-only trigger and the value case score 0. A tested description rewrite brings every trigger and the value case to 3/3 with all skills loaded, at the cost of one leak in three runs on the new Godot-import negative. The suite now has 6 cases (3 added, none removed or edited), all loading cleanly; two are left failing as description problems.

**Routing:** Final run, --all-skills on Haiku, 3 runs, original description: 2/5 routing cases pass (game-audio-vs-game-feel 1.00, negative-godot-audio-import 1.00); failing: trigger-game-audio-1 0.67, trigger-game-audio-2 0.67, trigger-implicit-slider-dead-zone 0.00. With the tested description rewrite: 4/5 pass (all three triggers 1.00, game-feel negative 1.00); failing: negative-godot-audio-import 0.67.

**Value cases:**

- `value-loudness-target-per-platform`: 0.47 with, 0.20 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/game-audio/SKILL.md:3. The description lists topics and quoted keywords but no symptoms, and nothing tells the model its remembered numbers are wrong. Evidence on Haiku at 3 runs: trigger-implicit-slider-dead-zone scores 0.00 with all skills and 0.33 with the skill loaded alone (never opened, no sibling read instead); trigger-game-audio-1 and -2 score 0.67 with all skills (the misses read no skill at all); value-loudness-target-per-platform is not opened in 0/3 runs with all skills and 1/3 in the final value run, so it answers -16 LUFS from memory.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: "Plans and reviews a game's audio mix and music system, engine-neutral: bus and mixer layout, volume in dB, ducking, adaptive music (layers, stems, transitions), SFX variation and voice limits, beat sync and per-platform loudness targets in LUFS. Use for mix and music-system questions, also when reported as a symptom: a volume slider or setting that does nothing over most of its range, music drowning out dialogue, pumping when the music dips, repetitive footsteps or gunshots, music that cuts abruptly, beats drifting out of sync, or how loud the game should be. Read before answering from memory: the numbers differ from music-streaming practice. Not for audio file formats, import or compression settings or engine audio API (engine skill, e.g. godot)." Scores with all skills loaded, Haiku, 3 runs: all three triggers 1.00, value case 1.00 (with/without 1.00/0.20 when loaded alone), game-feel negative 1.00, negative-godot-audio-import 0.67 (one run read both godot and game-audio). An earlier variant containing "Use whenever sound in a game is the problem" and no Not-for clause scored 0.00 on that negative, so keep the Not-for clause.
- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/game-craft/references/audio.md:1-52 restates this whole skill (same bus rule, slider rule, -24/-18 LUFS, ducking numbers, SFX caps, beat-sync pseudocode, adaptive music), and game-craft's description (game-craft/SKILL.md:3, "audio ... music mixes") claims the same requests. packages/skills/skills/godot/references/audio.md:3 sends mix design to game-craft, not game-audio, while game-audio/SKILL.md:8 and :68 point at godot. In evals, game-craft/trigger-audio-ducking/prompt.md is word for word game-audio/trigger-game-audio-1/prompt.md, and game-craft/value-loudness-target-not-streaming tests the same fact as the new value case here. In my runs Haiku never chose game-craft over game-audio for these prompts, so the collision is not yet costing routing, but two copies of each number will drift (see the provenance note that only one copy carries).
  - Suggested: Pick one owner. Either drop the audio row and references/audio.md from game-craft and have godot/references/audio.md:3 point at game-audio, or retire game-audio in favour of game-craft. Then give the duplicated ducking prompt to the one owning skill.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/game-audio/SKILL.md:20, :46 and :57 say to use the playback position plus output latency. The position being heard is the mixed position minus output latency: Godot's sync_with_audio tutorial (checked through Context7, godot-docs) uses get_playback_position() + get_time_since_last_mix() - get_output_latency(), and this repo's own packages/skills/skills/godot/references/audio.md:82-83 subtracts as well. As written, the pseudocode at :46-47 fires visuals early by twice the latency. No harm was measured: a draft case asking for the sign scored 1.00 in both arms, but Haiku did not open the skill in any of those runs.
  - Suggested: Change :20 to "Schedule beat-locked events from the audio playback position corrected for output latency (subtract it to get what the player hears now)", :46 to `pos = playback_position() - output_latency()`, and :57 to "subtract output latency". Apply the same fix to game-craft/references/audio.md:29 and :32.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/game-audio/SKILL.md:16 states "about -18 LUFS for mobile and handheld per current PlayStation guidance" as first-hand and current. The duplicate at packages/skills/skills/game-craft/references/audio.md:17 says the same figure is second-hand ("as reported by Audiokinetic", checked 2026-10-17). I could not verify the figure against a primary source.
  - Suggested: Carry the same provenance as the game-craft copy: "about -18 LUFS for mobile and handheld (PlayStation guidance as reported by Audiokinetic, second-hand)".
- **low, no-measurable-value.** packages/skills/skills/game-audio/references/adaptive-music.md:48-56 (transition strategy table). A draft case matching five situations to stinger, resume, crossfade, bridge and quantised switch scored 0.80 with the skill and 0.93 without; Haiku picks these from general knowledge, and it did not open the skill in any with-skill run. For Haiku the table changed nothing, so the case was not added.
  - Suggested: No change needed for correctness. If the reference should earn its place, keep only what a model does not already know: the hysteresis thresholds and dwell time (:65-70), the boundary-by-section-length rule (:42) and the authoring constraints (:75-78).
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/game-audio/SKILL.md:52, :54, :55, :56, :57 and :58 repeat workflow steps 2, 1, 4, 5, 7 and 6 (:15, :14, :17, :18, :20, :19) with no new information. Only :53, :59 and :60 add something. The one gotcha a bare model gets wrong (-14 LUFS, :53) sits in the middle of the repeats.

In run v7-alt, all three Haiku runs that read SKILL.md (none opened juice.md) labelled the reference's own recipe `if stopping: remaining = max(remaining, d); return` a BUG, citing the missing per-second cap.

Then either add the cap to the pseudocode at references/juice.md:48-51 or reword SKILL.md:67 to say the cap applies to held or multi-hit attacks that call hit-stop every frame, not to the extend rule.

Rules that exist only in references (hits add to trauma and never reset it, references/camera.md:62; tier presets, references/juice.md:65-69) therefore do not reach a small model.

### game-genres

The skill's content is sound and its cross-references resolve, but on Haiku it is rarely opened: with all skills loaded the three fair triggers score 0.33 / 0.00 / 0.00, and even loaded alone it is not read for calculation-style questions. A rewritten description (tested) lifts routing to 1.00 / 0.67 / 1.00 and makes the new RPG value case go from 0.00/0.00 to 1.00 with vs 0.00 without. The evals now hold 4 routing cases and 3 value cases; the two older value cases need the Write tool and score 0/0 under the permitted runner flags, and Haiku solves both without the skill anyway.

**Routing:** 1/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (run r08): negative-game-genres-bt 1.00; failing: trigger-game-genres-1 0.33, trigger-game-genres-2 0.00, trigger-game-genres-implicit-survival 0.00. Skill loaded alone: all three triggers 3/3. With the tested description rewrite and --all-skills: 3/4 pass (1.00, 0.67, 1.00, negative 1.00).

**Value cases:**

- `value-rpg-modifier-order-and-damage`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without
- `value-daily-sliding-puzzle`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without
- `value-mod-dialogue-conditions`: 0.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/game-genres/SKILL.md:3. On Haiku with --all-skills the skill is not opened for fair prompts: trigger-game-genres-1 0.33, trigger-game-genres-2 0.00, trigger-game-genres-implicit-survival 0.00 (3 runs each, run r08; the misses call no tool or only look for workspace files, so it is 'never opened', not 'lost to a sibling'). Loaded alone the same three prompts score 3/3 each (r04). Loaded alone it is also never read for 'check my math' prompts (RPG stat stacking, FPS TTK, dialogue set block: zero SKILL.md reads in 9 with-arm runs, r05/r09). The current text says 'Use for "make a roguelike/platformer/deckbuilder..." or genre-specific tuning', which does not tell a small model to read it before answering from memory.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement (only the description changed, copy in /tmp/skill-evals/game-genres/alt): "Genre reference numbers and rules for any engine: build order, data model, formulas, starting values and pitfalls for platformers, roguelikes, deckbuilders and card games, puzzles, RPGs, FPS, tower defense, survival-crafting and visual novels, plus branching dialogue runners. Read it before answering any question about building, tuning or checking the math of a game of one of these kinds, even when the genre is only described and no project files exist: \"make a roguelike\", what to build first, jump numbers, TTK and damage falloff, damage formulas and stat modifier stacking, wave HP and income scaling, hunger drain and day length, dialogue variables and conditions. Its numbers replace answers from memory." Scores with --all-skills on Haiku, 3 runs: trigger-1 1.00, trigger-2 0.67, implicit-survival 1.00, negative-game-genres-bt still 1.00 (r06). Value with this text: rpg-modifier-order-and-damage 1.00 with / 0.00 without (r07). Not tested: whether the broader wording pulls prompts away from game-design or game-feel in their own evals.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/game-genres/references/roguelike.md:29-34. The energy scheduler pseudocode restarts `for a in actors` from the first actor on every call of next_actor(). Read literally, the first actor with speed >= 100 gains 100 energy and is returned on every call, so no other actor ever acts; a speed-150 monster never gets its extra turns. rpg.md:44 tells the reader to reuse this scheduler. Found by reading the code, not by an eval.
  - Suggested: Keep the position between calls or make it a time-step loop, e.g. `tick(): for a in actors: a.energy += a.speed` and `next_actor(): loop: for a in actors (resume after the last actor returned): if a.energy >= TURN_COST: a.energy -= TURN_COST; return a; if nobody ready: tick()`. State that an actor with energy still >= TURN_COST acts again before the next tick.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** Of five points tried on Haiku, four showed no gain from the skill because the bare model already gets them right: FPS TTK with the first shot at t = 0 (fps.md:62; 417 ms in 6/6 no-skill runs), simultaneous dialogue set blocks (dialogue.md:53; no-skill runs side with the runner in about 6 of 9), solvable sliding-puzzle generation (puzzle.md:51; all 3 no-skill runs use a legal-move walk or an inversion check) and not using Expression on untrusted dialogue (dialogue.md:92; 0 of 3 no-skill runs use Expression). Only the RPG modifier order and damage constants (rpg.md:29, 38-39) and the recited defaults (falloff 20 m / 60 m / 40%, fps.md:70) differ from Haiku's own answers.
  - Suggested: The measurable value of this skill is its concrete defaults and stacking rules, not the general pitfalls. Keep the tables and formulas prominent and consider trimming pitfalls a model already knows (seeded shuffle, parity, eval on untrusted text) to one line each.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/game-genres/references/rpg.md:29. 'Modifier order: base, then flat adds, then percent multipliers, then overrides, then clamp' does not say whether several percent modifiers add (+25% and +10% = x1.35) or multiply (x1.375), and does not say outright that application order is irrelevant. Without the skill Haiku stacks in application order every time (FINAL_ATK 73 instead of 75 in 9 of 9 no-skill runs, r05/r07/r09), so this is the rule the reference most needs to state plainly.
  - Suggested: Add one sentence: 'The order effects were applied never matters: sum all flat adds, then sum all percent values and multiply once (base + flats) * (1 + sum of percents).' or the multiplicative variant, whichever is intended, with a worked line such as 40 base, +12, +25%, +8 = 75.

### game-performance

The skill content is sound and, when Haiku opens it, it is used correctly (8 of 8 opened runs gave the skill's budget numbers), but opening is the weak point: an implicit thermal-throttling prompt never routes with all skills loaded (0/6), the pre-existing hitch trigger is flaky (4/6), and even loaded alone the skill is opened in only about 60% of runs. Evals now hold 5 cases (2 positive routing, 2 negative, 1 value); the two pre-existing cases were left unchanged, and two further value ideas were dropped because Haiku scored 1.00 without the skill. A tested description rewrite fixed routing (4/4 cases at 3 runs with all skills) but did not raise the open rate on the value case.

**Routing:** Final round, --all-skills on Haiku, 3 runs: 2/4 cases pass. Passing: game-performance-vs-feel 3/3, negative-slow-asset-build-script 3/3. Failing: route-implicit-phone-heat-slowdown 0/3, trigger-game-performance-1 1/3 (was 3/3 in the first round). With the tested description rewrite: 4/4 cases at 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-starting-budget-share`: 0.78 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/game-performance/SKILL.md:3 lists only symptom words ("low FPS", "stutter", "hitches", "frame drops", "frame budget") and says nothing about mobile heat or slow-after-a-while, although SKILL.md:54 covers thermal throttling. Case route-implicit-phone-heat-slowdown (game smooth for 2-3 minutes on a phone, then choppy) scored 0/3 twice with --all-skills on Haiku (no skill read at all), and 3/3 with the skill loaded alone, so it is 'never opened', not 'lost to a sibling'. The existing trigger-game-performance-1 scored 3/3 in one run and 1/3 in the next (4/6).
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite: "Finds and fixes game frame-rate problems by measuring first, in any engine. Covers frame budgets in milliseconds, profiling a release build on target hardware, CPU versus GPU triage, draw calls and batching, overdraw, allocation and GC hitches, shader-compile and loading spikes, pooling, asset budgets and thermal throttling on phones and handhelds. Use when a game runs slow, choppy or laggy, e.g. "low FPS", "stutter", "hitches", "frame drops", "smooth at first then slows down after a few minutes", or "which system is over its frame budget". Not for slow build scripts or tools." Tested once with --all-skills, 3 runs on Haiku: all four routing cases 3/3 (phone-heat 0/3 -> 3/3, hitch trigger 3/3, both negatives stayed closed). It did not help the value case: there the skill was opened in 2/6 runs with the rewrite against 7/12 with the current text (small samples).
- **medium, description.** Loaded as the only skill, game-performance is not opened in roughly 40% of Haiku runs on a direct frame-budget question (value-starting-budget-share: opened 7/12 runs with the current description). Unopened runs invent shares (3.33 ms equal split, or 3.5/4.5); every opened run (8/8 across both descriptions) answered physics 3 ms and scripts 5 ms from SKILL.md:29. The description (SKILL.md:3) gives no reason to open the skill when the user already has a profile and only needs to decide what to attack.
  - Suggested: Say in the description that the skill holds concrete numbers a model should not guess, e.g. add "Holds starting per-subsystem millisecond budgets and asset budget tables; read it before proposing a budget or choosing which subsystem to optimize." Not tested; the tested rewrite above, which only added a trigger phrase about frame budgets, did not raise the open rate.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/evals/game-craft/trigger-performance-first-use-hitch/prompt.md carries the same prompt word for word as packages/skills/evals/game-performance/trigger-game-performance-1/prompt.md, and each case demands its own skill. packages/skills/skills/game-craft/SKILL.md:3 claims "performance" and "stutter", and game-craft/SKILL.md:26 routes low FPS, stutter, hitches and frame budget to its own references/performance.md, so two skills compete for every trigger of this one. This is a likely cause of the 4/6 flakiness on the hitch trigger (not separately measured).
  - Suggested: Decide which skill owns frame-rate problems. If game-performance does, drop "performance" and "stutter" from the game-craft description, have game-craft/SKILL.md:26 point to game-performance, and change the game-craft eval to a different prompt. If game-craft is the intended umbrella when game-performance is not installed, state that in both descriptions and let the shared prompt accept either skill.
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Two of three value ideas showed no effect on Haiku at 3 runs: CPU-versus-GPU triage from a resolution hint against an obvious O(n^2) script loop (SKILL.md:26-28) scored 1.00 with and 1.00 without, and reverting a pooling change that did not move the measured frame time (SKILL.md:19) scored 1.00 with and 1.00 without. The measure-first workflow and the triage rule are things Haiku already does; only the concrete numbers at SKILL.md:29 changed an answer.
  - Suggested: Keep the workflow short and put the weight on what a model cannot derive: the per-subsystem budget at SKILL.md:29, the asset budget table and the regression recipe thresholds in references/profiling-and-budgets.md sections 8 and 9. Consider moving the 60 FPS budget split into the Workflow step 1 or 4 so it is not buried as the last bullet of the CPU or GPU section.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/game-performance/SKILL.md:10 sends slow non-game code to a `problem-solving` skill. No skill of that name exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills (it exists only under the user's ~/.agents/skills).
  - Suggested: Add "if installed" as is done for `godot` on the same line, or drop the skill name and say "slow non-game code such as tools, servers and build scripts is out of scope".

### game-playtest

The skill content is sound and gives Haiku a measurable gain on issue triage (1.00 with, 0.22 without), but its description does not get it opened for implicit requests when all skills compete: routing is 3/5 cases at 3 runs, and both failures are "no skill opened at all". A tested description rewrite scores 5/5. The evals now hold 6 cases (3 existing, 3 new), all loading without errors; the two failing triggers are left failing on purpose.

**Routing:** 3/5 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: trigger-game-playtest-2 (0/3), trigger-implicit-demo-drop-off (0/3). Both are 3/3 with the skill loaded alone, and 5/5 cases pass with the tested description rewrite.

**Value cases:**

- `value-triage-priority-score`: 1.00 with, 0.22 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/game-playtest/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded on Haiku, two fair implicit triggers do not open the skill: trigger-game-playtest-2 (tester notes into a fix order) scored 2/3 in the first run and 0/3 in the final run, and trigger-implicit-demo-drop-off (what to record to see where demo players stop) scored 0/3. In every failing run Haiku read no skill at all, so it is not losing to a sibling. With the skill loaded alone both cases score 3/3.
  - Suggested: Tested: 5/5 routing cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (both failing triggers 3/3, both negatives still 3/3). Text: Plans, runs and analyses game playtests, demos and betas with real players. Covers research questions, recruiting, session scripts, observer notes, surveys, what to log to see where and why players stop (telemetry events, funnels, quit points), and turning tester notes or feedback into a ranked fix list with keep-or-kill criteria. Use whenever testers or players have played or will play a build, even if the word "playtest" is not used, such as "notes from testers", "is it fun", "players drop off before level 3", "what should I record in the build" or "what do we fix first".
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/game-playtest/SKILL.md:30-31. Steps 7 and 8 say "severity" and "players affected x severity" but the 4-level scale and the tie-break exist only in references/session-kit.md:125 and its section 8, and neither step points there. In value run r3, one of three with-skill runs read only SKILL.md and invented its own scale (A=2 B=5 C=12 D=4 instead of 4/10/12/6). Across the three value runs, one with-skill run also never opened the skill.
  - Suggested: Put the scale inline in step 7 ("severity 4 blocker, 3 major, 2 minor, 1 cosmetic") and end step 8 with "scale, tie-break and triage table: references/session-kit.md sections 8 and 9".
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/game-craft/SKILL.md:3 and :20 claim "playtests" and "playtest plans", and game-craft/references/playtest.md is a condensed copy of this skill. The prompt of evals/game-playtest/trigger-game-playtest-1 is word for word the prompt of evals/game-craft/trigger-playtest-plan, so the two suites expect different skills for the same request. In my runs Haiku opened game-playtest for it 6/6 times, never game-craft.
  - Suggested: Decide which skill owns playtest requests. If both stay, drop "playtests" and "playtest plans" from the game-craft description or change the game-craft eval prompt so the two suites do not contradict each other.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/game-playtest/SKILL.md:10 names a `unit-testing` skill. No skill of that name exists in the four skills directories of this repo. (`godot-testing`, `gh-triage`, `game-design` and `game-ui` do exist.)
  - Suggested: Remove `unit-testing`, or name real ones: "automated tests and code QA (`godot-testing`, `dotnet-testing`, `java-testing`)".
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/game-playtest/references/session-kit.md:64. The rule to say "I didn't make this" even when the facilitator did is a parenthesis inside a script block. In a discarded plan-review case, Haiku with the skill loaded answered CHANGE on that item 3/3 and never opened the reference. The rule also asks the facilitator to lie to participants, which a model will resist unless told why.
  - Suggested: If the rule is intended, state it in SKILL.md step 5 with the reason (players soften criticism for the author). Otherwise replace the line with a truthful one such as "Be blunt, we need the problems more than the praise".
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/game-playtest/references/session-kit.md:125. `priority = players_affected x severity` on a 1 to 4 scale ranks a cosmetic issue seen by all 8 players (8) above a blocker that made 1 player quit (4). Nothing limits this.
  - Suggested: Add a floor, for example "any severity 4 issue is fixed or explicitly waived before lower severities, whatever its score".
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Two plan-review value ideas did not discriminate on Haiku and were dropped. Scores were 0.75 with against 0.67 without, and 1.00 with against 0.78 without. Haiku already knows most of SKILL.md:26-32 and the Gotchas section.
  - Suggested: No change required. If SKILL.md is shortened, the Gotchas that restate the workflow (helping the player, team and friends as testers, small-sample percentages) are the candidates; the specific numbers and the triage scale are what add value.

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/game-prototype/SKILL.md:3. The description covers setting up a spike and planning a jam, but not judging a finished spike or checking an existing jam plan, and gives no hint that the skill holds specific rules. Evidence: with the skill loaded alone, Haiku read it 0/6 times on the two value cases (its reasoning in the log: 'the question is clear enough that I can answer'), so with/without were 0.50/0.46 and 0.63/0.54. With all skills loaded, game-prototype-mechanic was read 1/3 (twice in two separate runs); the other runs made no tool call at all, so it is 'never opened', not lost to a sibling.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: "Timeboxed game prototyping and game jams: sets up a greybox mechanic spike or vertical slice around one question, judges playtest results against fixed keep, kill or retune rules, and scopes a jam to the clock (per-length budget for mechanics, levels and audio, hour schedule, feature freeze, cut list, submit early). Use when prototyping or greyboxing a mechanic, deciding whether to keep, kill or retune a prototype, or planning or checking a plan for a game jam or 48-hour build. Its verdict rules and jam budgets are stricter than common advice, so read it before giving a verdict or reviewing a plan." Scores with this text (Haiku, 3 runs): routing with --all-skills 4/4 cases at 1.00 (mechanic 3/3, jam 3/3, both negatives clean); value-jam-scope-budget 1.00 with / 0.50 without; value-spike-verdicts 1.00 with / 0.54 without, skill read 6/6.
