### gh-repo-setup

The skill is accurate (the rulesets reference matches the GitHub REST docs fetched today) and clearly helps Haiku on a full setup plan, but its description omits branch-protection wording and three of its rules are not followed as written. It had no evals; it now has 5 cases (2 positive routes, 2 near-miss negatives, 1 value case) that all load cleanly. Two are left failing on purpose: the implicit force-push route scores 0/3 with all skills loaded, and the value case swings between 0.54 and 0.88 with the skill; a tested description rewrite plus a two-sentence instruction fix bring them to 3/3 and 0.96-1.00.

**Routing:** 3/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-implicit-force-push-to-main (0/3; 3/3 with the skill alone and 3/3 with the tested description rewrite)

**Value cases:**

- `value-setup-plan-contract`: 0.54 with, 0.25 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/gh-repo-setup/SKILL.md:3 names 'branch or tag rulesets' but none of the words a user uses for that job (branch protection, force-push, require reviews). The implicit case route-implicit-force-push-to-main (force-push over main, self-merges, 'give me the exact commands') scores 0/3 with all skills loaded in two separate runs; the logs show no tool call at all, Haiku answers from memory. With the skill loaded alone it is 3/3, so it is never opened rather than lost to a sibling. The same weakness shows in the value case: in one run 2 of 3 with-skill runs did not open the skill even though it was the only one loaded.
  - Suggested: Tested: 3/3 on the implicit case with all skills loaded (other three routing cases stayed 3/3, including both negatives). Replace the description with: "Audits and sets up a GitHub repository's surface with gh: branch protection through rulesets (block force-pushes and deletion of main, require PR approvals, bypass actors), label taxonomy, issue forms, PR template, CODEOWNERS, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, with a dry-run plan and an applied/skipped/failed report. Use when creating or tidying a repo, when asked to protect a branch, stop direct or force pushes, require reviews before merge, or add rulesets, templates or labels. GitHub only, not for Forgejo, Codeberg or Gitea."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/gh-repo-setup/SKILL.md:36 asks for a plan table 'module | action (create/update/skip) | exact command | reason'. In 12 with-skill runs of value-setup-plan-contract, 10 opened the skill and only 1 of those produced that table; the rest wrote numbered steps, or a table without the command column. Commands with JSON bodies do not fit a table cell and the line does not say where they go.
  - Suggested: Tested together with the rulesets.md:26 fix and the description rewrite: plan table 6/6, case score 1.00 and 0.96 at 3 runs each. Replace the first sentence of SKILL.md:36 with: "Open the plan with one markdown table whose header row is `| module | action | exact command | reason |`, one row per module (action is create, update or skip), then wait for approval. File contents and JSON bodies go below the table; the command cell names the file it sends."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/gh-repo-setup/references/rulesets.md:26 says to trial with evaluate 'where the plan allows it (evaluate needs GitHub Enterprise; otherwise use disabled, check, then flip to active)'. 'The plan' reads as either the GitHub plan or the skill's own Plan step, and a disabled ruleset checks nothing, so there is no trial. On a Team-plan prompt, of the 10 with-skill runs that opened the skill one still sent "enforcement": "evaluate" ('try evaluate first'), and most others invented their own trial (an active ruleset on a throwaway branch, or a scratch repo).
  - Suggested: Tested (0 of 6 runs sent evaluate; all trialled on a throwaway branch pattern). Replace the sentence with: "To trial a new rule on GitHub Enterprise, create the ruleset with `\"enforcement\": \"evaluate\"`. On Free, Pro or Team never send `evaluate` (the API rejects it): a `disabled` ruleset checks nothing, so trial the same rules as an `active` ruleset scoped to a throwaway branch pattern, then create the real one."
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/gh-repo-setup/SKILL.md:8 and :48 hand work off to `gh-actions`, `dependabot` and `agent-instructions`. None of the three exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills, so the CI module (SKILL.md:48 'Hand off to gh-actions') points nowhere.
  - Suggested: Drop the backticked names and state the boundary in plain words ("Not for workflow content, Dependabot config or agent instruction files"), and change the CI row to "Out of scope: do not write workflow content here; only add `.github/workflows/` to CODEOWNERS". Restore the names if those skills are added to this repo.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/gh-repo-setup/references/labels.md:24-30 says 'The API has no create-or-update call. Check, then create or update' and then gives only `gh label create ... --force`, which is an unconditional overwrite. That conflicts with SKILL.md:14 ('never overwrites customized files') and SKILL.md:36 (list the labels --force would change). Haiku resolved it the safe way in every run that opened the skill (dropped --force for existing labels), so this is wording, not a measured failure.
  - Suggested: Give both commands: `gh label create` without --force for labels missing from `gh label list`, and `gh label edit "<name>" --color ... --description ...` (or --force) only for existing labels the approved plan lists as changed.
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Two fact-quiz value ideas did not discriminate on Haiku and were dropped: ruleset API facts from references/rulesets.md:16-26,55,61,67 (PUT not PATCH, full body, 422 on missing pull_request parameters, evaluate needs Enterprise, exempt leaves no audit entry, pull_request rule last) scored 0.94 with and 0.94 without; label and CODEOWNERS facts from references/labels.md:30-32 and community-files.md:7,36-38 plus SKILL.md:59 scored 0.94 with and 0.89 without. Asked directly, Haiku already knows these; the skill's measurable value is in applying them unprompted inside a plan (~DEFAULT_BRANCH, no evaluate on Team, the codeowners/errors check).

Loaded alone, the same cases score 3/3. The description is a list of quoted command phrases and gives no reason why memory is not good enough. It also names `git-commit`, which does not exist in the four skills directories.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite, 3/3 on all three routing cases with --all-skills (9/9 runs) and 1.00 on both value cases loaded alone: "Runs and explains git-flow in a repo with main + develop and feature/release/hotfix/support branches, using git-flow-next, the apt AVH CLI or plain git. Related: the siblings that point at this skill describe it as 'history spelunking (git-history)' (packages/skills/skills/git-flow/SKILL.md:3, packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/SKILL.md:3), which is reading history, not what this skill does, and trunk-based lists the trigger 'release branch cherry-pick', which collides with this skill's 'backport a fix' (collision not measured).
  - Suggested: Drop the sentence at SKILL.md:8 or write it as 'when a git-commit skill is installed', the wording branching-models/SKILL.md:32 already uses. In git-flow and trunk-based change 'history spelunking (git-history)' to 'rewriting or recovering history (git-history)'.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/git-history/SKILL.md:15 says to undo a rewrite 'through a backup or rescue branch' but the command (`git branch rescue/<name> <sha-or-HEAD@{n}>`) is only in references/recovery-and-bisect.md:43, reached through the pointer at SKILL.md:90. In run value3-alt, 2 of 3 with-arm runs read SKILL.md, did not open the reference, and answered 'undo that rebase, pre-rebase tip is 4be1a90' with a backup branch of the current HEAD (the 'Before a rewrite' step 3 pattern) instead of a rescue branch at 4be1a90; the one run that opened the reference got it right. After the question was reworded to ask for the command that makes the old commits available again, 3/3 passed without the reference (run value4-alt), so the gap is narrow.
  - Suggested: Put the command in the rule at SKILL.md:15: '...restore through a rescue branch instead: `git branch rescue/<name> <pre-rewrite-sha>` (sha from the backup ref, `ORIG_HEAD` or `git reflog`), which moves nothing.'
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/git-history/SKILL.md:17 and :38 tell the agent to ask 'with AskUserQuestion'. That is a Claude Code tool name; pi's equivalent is `ask_user`, and in the eval harness neither exists. Seven skills in packages/skills/skills use the same name, so this may be a deliberate convention.
  - Suggested: Say 'ask the user (AskUserQuestion or ask_user where available)' or just 'ask the user, showing the exact command and what would be lost'.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/git-history/references/recovery-and-bisect.md:21 lists exit status 1 to 127 except 125 as 'bad'. Current git treats 126 and 127 specially in `bisect run`: when the command returns one of them it re-runs it on the known-good revision and stops with 'bisect run failed' if it still does, so a missing or non-executable script is not recorded as bad. Checked only against message strings in the local git 2.56.1 binary ('unable to verify %s on '%s' revision', 'exit code %d from %s is < 0 or >= 128'); not checked against the documentation.
  - Suggested: Add a row or a note: '126/127 (script not executable or not found): git checks the command against the known-good commit and stops the run instead of marking commits bad.'
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Several rules were tried as value items and dropped because Haiku gets them right with no skill loaded, 3/3 each (runs value1, value2): the bisect exit-status table at references/recovery-and-bisect.md:18-23 (0, 1, 2, 125, 139, 255 all correct), ask rather than stash a dirty tree (SKILL.md:14, when ASK is offered as an answer), `--force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>` (SKILL.md:16), `cherry-pick -x` for a backport (SKILL.md:79, :85) and `GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue` when told the shell is non-interactive (SKILL.md:54). The skill changed the outcome only for the backup ref before a rebase (SKILL.md:25), rescue branch instead of reset (SKILL.md:15) and a dedicated backport branch (SKILL.md:85).
  - Suggested: No change required. If the skill is shortened, the three rules that discriminate are the ones to keep prominent; the bisect exit-status table is the safest candidate to cut down to the 125 rule.

Scores with this text on Haiku at 3 runs: OutOfSync case 3/3 alone and 2/3 with all skills (was 0/3 and 0/3); the implicit setup trigger and the Kustomize negative stayed at 3/3 in both modes.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** For Haiku the skill changed nothing on the three things tried (3 runs each, skill loaded alone vs none). (1) Writing an ExternalSecret and a HelmRelease with current API versions (references/secrets.md:32, references/flux.md:3): with 1.00, without 1.00. (2) Six true/false claims on wait vs healthChecks, retryInterval default, deny windows and manual sync, no retry of a failed revision, api-resources group matching, finalizer cascade (references/flux.md:3,56-57, references/argocd.md:44,91,37): with 1.00, without 1.00. (3) Defaults and numbers (homelab default Flux, directory per environment, 60 s minimum interval, ESO 0.17, default refreshPolicy; SKILL.md:44,61, references/flux.md:57, references/secrets.md:32,34): with 0.80, without 0.73 as run; one of the five graders in that trial had a broken regex, and re-scored by hand from the logs it is about 0.87 vs 0.80. Only the ESO version question differed, and only in the one with-run that opened the skill.
  - Suggested: Do not expect the factual content to lift a current small model. If the skill should earn its place, the distinct parts are the safety contract (SKILL.md:12-18) and the workflow (SKILL.md:73-81); those need cases with shell tools and a scaffolded repo, which were out of scope here (Read/Glob/Grep only, no workspace).
- **medium, instructions.** In the defaults trial, 2 of 3 runs with the skill loaded alone never opened SKILL.md and answered the ESO version 'from memory' as 0.10 (run logs under /tmp/skill-evals/gitops/r4-value). Combined with the routing result, Haiku treats GitOps questions without repo files as recall questions, and nothing in packages/skills/skills/gitops/SKILL.md:3 tells it to read the skill for a question as opposed to a setup task.
  - Suggested: Same description change as above; the clause 'read it before answering even when no repo files are at hand' is the part that moved the debugging case from 0/3 to 3/3 with the skill alone.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/gitops/references/secrets.md:32 says v1beta1 'has been deprecated since ESO 0.17' and that v1 is 'GA since ESO 1.0'. The ESO v0.17.0 release notes say that release stops serving the v1beta1 APIs and that manifests must be moved to v1 before upgrading from 0.16, where v1 is already supported. So v1beta1 manifests fail to apply on 0.17 and later, which is stronger than deprecated. I did not check the 1.0 GA wording.

- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/gitops/SKILL.md:71 and references/argocd.md:44 say Argo CD does not retry a failed revision, while the example Application at references/argocd.md:33-38 sets retry with limit 5. The Argo CD auto-sync docs confirm the no-reattempt rule, but the skill does not say how the two relate, and the docs also describe retry.refresh, which the skill omits.
  - Suggested: Add one sentence at references/argocd.md:44: "`retry` re-runs the same sync operation up to `limit` times; once that is exhausted, auto-sync does not start a new attempt for the same commit. Set `retry.refresh: true` to pick up a newer revision while a sync is retrying."

With --all-skills on Haiku the two fair positive triggers are read in 1/3 and 2/3 runs (first pass) and 0/3 and 1/3 runs (final pass). The description is a keyword list and gives no reason to open the skill when the flag is already in the prompt.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite, scored 3/3 on both positives and 3/3 on the negative with all 173 skills loaded (/tmp/skill-evals/goff-flags/route3-alt): "Writes, reviews and debugs GO Feature Flag (GOFF) flag files: the YAML, JSON or TOML with `variations`, `targeting`, `defaultRule`, `percentage`, `progressiveRollout`, `scheduledRollout`, `experimentation` and `bucketingKey`. Read it before answering any question about how such a flag evaluates, even when the flag is pasted in the prompt and no file exists: GOFF's rules cannot be guessed (percentages are relative weights, a rule's percentage overrides its variation, a disabled flag or a missing bucketingKey attribute returns the SDK default). Use for a `*.goff.yaml` file, a flag that serves the wrong variation or the wrong share of users, splitting by team or company instead of by user, rule order, query syntax, time-based rollouts, and `go-feature-flag-cli` lint, evaluate and manifest. Not for the relay proxy, retrievers, exporters or notifiers (goff-relay-proxy), OpenFeature SDK and provider code (goff-sdk), vendor-neutral flag practice in app code (feature-flags), or stale flag audits (flag-hygiene)."

Text: 'Gradle builds: ./gradlew failures, slow or never-cached tasks, build.gradle(.kts) and settings.gradle(.kts), libs.versions.toml catalogs, convention plugins in build-logic, toolchains, dependency resolution. Read this before answering any Gradle question, including when the build files are not in the workspace and the user only describes the build or pastes an error. Use for configuration cache failures ("Task.project at execution time is unsupported"), "Could not resolve" or "No matching variant", a task that reruns or misses the build cache, the same setup copied into every module, or adding a task, dependency or convention plugin. - **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/gradle/SKILL.md:59 and references/config-cache.md:20 say that wrapping the read in `providers.provider { project.version }` and calling `.get()` in the action still fails. Checked on Gradle 9.8.2 (local wrapper dist, JDK 27) with --configuration-cache: `val v = providers.provider { project.version }` in the register block with `doLast { println(v.get()) }` stores the entry, prints the version and the second run reports 'Reusing configuration cache'. It only fails when the provider is created inside the action itself (`doLast { providers.provider { project.version }.get() }`), and then with 'cannot serialize object of type DefaultProject', not the Task.project message.
  - Suggested: Rewrite both places: a provider created at configuration time in the register block and read with `.get()` in the action is fine, because Gradle evaluates it when it stores the cache entry. What fails is creating the provider, or touching `project`/`providers` through the script object, inside `doLast`/`doFirst`. Drop 'does not fix it'.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/gradle/references/config-cache.md:23 lists `System.getenv("X")` inside a task action as a configuration cache violation. On Gradle 9.8.2 a task with `doLast { println(System.getenv("HOME")) }` runs with --configuration-cache with no problem reported and the entry is reused on the second run. Reading the environment at execution time is allowed.
  - Suggested: Remove the row, or change it to the real concern: `System.getenv` read at configuration time becomes a cache input and invalidates the entry when it changes; `providers.environmentVariable("X")` is the way to declare it as a task input.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/gradle/SKILL.md:10 sends the reader to `gradle-skills:gradle-best-practices`, `gradle-skills:gradle-wrapper-upgrade` and `android-skills:agp-9-upgrade`. ### grafana-dashboards

The skill had no evals; it now has 3 routing cases and 1 value case under packages/skills/evals/grafana-dashboards/, all loading cleanly (10 runner invocations, logs in /tmp/skill-evals/grafana-dashboards/). The skill helps Haiku on the provisioning rules (1.00 with, 0.33 without) and routes 3/3 when loaded alone, but with all skills loaded the two positive triggers are opened only about half the time; a tested description rewrite took them to 6/6. The skill has one real contradiction (its provider example breaks its own folder rule), and its "do not write JSON from memory" rule had no effect on Haiku.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run: route-negative-quantile-query 3/3, route-incident-board-cleanup 2/3, route-implicit-boards-lost-on-rebuild 2/3; earlier run 3/3, 2/3, 1/3); failing: route-incident-board-cleanup, route-implicit-boards-lost-on-rebuild. Skill loaded alone: 3/3 cases pass. With the tested description rewrite and --all-skills: 3/3 cases pass in two runs.

**Value cases:**

- `value-dashboards-as-code-review`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/grafana-dashboards/references/provisioning.md:14 and :21 vs :25. The example provider sets both `folder: Services` and `foldersFromFilesStructure: true`, and the bullet four lines below says not to combine them. Grafana's provisioning docs (checked via Context7, /websites/grafana_grafana) say: 'To use foldersFromFilesStructure, you must unset the folder and folderUid options.' The example is the thing an agent copies. In the value case Haiku followed the bullet (R1: CHANGE in every run where it read the reference), but the copy-paste example is still wrong.
  - Suggested: Remove `folder: Services` from the example at provisioning.md:14 (keep `foldersFromFilesStructure: true`), and reword line 25 to the documented rule: "`foldersFromFilesStructure` maps directories to folders; `folder` and `folderUid` must be unset."
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/grafana-dashboards/SKILL.md:3. With --all-skills on Haiku the two fair positive triggers are opened only part of the time: route-implicit-boards-lost-on-rebuild 1/3 and 2/3 (3/6 over two runs), route-incident-board-cleanup 2/3 and 2/3 (4/6). With the skill loaded alone both are 3/3. The event logs of the failing runs show no sibling skill being read: Haiku lists the empty workspace and answers from memory, so this is 'never opened', not a collision with promql or observability-instrumentation. The description leads with method ('from operator questions rather than the metric list') and has none of the words a user uses for these problems (too many panels, boards lost, datasource not found).
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite, scored 3/3 on all three routing cases in two separate --all-skills runs (6/6 on each positive, negative still 3/3): "Designs, reviews and trims Grafana dashboards (boards) so they answer on-call questions, and keeps them in git. Use for any Grafana dashboard question, even when the workspace holds no dashboard files: too many panels, what goes at the top, RED or USE panels, dashboards lost after a rebuild, 'datasource not found' after an import, dashboard JSON and datasource UIDs, file provisioning, Terraform or the Foundation SDK. Not for writing the PromQL inside a panel (promql)." Caveat: the text was written after the two trigger prompts and shares some of their wording, so the gain is likely overstated for other phrasings; the clause 'even when the workspace holds no dashboard files' is the part aimed at the observed failure.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/grafana-dashboards/SKILL.md:43 ('Do not write dashboard JSON from memory') and :16 ('Do not invent metrics'). Tried as a value case (prompt: 'give me the dashboard JSON for checkout-api so I can import it', no export, no metric names): 0.33 with and 0.33 without. In all 3 with-skill runs Haiku read SKILL.md and still wrote a complete dashboard JSON with assumed client_golang metric names, only adding a 'verify the names' note (/tmp/skill-evals/grafana-dashboards/r2-value/runs/grafana-dashboards/value-no-json-from-memory/). The rule sits in the middle of a reference-style paragraph after the checklist, the workflow gives no step for the case where no export or datasource is reachable, and SKILL.md:14 says to ask the user but nothing says to stop until they answer.
  - Suggested: Move the rule into the Workflow as a gate in step 3, e.g.: "If you have neither an export from the target instance nor the real metric names, stop and ask for them (Dashboard settings > JSON Model, and a /metrics sample or a metric-name query). Do not hand over JSON built from assumed metric names or a remembered schema." If a draft with assumed names is acceptable when the user insists, say so explicitly; as written the rule is absolute and is not followed.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/grafana-dashboards/references/provisioning.md:24 says with `allowUiUpdates: false` 'edits in the UI are lost or refused'. Grafana's docs say saving is refused (a 'Cannot save provisioned dashboard' dialog); edits are overwritten on the next file change only when `allowUiUpdates` is true.
  - Suggested: "`allowUiUpdates: false` makes the file the source of truth: Grafana refuses to save UI edits. With `true`, UI saves go to the database and are overwritten the next time the file changes."
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/grafana-dashboards/SKILL.md:43 describes the V1 resource only as a wrapper and V2 as 'for newer layouts'. Current Grafana docs call V2 'the current schema', say V1 was the default API format between v12.2.0 and v13.0.0, and the export dialog says to choose Classic 'if you plan to use the dashboard in Grafana v12.4 or older'. The skill's statement is not wrong but stops at v12.2. Separately, provisioning.md:40 points to `$__env{...}` expansion for provisioning files; I could not verify that syntax against the provisioning docs (they document `$ENV_VAR` and `${ENV_VAR}`), so it is unverified, not confirmed wrong.
  - Suggested: Add the version bounds: Classic default before v12.2, V1 resource default from v12.2 to v13.0, V2 the current schema; export Classic for targets on v12.4 or older. Check the `$__env{...}` claim against the provisioning docs and switch to `${ENV_VAR}` if it is not documented there.

### handoff

handoff is a manual command (disable-model-invocation: true), so it can only be tested for staying quiet on routing and for value through /skill:handoff. All three quiet cases pass 3/3 with all skills loaded, and both new value cases discriminate on Haiku. The main problem is that the skill is written for Claude Code: on pi it tells the user to launch `claude --bg` and its recover mode reads Claude Code's transcript store. The --recover mode has no eval, because it needs a shell the runner does not give.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (all are must-not-fire cases; the skill is manual, so no positive trigger can exist). Routing cases were run once and not changed afterwards.

**Value cases:**

- `value-bg-document-and-launch`: 1.00 with, 0.22 without
- `value-catchup-flag-briefing`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/SKILL.md:36, :43, :46-50 prescribe Claude Code commands (`claude "$(cat <file>)"`, `claude --bg --name`, `claude agents/attach/logs/stop`) in a package installed into pi. The commands are real (checked against `claude --help`, Claude Code 2.1.332), but nothing is given for pi. In run value1, value-bg-document-and-launch with-0, Haiku running in pi told the user to start the new session with `claude --bg --name "Fix checkout flake" -- "$(cat "$F")"`. The bare arm (without-0) read pi's docs/cli.md and proposed `pi -n "checkout-flake" @<file>`, which is the right harness. `scripts/import.ts:83` already lists `claude --` and `CLAUDE_SESSION` as Claude-only patterns.
  - Suggested: Give the pi path, or mark the skill claude-code-only in `scripts/import.ts` CLAUDE_CODE_ONLY. For pi: line 36 becomes `pi @<file>` (or `pi "$(cat <file>)"`). For --bg, pi 1.7.0's docs/cli.md lists no background flag, so either drop the mode on pi or state "if the harness is pi, skip the launch, give the file path and say why", as line 50 already does for older Claude Code. If the skill changes, update graders t3 and t5 of value-bg-document-and-launch with it.
- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/SKILL.md:17 and references/recover.md:86-105: the --recover mode only works for Claude Code sessions. `scripts/session_recover.py:77-87` reads `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude/projects`; `<this-session-id>` is `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}`, which pi does not substitute; recover.md:86 and :94 send the user to `claude --resume` and `claude "$(cat <file>)"`. On pi the list step would report no sessions or list unrelated Claude Code ones. Not verified by an eval: the runner gives no shell.
  - Suggested: State at SKILL.md:17 that --recover covers Claude Code transcripts only and say what to do on pi (`pi --resume`, or `pi --fork <id>` for a copy), or teach the script pi's session store and take the session id from pi's environment.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/SKILL.md:17 gives the script as `python3 -I scripts/session_recover.py` and says "run the script exactly that way". The path is relative to the skill directory (the import strips `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/`, `scripts/import.ts:111`), but recover.md:92 and :95 run it with `--project "$PWD"` from the project directory, where `scripts/session_recover.py` does not exist. Not verified by an eval (no shell in the runner).
  - Suggested: Write "`python3 -I <this skill's directory>/scripts/session_recover.py`; resolve the path against the directory of this SKILL.md, not the working directory".
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/references/catchup.md:3-33 is a near-verbatim copy of packages/skills/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:8 and :15-43 (same workflow, rules and checklist). Two copies of one rule set will drift. catchup/SKILL.md:13 also points to a `session-recover` skill that exists in none of the four skills directories; that job is now `handoff --recover`. The eval prompt of handoff/handoff-quiet-away is word for word the prompt of catchup/catchup-away; here that is the intended counterpart (catchup must fire, handoff must stay quiet), so it was left.
  - Suggested: Keep one owner. Either drop the --catchup mode (description, SKILL.md:9 and :16, references/catchup.md), since the model-invocable catchup skill already covers it and `/skill:catchup` invokes it by hand, or reduce references/catchup.md to the one difference ("writes no handoff file") plus a pointer to the catchup skill. In catchup/SKILL.md:13 replace `session-recover` with `handoff --recover`.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/handoff/SKILL.md:13 opens with "`the arguments given with the command` may start with one flag". This is the import's replacement for `$ARGUMENTS` (`scripts/import.ts:113`) left inside backticks, so it reads as a literal string. SKILL.md:32 tells the next agent to "call the Skill tool", which pi does not have. In run value1 Haiku wrote "Suggested skills: None specified." in every with-skill run.
  - Suggested: Line 13: "The text typed after the command may start with one flag:". Line 32: "**Suggested skills**: the skills the next agent should load first, by name; leave the section out when there are none."

**Eval changes**

### hubflow

hubflow had no evals; it now has five (two positive routing cases, one near-miss negative, two value cases), all loading cleanly and all passing on Haiku. The skill routes reliably against the full skill set and clearly changes Haiku's answers, but it is duplicated almost wholesale inside branching-models, and two of its safety statements are wrong or needlessly hedged when checked against the HubFlow source.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (both positives 3/3 reading hubflow, negative 0/3); failing: none

**Value cases:**

- `value-feature-finish-after-squash-merge`: 1.00 with, 0.52 without
- `value-old-line-hotfix-plan`: 1.00 with, 0.29 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/branching-models/references/hubflow.md is a near copy of packages/skills/skills/hubflow/SKILL.md (same sections and command table), and branching-models/references/detection.md is byte-identical to hubflow/references/detection.md. branching-models' description (SKILL.md:3) also claims `git hf` and `[hubflow]` config. The sibling evals disagree about the owner: evals/branching-models/trigger-hubflow-command requires branching-models to fire on a `[hubflow]` prompt, while evals/git-flow/route-negative-hubflow-feature says such a prompt belongs to 'hubflow (or branching-models)'. In my runs with all skills loaded, hubflow was read in 6/6 positive runs and branching-models in none.
  - Suggested: Pick one owner for HubFlow. Either drop HubFlow from branching-models (remove `git hf` and `[hubflow]` from its description, delete references/hubflow.md, point to the hubflow skill) or retire hubflow, git-flow and trunk-based in favour of branching-models. Do not ship both copies; the two accuracy fixes below would otherwise need making twice.
- **medium, accuracy.** SKILL.md:19 and references/commands.md:3 say to ask before `update -p` ('assume it pushes unless checked'), and SKILL.md:54 describes `git hf update` as only merging and pruning. In the source (git-hf-update, hubflow-common `hubflow_merge_latest_changes_from_origin`), `-p` is the prune toggle (default on), and plain `git hf update` itself pushes: it pushes the current branch, then pushes master and develop after merging origin into them. So the ask-first rule is attached to the wrong thing and the Refresh row hides a push.
  - Suggested: SKILL.md:19 and commands.md:3: replace '`update -p` (assume it pushes unless checked)' with '`git hf update` (pushes the current branch, and master/develop after merging origin into them; `-p` only toggles pruning)'. SKILL.md:54: add 'pushes the current branch, master and develop' to the Refresh row. commands.md:31: annotate `[-p]` as prune.
- **medium, accuracy.** SKILL.md:19, SKILL.md:53 and references/commands.md:3 call the remote delete on `cancel` 'unverified', and commands.md:17 shows `-f` as optional. The source of `git hf feature cancel` settles both: without `-f` it exits ('you _must_ use the -f flag'), and with push on (the default) it pushes the branch, then deletes it on origin, then runs `git branch -D` locally.
  - Suggested: State it as fact: '`git hf feature cancel -f NAME` is refused without -f; it pushes the branch, deletes it on origin and force-deletes it locally (`-k` keeps the local branch).' Change commands.md:17 to `git hf feature cancel -f [-k] <name>`.
- **low, accuracy.** SKILL.md:63 says 'HubFlow's source wasn't checked, so assume it doesn't either' about a hotfix while a release branch is open. git-hf-hotfix `cmd_finish` merges only into master and develop (tag or branch); there is no release-branch handling.
  - Suggested: Replace the hedge with: 'HubFlow's hotfix finish merges only into master and develop, never into an open release branch.' Keep the manual-merge instruction.
- **low, description.** SKILL.md:3 names `git-commit` in the 'Not for' list, and SKILL.md:20 defers to it; no git-commit skill exists in the four skills directories of this repo. (git-flow, trunk-based, git-history and gh-release do exist.) Line 20 hedges with 'when it is installed'; the description does not.
  - Suggested: Drop '(git-commit)' from the description, leaving 'Not for ... commit messages or branch names', or add the skill to the repo. Line 20 can stay as written.

**Eval changes**

- added: `hubflow/route-feature-finish-refused`. Positive trigger: user pastes the 'Please raise a pull-request via GitHub first, or use the -f flag.' refusal from `git hf feature finish` and asks whether -f is safe. Never says HubFlow. 3/3 with all skills loaded.
- added: `hubflow/route-implicit-datasift-release`. Implicit positive trigger: 'the DataSift flavour of gitflow' with auto-pushed, PR-merged features, needs to cut 4.1.0. Names neither HubFlow nor `git hf`. 3/3 with all skills loaded; branching-models was not read in any run.
- added: `hubflow/route-negative-plain-gitflow-release`. Near-miss negative (min 0, max 0): `git flow release finish` with `[gitflow]` config and the AVH CLI, which belongs to git-flow. hubflow was not read in 3/3 runs.
- added: `hubflow/value-feature-finish-after-squash-merge`. Four fixed final lines graded by regex: feature start pushed on its own, finish refuses after a squash merge, -f merges locally and pushes develop, open the next PR with gh pr create rather than feature submit. After the first run I lowered the FINISH grader to weight 1 because bare Haiku always got it, and raised the others to 2. With 1.00, without 0.52 (bare runs were 1.00, 0.14 and 0.43, so the without score is noisy and sits just above the 0.5 target).

Five fixed final lines graded by regex on a plan to hotfix an old line: no brew install (clone and install.sh), hotfix start pushes, finish merges into latest master, conflicts resolve toward the hotfix branch, open release needs a manual merge. ### implement-plan

The skill routes well on explicit triggers and measurably helps Haiku: the new fixed-answer value case scores 1.00 with the skill and 0.39 without. The implicit "pick it up where it stopped" trigger is unreliable with all skills loaded (5/9 over three runs of 3, last run 2/3), and a one-clause description addition scored 6/6. The two pre-existing value cases need --scaffold and --allow-tools, which I was not allowed to pass, so their numbers below are not meaningful and my grader fix in one of them is only checked offline against synthetic and recorded traces.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run); failing: route-resume-remaining-slices at 2/3 (5/9 across three runs; 3/3 with the skill loaded alone; 6/6 with the tested description rewrite). implement-plan-routing 3/3, route-negative-plan-to-issues 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-slice-run-decisions`: 1.00 with, 0.39 without
- `value-contradictory-plan`: 0.75 with, 0.75 without
- `value-status-and-run-through`: 0.40 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/implement-plan/SKILL.md:3 lists only "implement this plan", "continue implementing" and pointing at a plan file as triggers. The implicit resume prompt in route-resume-remaining-slices ("slices 1 and 2 landed ... pick it up where it stopped and take it the rest of the way") fired 3/3, 0/3 and 2/3 on Haiku with --all-skills (5/9). With the skill loaded alone it fired 3/3, and in the failing runs no sibling skill was read: Haiku looked for the plan file, did not find it and stopped. So it is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite, 6/6 on the same case with --all-skills (two runs of 3, against 5/9 for the current text; the sample is small): "Executes an approved multi-slice implementation plan file end to end, running independent slices in parallel worktrees and checking, reviewing, committing, and updating a Status block after each slice without asking. Use when the user says "implement this plan", "continue implementing", asks to pick up or finish the remaining slices of a partly done plan, or points at a plan file to carry out."
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/implement-plan/SKILL.md:10, :18 and :21 send the reader to the skills `planning`, `coding`, `second-opinion` and `review-loop`. None of them exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills. The "if installed" hedge keeps this from being wrong, but in this repo the step 4 review instruction always falls through to its second half.
  - Suggested: Drop the four names or replace them with skills that ship here. For line 21 say what to do directly, e.g. "Review the diff against the slice's acceptance criteria with a reviewer subagent; for a non-trivial diff repeat until the reviewer has no blocking finding." For line 10 name the boundary without a skill name, plus the real sibling: "Not for writing or revising the plan, a single bounded edit, review-only passes, or filing the slices as issues (`issue-breakdown`)."
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/implement-plan/SKILL.md:16-18 names Claude Code tools: AskUserQuestion, TaskCreate, Agent with `isolation: "worktree"`, and "a Workflow script". The pi tool list in this environment has ask_user, Agent and SubagentWorkflow and no TaskCreate. I could not verify whether pi's Agent tool accepts `isolation: "worktree"`. In the value runs Haiku repeated "each in its own worktree" without any way to check it.
  - Suggested: Describe the action and give the pi name where one exists: "ask the user (ask_user)", "track one task per slice in the todo list if there is one", "each in its own git worktree (Agent with worktree isolation where the tool offers it, otherwise `git worktree add`)". Verify the isolation parameter against the pi-subagents docs before keeping it.
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/implement-plan/SKILL.md:18 ends with "a Workflow script can fan out the parallel slices instead" without saying which. packages/agents/skills/subagent-workflows ships a workflow named plan-slice-implement for the same job, and neither skill points at the other. No routing collision showed up in the evals (subagent-workflows was never read on these prompts).

- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/implement-plan/SKILL.md:18 is one paragraph of about 170 words holding seven separate rules (parallel by write surface, land in plan order, rebase only finished branches, regenerate lockfiles, commit the plan before spawning, what to do when commits are not approved, the implementer brief, the workflow opt-in). Haiku with the skill still answered the tested rules correctly, so this is readability, not a measured failure. The 'rebase only finished branches' rule was not tested with the skill actually read.

Final run: with 1.00 (1.00, 1.00, 1.00), without 0.39 (0.50, 0.33, 0.33). Bare Haiku consistently answers ONE-BY-ONE, NEXT and UNCHANGED, and usually STOP after two attempts. Question-style prompts ("give me the exact jj command for each step") were read 0/9 with the skill loaded alone; Haiku answered from memory.

Use whenever a repository has a .jj directory or the user mentions jj, Jujutsu, change IDs, bookmarks or the operation log, including when only answering a jj question or writing a jj script and before running any jj command, because flags and subcommands changed between releases. In a jj repo use it instead of git commands." With --all-skills on Haiku at 3 runs: recover-abandoned 3/3, resolve-conflict 3/3, both new positive routing cases 3/3, the git-reflog negative still quiet 3/3. Loaded alone, two of the three question-style prompts were read 3/3 each; the conflict-marker one stayed at 0/3.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** Three read-only value ideas, none discriminates on Haiku at 3 runs (with / without): (1) exact no-terminal commands for split -m, squash --use-destination-message, revert and duplicate with a destination: 1.00 / 0.90; (2) reading the diff-style conflict markers of references/conflicts.md:21 where the diff removes a line the snapshot keeps: 1.00 / 1.00; (3) the ask-before list of SKILL.md:52 as a RUN/ASK table: 0.85 / 0.85, and 1.00 / 0.97 after a neutral rewording. In those with-arms the skill was never opened, but with the rewritten description it was read and scored 1.00, 1.00 (unread) and 0.90, so reading it does not help either. For Haiku the skill changes nothing on knowledge questions.

Measure it with `--scaffold --allow-tools Bash,Write,Edit` as packages/jj/README.md:22 describes; the earlier commit reports set-aside-work at 1.00 vs 0.50, on a different model.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/jj/skills/jj/SKILL.md:58 says of `jj undo` and `jj op restore`: "Both are recorded as new operations, so they can be undone too." On jj 0.47.1 a second `jj undo` does not undo the first; `jj help undo` says repeated use "will restore increasingly older operations" and names `jj redo` as the reverse. In a scratch repo two `jj undo` calls removed two commits. An agent following this line to take back an undo loses one more operation.
  - Suggested: Rewrite line 58: "`jj undo` reverts the last operation; running it again goes one operation further back, and `jj redo` steps forward again. For a specific older point use `jj op restore <op-id>` (ask first), which returns the whole repo to that operation."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/jj/skills/jj/references/git-interop.md:17-18 is the only place that gives `jj duplicate <c> -o @` and `jj revert -r <c> -o @`.   - Suggested: Add two rows to the Everyday workflow table in SKILL.md: "Revert a change | `jj revert -r <rev> -o @` (destination is required)" and "Copy a change (cherry-pick) | `jj duplicate <rev> -o @`".
- **medium, instructions.** packages/jj/skills/jj/SKILL.md:26 states "The environment sets `JJ_EDITOR=false`" and references/git-interop.md:23 mentions "what the guard warns about". Both come from the extension (packages/jj/src/index.ts:13), not the skill. The eval runner uses --no-extensions and the skill can be installed alone; there a forgotten -m opens the default editor and hangs instead of failing fast.
  - Suggested: Make it conditional: "With the pi-jj extension loaded, `JJ_EDITOR=false` is set and a forgotten `-m` fails fast. Otherwise prefix the command with `JJ_EDITOR=false`." In git-interop.md:23 replace "what the guard warns about" with "what muddles history (see SKILL.md, Git in a jj repo)".
- **low, accuracy.** packages/jj/skills/jj/SKILL.md:8 says "Written for jj 0.30 or newer", but lines 42 and 50 and git-interop.md:15,17,18 use `-o` (`--onto`). On 0.47.1 `-d/--destination` is listed as the alias; I believe `-o` arrived several releases after 0.30 but could not verify the exact version from the installed binary.
  - Suggested: Either raise the stated minimum to the release that added `--onto`, or add after line 42: "on older jj use `-d` instead of `-o`".
- **low, instructions.** packages/jj/skills/jj/SKILL.md:35 lists `jj new -m "msg"` for "Finish this change, start the next". The message goes on the new empty change, not on the finished one, so read as a way to name the finished work it leaves that work undescribed.
  - Suggested: Change the row to: "Start the next change | `jj new` (`-m` describes the new change, not the one you leave)".
- **low, instructions.** packages/jj/skills/jj/SKILL.md:52 requires asking before `jj op restore`, while line 58 gives it as the normal recovery step with no mention of asking.
  - Suggested: Add "(ask first, see above)" to the `jj op restore` clause in line 58, as in the rewrite suggested for that line.

### lens-review

lens-review is a manual command (`disable-model-invocation: true`), so pi never lists it to the model: natural-language routing is impossible by design, and the only meaningful routing checks are negatives. Invoked as `/skill:lens-review`, it helps Haiku a lot: both new value cases score 1.00 with the skill and 0.00 without, at 3 runs. The suite now has 5 cases, all loading and passing; the two pre-existing negatives were kept unchanged, although they pass trivially because the skill is hidden.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (lens-review-quiet-devils 1.00, lens-review-quiet-format 1.00, route-negative-plain-plan-review 1.00); all three are negatives. No positive routing case exists because the skill is manual-only and hidden from the model; failing: none.

**Value cases:**

- `value-duplicate-roles-collapse`: 1.00 with, 0.00 without
- `value-split-returns-question`: 1.00 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/lens-review/SKILL.md:3-4. The skill is manual-only, so a user who asks in plain words never gets it, even though SKILL.md:33 says "Run only when the user asks". pi drops skills with this flag from the prompt (pi-coding-agent dist/core/skills.js:279). Two fair triggers run against the real skill, loaded alone on Haiku, scored 0/3 and 0/3 (explicit: "look at this plan from a few different angles and tell me where they disagree"; implicit: three stakeholders disagree, "what's the one thing I'd need to find out to settle it"). The description also carries no trigger phrases: with only the flag removed in a /tmp copy, explicit scored 3/3 and implicit 1/3.
  - Suggested: If manual-only is intended, change nothing; the description is fine for a command list. If a plain-language ask should reach it, remove the flag and use: "Reviews one artifact (a claim, plan or file) through 2 to 5 independent lenses, one per failure mode such as correctness, security or cost, and returns where they agree, where they disagree and the one question that resolves the disagreement. Use only when the user asks for several angles, perspectives or lenses on one artifact, or asks whether differing views of it really conflict, as in "look at this from a few angles", "where do these views disagree" or "what one question settles this". Not for a single adversarial critique (devils-advocate) or an ordinary one-pass review." Tested on Haiku at 3 runs with the flag removed: loaded alone, explicit 3/3 and implicit 3/3; with all 173 skills, explicit 3/3 and implicit 0/3 (the skill was never opened); all three negatives stayed at 1.00 with all skills.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/lens-review/SKILL.md:18. Step 2 says the lens count "lands between 2 and 5" but does not say what to do when the artifact has one distinct failure mode, or more than five. Not exercised by an eval; found by reading.
  - Suggested: Add one sentence, e.g. "If only one failure mode exists, say so and give a single read instead of a lens review; if more than five, keep the five whose failure would cost most and name the ones dropped."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/lens-review/SKILL.md:21 says of the resolving question "That question is the output", while SKILL.md:37 requires the result to show which lenses agreed, which disagreed and the question. In the runs Haiku followed line 37 (a verdict table plus the question), so nothing broke, but the two lines disagree on what is returned.
  - Suggested: Reword line 21 to "That question is the headline of the output, placed after the per-lens verdicts."

**Eval changes**

- left-failing: `lens-review-quiet-devils`. Not failing and not edited; no other action value fits. Scores 1.00 at 3 runs with all skills, but passes trivially: the skill is hidden from the model, so it cannot fire on any prompt. Kept as is. The prompt is not duplicated in any sibling's evals.
- left-failing: `lens-review-quiet-format`. Not failing and not edited; no other action value fits. Scores 1.00 at 3 runs with all skills, and passes trivially for the same reason. Kept as is.
- added: `route-negative-plain-plan-review`. Near-miss negative: an ordinary "review this plan before I send it" that never asks for several lenses must not load lens-review (max: 0). 1.00 at 3 runs with all skills, and 1.00 against the tested model-invocable description rewrite with all skills. Unlike the two older negatives it sits in the skill's own territory, so it would catch the skill turning greedy if the manual flag is ever removed.
- added: `value-duplicate-roles-collapse`. Invoked with `/skill:lens-review` and six requested reviewers (three security titles, three performance titles). Tests SKILL.md:18 and :28: one lens per failure mode, 2 to 5 in total. A regex on the final line `VERDICTS GIVEN: <n>` accepts 2 to 5. ### mcp-server-review

The skill's content is accurate where I could check it and clearly helps Haiku once opened, but the current description does not get it opened for protocol-expectation questions and only intermittently for a plain pre-release review when all skills compete. The evals now hold 4 cases (1 existing, 3 new): two routing cases pass 3/3, the original trigger stays at 1/3 under --all-skills, and the new value case is left failing (with 0.30 / without 0.37) because Haiku never opens the skill. With a tested description rewrite the same value case scores with 1.00 / without 0.37, and all three routing cases pass 3/3.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (route-implicit-pre-tag-checks 3/3, route-negative-third-party-server 3/3); failing: trigger-review-1 at 1/3. With the tested description rewrite: 3/3 cases pass.

**Value cases:**

- `value-release-qa-modern-era`: 0.30 with, 0.37 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/mcp-server-review/SKILL.md:3. The description only promises a review process, so Haiku does not open the skill when a user doing release QA asks what a conforming server should answer. In value-release-qa-modern-era, with the skill loaded alone, 0 of 6 with-arm runs across two invocations read SKILL.md, and they answered from older revisions (Q1 '200 -32601', Q4 exit '0', Q5 'YES'); with 0.43 then 0.30 against without 0.43 then 0.37. The existing trigger-review-1 was read in 1/3 runs under --all-skills in both invocations (3/3 with the skill alone): Haiku spent its turns hunting for the nonexistent src/acme_mcp/ and one run timed out at 300s.
  - Suggested: Tested replacement: "Reviews an MCP server or client you own before release, in two passes, a static security review of the source (exposure, auth, sessions, rate limits, schemas, code-execution vectors, OWASP MCP Top 10) and a release QA pass over one real local protocol session. Holds the expected protocol answers for revision 2026-07-28 (HTTP status and JSON-RPC error codes, required headers, no initialize handshake, Inspector CLI exit codes), which differ from earlier revisions, and the release verdict rules. Use when asked to review, audit, release-check or QA MCP server or client code, or what a conforming server should answer to a protocol check, even when no code is at hand." Scores with this text in a copy of the skill, Haiku at 3 runs: value case with 1.00 / without 0.37 (skill alone) and 1.00 with --all-skills; routing with --all-skills 3/3 on trigger-review-1, route-implicit-pre-tag-checks and the negative route-negative-third-party-server. One invocation each, so the trigger-review-1 gain (1/3 to 3/3) is indicative only.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/mcp-server-review/SKILL.md:8 sends generic code security review to a skill named `security-review`. No skill of that name exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills. The nearest is `security-scan`, which is a manual command (disable-model-invocation: true). `mcp-server` and `mcp-server-audit` on the same line do exist.
  - Suggested: Drop the `security-review` name or replace it: "...or generic code security review of non-MCP code (`security-scan`, a manual command, if installed)."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/mcp-server-review/references/release-qa.md:118-122. The verdict rules have a hole. FAIL lists four conditions, PASS WITH CAVEATS covers drift 'that doesn't misrepresent a dangerous capability', and PASS is 'everything else'. Drift that does misrepresent a dangerous capability (for example a destructive tool missing from the README, or a wrong read-only annotation) matches neither FAIL nor CAVEATS and so lands in PASS. Found by reading; not exercised by an eval.
  - Suggested: Add to the FAIL line: "..., or documentation, metadata or annotations misrepresent a dangerous capability (an undocumented mutation tool, a destructive tool annotated read-only)". Change PASS to "no findings".
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/mcp-server-review/references/security.md:25 says a published port makes the server network-exposed 'even if the process binds 127.0.0.1 inside the container'. A process bound to the container's loopback is not reachable through a published port, since Docker forwards to the container's own interface address. The usual symptom is connection refused. This is from my knowledge of Docker networking and was not checked against documentation in this session.
  - Suggested: Reword to: "Network-exposed when the process binds 0.0.0.0 or the container interface. A process bound to 127.0.0.1 inside the container is not reachable through the published port; record that as a deployment defect and mark exposure NEEDS INVESTIGATION."
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/mcp-server-review/references/security.md:82 links the SDK tier list as https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/sdk, while the Sources list at security.md:182 gives https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/sdk for the same page. I did not fetch either URL.
  - Suggested: Use one URL in both places after checking which one resolves.

With all skills loaded (3 runs each): mise-agent-shell 0.33, mise-tool-pin 0.00, route-implicit-untrusted-clone 0.00. With mise loaded alone, agent-shell and tool-pin reach 1.00, but untrusted-clone stays at 0.00 and the value case scores 0.33 with = 0.33 without because the skill was read in 0/3 runs. The memory answers were wrong on the points the skill covers: `.nvmrc` is read by default, and `mise run` refuses an untrusted config.
  - Suggested: Replace the description with the following text. Tested on Haiku at 3 runs: all-skills routing agent-shell 1.00, tool-pin 1.00, untrusted-clone 0.67, both negatives 1.00; value case 1.00 with / 0.33 without.

'Configures, debugs and explains mise (mise-en-place): pinned tool versions, project env vars, tasks and config trust. Read it before answering any question about how mise behaves, even a quick factual one, because defaults changed across releases (which version files are read, what needs mise trust, which backends are deprecated) and answers from memory are often out of date. Use when a task or question involves mise.toml, .mise.toml, mise.local.toml or .tool-versions, a mise command (use, install, exec, run, trust, env, tasks, activate), a "mise ERROR" message, or "command not found" for a tool mise should provide, including in scripts, CI and non-interactive shells. Not for devenv.nix or other Nix shells, devcontainers, or project dependency files such as package.json, pyproject.toml and uv.lock.'
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/mise/SKILL.md:3 and :8. The exclusions point to "Nix environments (devenv)" and "language package-manager skills". None of the four skills directories in this repo has a devenv, nix, npm, uv or cargo skill. The real neighbour for tool-version pinning, devcontainer, is not mentioned.
  - Suggested: Name the exclusions by artefact rather than by skill ("Not for devenv.nix or other Nix shells, devcontainers, or project dependency files such as package.json, pyproject.toml and uv.lock"), as in the tested description above. Drop "(language package-manager skills)".
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/mise/SKILL.md:41. "`mise run`, `mise install` and `mise exec` trust the active config for you" is stated without its conditions. The mise docs (security.html "Implicit trust", paranoid.html) say this holds in normal mode outside CI, that it also applies to `mise watch`, task shorthand and `mise daemons start/restart/register`, that it covers every non-global config loaded including parent directories, and that paranoid mode turns it off. The parent-directory part matters for the warning this line is making.
  - Suggested: Rewrite the sentence as: "Outside paranoid mode, `mise run` (and task shorthand like `mise build`), `mise install`, `mise exec` and `mise watch` record trust for every non-global config they load, parent directories included, so read an unfamiliar `mise.toml` before running any of them."

### play-publishing

The skill body is sound and mostly accurate, but on Haiku with all skills loaded its description routes only 3 of 5 cases: the version-code error and the implicit bad-rollout prompt are never opened (0/3 each, 2/3 with the skill alone). A tested description rewrite takes both to 3/3 without breaking the negatives. Evals now have 7 cases (2 routing and 1 value added, 1 fixed); the value case discriminates (0.89 with, 0.39 without), though most of that lift comes from the description line "Never publishes without an explicit yes", because SKILL.md was opened in only 1 of 6 with-skill runs. The pre-existing outcome case gpp-internal-track was not run and is unchanged: it needs --scaffold and Write/Edit, which were off limits here.

**Routing:** 3/5 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (trigger-play-2, not-play-testflight, route-negative-godot-android-aab); failing: trigger-play-1 0/3, route-implicit-bad-release-spreading 0/3 (each 2/3 with the skill alone, 3/3 with the tested description rewrite, where all 5 pass)

**Value cases:**

- `value-confirm-before-publishing`: 0.89 with, 0.39 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:3. With --all-skills on Haiku, trigger-play-1 (the "Version code N has already been used" upload error, which the description quotes) and route-implicit-bad-release-spreading both score 0/3. With the skill loaded alone they score 2/3 each, so the skill is not losing to a sibling; it is never opened. In the logs Haiku looks for app/build.gradle.kts, finds nothing and answers from memory, or makes no tool call at all. The description also says nothing about stopping a release that is already reaching users unless the user says "staged rollouts".
  - Suggested: Tested replacement (copy of the skill with only the description changed, all 172 siblings symlinked, --all-skills, Haiku, 3 runs): trigger-play-1 3/3, route-implicit-bad-release-spreading 3/3, trigger-play-2 3/3, not-play-testflight 3/3, route-negative-godot-android-aab 3/3. Text: 'Google Play release path for an Android app: uploads, tracks, staged rollouts and signing keys. Read this before answering any question about a Play upload error ("Version code N has already been used", "signed with the wrong key"), a lost upload key, getting an AAB to the internal track from CI, stopping, halting or widening the rollout of a release that is already reaching users, or the target API deadline, even when the workspace has no project files. Covers upload key versus Play App Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, fastlane supply, mapping upload, store listing and data safety drafts. Never publishes without an explicit yes.'
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:32 and :42, references/tracks-and-rollouts.md:20. In value-confirm-before-publishing with the skill loaded alone, Haiku opened SKILL.md in only 1 of 6 runs. The other five answered from the description. The two wrong answers both came from unread runs: one ran the 10% to 25% step on yesterday's blanket approval, one ran the draft upload unasked. The rule that each rollout step needs its own yes even under a pre-approved plan sits only in the reference file; SKILL.md:42 says "A yes covers that action only", which does not settle a plan approved in advance.
  - Suggested: Adopt the description rewrite above (with it, the same case scored 3/3 on the with arm under --all-skills, and SKILL.md was read in 2 of 3 runs). Also extend SKILL.md:42 to: "A yes covers that one action only. A plan approved in advance (\"10%, then 25, 50, 100 if vitals are fine\") is not a yes for each step: confirm every rollout change when it is due. A draft upload needs a yes too."
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:31 makes Gradle Play Publisher the default for new setups. The plugin's README (github.com/Triple-T/gradle-play-publisher, master, fetched during this review) says "Project status: maintenance mode. Issues are ignored, but pull requests are not." The skill does not mention this.
  - Suggested: Either keep the default and add the caveat ("GPP is in maintenance mode; say so and offer fastlane supply when the team wants an actively supported tool"), or change the no-preference default to fastlane supply.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/references/gradle-play-publisher.md:34 states that with commit.set(false) "the edit is validated by Play but not applied", and SKILL.md:32 uses a successful run of it as the done criterion. The GPP README documents `commit` only under "Combining artifacts into a single release" (uncommitted changes that a later flavor commits) and says nothing about validation. I could not verify the validation claim; it would need a check against the plugin source.
  - Suggested: Verify against the GPP source for the pinned version. If an uncommitted edit is not sent to Play's validate endpoint, reword to "commit.set(false) uploads into an edit that is never committed; this proves credentials and upload work but is not a Play validation" and stop equating it with fastlane validate_only in SKILL.md:32.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:46. In run r1 of trigger-play-2 (with-0), Haiku read SKILL.md and references/gradle-play-publisher.md and still advised "Once you trust the pipeline, switch to ReleaseStatus.COMPLETED so each tag reaches internal testers immediately". The default says new setups use draft releases but not whether the skill may propose leaving draft. Seen in 1 of 3 runs.
  - Suggested: Add to SKILL.md:46: "Do not propose switching CI to completed releases on your own; if the user asks for it, treat the change as a confirmed step and say that every tag will then reach testers without a manual rollout."
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/references/gradle-play-publisher.md:27 names the task `bootstrapReleasePlayResources` and calls it read-only. The old name is from GPP 2.x; the line does tell the reader to check the task list.

- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/references/tracks-and-rollouts.md:22 says "A rollout cannot be reduced". Sources found disagree: a Play CLI guide says the API rejects a lower percentage, while a Stack Overflow answer says the Console UI allows lowering it (without affecting users who already updated). I did not manage to confirm this against Play Console Help. Haiku answers HALT with or without the skill, so the line changes nothing measurable.
  - Suggested: Check Play Console Help answer 6346149 and reword to what holds either way: "Lowering the percentage does not take the release back from users who already have it; to stop exposure, halt, then ship a fixed build with a higher versionCode."
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:57 says the rule and dates "with their fetch date" are in references/target-api.md, but target-api.md:3-5 holds no level, date or fetch date and tells the reader to fetch them. SKILL.md:47 promises "Steps and commands" in references/tracks-and-rollouts.md, which contains no commands.
  - Suggested: SKILL.md:57: "references/target-api.md says where to fetch the current level and deadline; it holds no dates." SKILL.md:47: change "Steps and commands" to "Steps", or add the GPP and fastlane rollout commands to tracks-and-rollouts.md.
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/play-publishing/SKILL.md:10 and :53, references/data-safety.md:3 send work to `android-skills:play-policy-insights`, `android-skills:play-billing-library-version-upgrade` and `android-skills:engage-sdk-integration`. None exists in the four skills directories of this repo. SKILL.md:10 marks them as a third-party plugin "if installed"; SKILL.md:53 and data-safety.md:3 do not.
  - Suggested: Keep the names only in SKILL.md:10 with the "if installed" qualifier. At SKILL.md:53 and data-safety.md:3 say "a policy audit is out of scope" and say what to tell the user when that plugin is absent.

### postmortem

The skill had no evals; it now has 5 cases (2 routing positives, 1 near-miss negative, 2 value cases) under packages/skills/evals/postmortem/, all loading without errors. On Haiku the skill clearly helps when it is opened (final run: 1.00 vs 0.40 and 0.92 vs 0.38), but opening is unreliable: with all skills loaded the implicit draft-review trigger never routes (0/3), and even loaded alone Haiku opened SKILL.md in only 15 of 18 with-arm value runs (one run of three opened it in 3/6 and scored 0.60 / 0.61). The runbook half of the skill showed no measurable value because the reference file holding it was never read. Final numbers come from the last run after the cases stopped changing (routing r1, value r4); only a case description line was edited afterwards.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-implicit-draft-blames-engineer (0/3; 2/3 with the skill alone; 3/3 with the tested description rewrite)

**Value cases:**

- `value-detect-and-resolve-durations`: 1.00 with, 0.40 without
- `value-draft-line-review`: 0.92 with, 0.38 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/postmortem/SKILL.md:3. A pasted incident summary that blames an engineer, says 'Cause: human error' and has vague next steps, with the request 'look it over before it goes to the VP', is never routed with all skills loaded on Haiku (route-implicit-draft-blames-engineer 0/3, no skill opened at all; 2/3 with the skill loaded alone, so it is 'never opened', not 'loses to a sibling'). The description only says 'a draft review' and never names the document as an RCA or incident report.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite: 'Writes or reviews a blameless postmortem after an outage or significant degradation, with a gap-flagged UTC timeline, 5 Whys to a fixable system gap, impact, detection gap, and owned, dated actions. Use when an incident is resolved and needs its write-up (postmortem, RCA, incident report), when a draft or pasted incident summary needs checking before it is sent, especially one that blames a person or says "human error", or when a runbook needs writing or fixing. Not for a live incident (aws-cloudwatch).' Scored 3/3 on all three routing cases with --all-skills on Haiku (implicit case 0/3 -> 3/3, negative stayed quiet). Value cases with this text, skill alone: draft-line-review 1.00 vs 0.49, durations 0.60 vs 0.40 (SKILL.md opened in only 1/3 runs there, so it does not cure the open-rate flakiness). A longer first attempt that led with 'RCA or incident report ... and writes or fixes on-call runbooks' scored only 2/3 on the implicit case and opened the skill in 2/6 value runs; do not use that one.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/postmortem/SKILL.md:3 says 'Not for a live incident (use incident response or aws-cloudwatch)' and :10 repeats 'live incident response'. No incident-response skill exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills; only aws-cloudwatch does. (adr-writing at :10 is the user's own skill and is hedged with 'if installed', which is fine.)

- **medium, instructions.** Runbook guidance exists only in packages/skills/skills/postmortem/references/templates.md:20-30, reached through a single pointer on SKILL.md:56; the workflow (SKILL.md:14-22) has no runbook branch. In a runbook-review case (six properties judged OK/FIX, dropped from the suite) Haiku opened SKILL.md in 0/3 runs with the skill loaded alone and in 1/3 with a runbook-forward description, and never opened templates.md. The rule 'mitigate before diagnosing' (templates.md:26) was missed in 6/6 with-skill runs, including the run that read SKILL.md.
  - Suggested: Either add an early branch in SKILL.md ('If the task is to write or fix a runbook, read references/templates.md first and follow its list; the rest of this workflow does not apply') and move the two most non-obvious runbook rules (safe first action before diagnosis; owner plus last-reviewed date) into SKILL.md, or split runbooks into their own skill with its own description.

### pr-comments

The skill helps Haiku once it is loaded (with/without 0.90/0.29 on Codeberg, 0.86/0.38 on GitHub), but it is never found by routing: `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps it out of the model's skill list, so both positive triggers score 0/3. Both pre-existing value cases were broken under this runner and were rewritten on the same points; three routing cases were added, and all 5 cases load with 0 errors. Routing figures are from the single all-skills run (those cases were not changed afterwards); value figures are from the re-run after the last grader edit.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-github-review-threads (0/3), route-implicit-approval-blocked (0/3). Both are also 0/3 with the skill loaded alone, and 3/3 once disable-model-invocation is removed.

**Value cases:**

- `value-pr-comments-codeberg-invoked`: 0.90 with, 0.29 without
- `value-pr-comments-github-invoked`: 0.86 with, 0.38 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/pr-comments/SKILL.md:4 sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, so pi never lists the skill. Both fair triggers (route-github-review-threads, route-implicit-approval-blocked) score 0/3 with all skills loaded and 0/3 with the skill loaded alone; with all skills loaded Haiku read gh-triage instead. The flag is the whole cause: a copy with only that line removed and the description unchanged scored 3/3 on both positives and 3/3 on the negative with all skills loaded. SKILL.md:3 also has no 'Use when' clause, and says 'Invoke as /pr-comments', which in pi is `/skill:pr-comments`.
  - Suggested: If the skill should be found automatically, delete SKILL.md:4. Optionally also use this description (tested together with the flag removed, all skills loaded, Haiku: 3/3 on both positives and the negative, the same score as the flag-only change): "Works through the review feedback already left on an open pull request, on GitHub (gh) or on Forgejo and Codeberg (fj): pulls the unresolved review threads and review summaries into context, triages each as fix, push back or clarify, then fixes only the rows the user picks and drafts replies. Never posts, resolves or pushes. Use when reviewers, Copilot or CodeRabbit commented on a PR, changes were requested, or approval is blocked on feedback. Not for opening a PR (`gh-pr`, `forgejo-pr`) or triaging a backlog of issues and incoming PRs (`gh-triage`)." If manual-only is intended, keep the flag, change 'Invoke as' to `/skill:pr-comments`, and accept that the two routing positives stay failing.
- **medium, overlap.** pr-comments covers Forgejo and Codeberg itself (SKILL.md:3, :34, references/forgejo.md), while the sibling forgejo-pr-comments does the same job with a near-identical body and a references/triage.md that differs in 4 lines. forgejo-pr-comments' description sends only github.com PRs to pr-comments, and forgejo-pr/SKILL.md:8 points at `/pr-comments` for review feedback. Both are manual-only today, so nothing collides yet; with both enabled, a Codeberg review-feedback prompt matches both.

Haiku without the skill declined alice's comment in 9 of 12 runs under its own wording, so the skill did not improve this judgment.

It did not recur in the final run (6/6 `fix`).
