### pre-commit

The skill's content checks out against the current prek docs, but its description does not get it opened when a hook has rejected a commit: on Haiku the repair trigger scores 0/3 with all skills loaded, and a deadline-pressure prompt never opens the skill even when it is the only one loaded, so Haiku recommends `SKIP=mypy git commit`. A tested description rewrite fixes this (repair routing 0.00 -> 1.00 with all skills; value case 0.17 -> 1.00 with the skill, 0.00 without). The evals now hold 5 cases (4 routing, 1 value), all loading cleanly; three are left failing against the current description on purpose.

**Routing:** 2/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: hook-repair-routing (0.00), pre-commit-routing (0.00). Passing: route-implicit-catch-before-commit (1.00), route-negative-ci-lint-job (1.00). Loaded alone: 3/4 pass, hook-repair-routing 0.33. With the tested description rewrite and all skills: 3/4 pass, hook-repair-routing 1.00, pre-commit-routing 0.67.

**Value cases:**

- `value-no-bypass-under-deadline`: 0.17 with, 0.17 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/pre-commit/SKILL.md:3 - the description leads with setup and only mentions repair as 'repairs commit-time hooks' and a trailing 'when a commit or `prek run` fails on a hook'. Haiku does not open the skill for a rejected commit. With all skills loaded: hook-repair-routing 0/3 and pre-commit-routing 0/3 in the final run (0/3 and 1/3 in the baseline run). Loaded alone: hook-repair-routing 2/3 then 1/3, pre-commit-routing 3/3. No sibling skill was read instead; Haiku looks for the files, finds none and answers from memory. In value-no-bypass-under-deadline the skill, loaded alone, was opened in 0/3 runs and Haiku recommended `SKIP=mypy git commit`, the exact thing SKILL.md:14 forbids.
  - Suggested: Replace the description with: "Gets a commit through after a commit-time hook rejected it, and sets up, updates and runs those hooks with prek (preferred) or pre-commit, plus Husky and lint-staged for Node repos. Read this first whenever a commit, `prek run` or `pre-commit run` failed on a hook (ruff, mypy, eslint, end-of-file-fixer, gitleaks) or the user asks how to get a blocked commit in, before suggesting `--no-verify` or `SKIP=`. Also use when adding a .pre-commit-config.yaml, running hooks across a repo, bumping hook revs or wiring hooks into CI." Tested on Haiku at 3 runs against a copy in /tmp/skill-evals/pre-commit/alt. With all skills: hook-repair-routing 1.00 (was 0.00), pre-commit-routing 0.67 (was 0.00-0.33), route-implicit-catch-before-commit 1.00, negative 1.00. Alone: hook-repair-routing 1.00. Value case: 1.00 with / 0.00 without (current description: 0.17 / 0.17).
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/pre-commit/SKILL.md:14 - 'Never suggest or run `git commit --no-verify`, `SKIP=<id>`...' is followed by 'If the user explicitly wants a hook skipped, tell them the command to run themselves.' The line does not say what counts as explicit. A user under time pressure asking 'what do I do right now to get this commit in' is the common case, and the bare model reads it as a request to skip. When Haiku did read the skill it held the line (3/3 in each of two runs), so the rule works; the boundary is just unstated.
  - Suggested: Add one sentence after the rule: "Time pressure or 'just get it in' is not a request to skip; only a direct request to skip or bypass the hook is. In that case give the command once, say what it skips, and don't run it."
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/pre-commit/SKILL.md:14 names a `check-bypass-guard` plugin. Nothing with that name exists anywhere in this repo (the only match is this line), and unlike the `devenv` and `gh-actions` mentions at SKILL.md:8 it has no pointer to where it comes from.
  - Suggested: Drop the sentence, or say where the plugin lives, e.g. "(the `check-bypass-guard` plugin from <package>, if installed, blocks those git forms)".
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/pre-commit/SKILL.md:8 and references/setup.md:95 point to `devenv` and `gh-actions` skills. Neither exists in the four skills directories of this repo (only `forgejo-actions` does, for the CI side). Both mentions are hedged with 'if installed', so they are not broken, but a Forgejo or Codeberg repo is sent to a skill that is not there.
  - Suggested: In SKILL.md:8 and setup.md:95 name the skill that does exist as well: "authoring CI workflows (`forgejo-actions`, or `gh-actions` if installed)".
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/pre-commit/SKILL.md:20 says 'prek follows a repo-local `core.hooksPath`'. The prek CLI reference (prek.j178.dev/reference/cli, `prek install`) adds that prek refuses to install when `core.hooksPath` points outside the repository unless `--force` or `--git-dir` is given; the skill omits that case. Everything else I checked against the prek docs is correct: `prek update` with `--dry-run`, `--freeze`, `--cooldown-days`, `--check`; `prek install --prepare-hooks`; `prek util yaml-to-toml`; shims following `--hook-type` or `default_install_hook_types` and not a hook's `stages`. I did not verify the pinned revs in references/setup.md:27 and :34 or the pre-commit.ci claims at setup.md:98.
  - Suggested: Extend SKILL.md:20: "prek follows a repo-local or worktree-local `core.hooksPath` and refuses one that points outside the repo unless `-f` is passed; pre-commit refuses to install while it is set at all."
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Two other value ideas did not discriminate on Haiku and were dropped. (1) prek-specific commands from references/setup.md:47, :77-80 and :97: the bare model already answers `--freeze --cooldown-days 7`, `--check` and `prek util yaml-to-toml` (it writes `prek auto-update` instead of `prek update`, which I could not show to be wrong; the docs list `prek autoupdate` as a hidden alias). (2) Repair decisions from SKILL.md:45 and :53 (re-stage only previously staged files; ask before suppressing a suspected false positive) and SKILL.md:20 (prek installs under a repo-local hooksPath): the bare model gets the first two right 3/3, and the third right 3/3 when asked per tool. For Haiku the measurable value is the never-bypass rule, not the command reference.
  - Suggested: No change required. If SKILL.md needs trimming, the command recap at SKILL.md:27-31 duplicates references/setup.md and is what the model already knows.

### prisma

The skill clearly helps Haiku once it is read (two value cases at 1.00/0.89 with vs 0.33/0.22 without), but Haiku does not open it under the current description: both fair positive triggers score 0/3 with all skills loaded, and one of them 0/3 even with the skill loaded alone. A tested description rewrite routes all three routing cases 3/3 with all skills loaded. The skill had no evals; there are now 5 (3 routing, 2 value), all loading cleanly, with the two positive routing cases left failing as a description problem. One factual error (findUnique and non-unique fields) was confirmed against the Prisma 7 docs.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run); failing: route-bulk-update-rows-back (0/3), route-implicit-transaction-closed (0/3); passing: route-negative-drizzle-migration (3/3). Skill loaded alone: 2/3 cases (bulk-update still 0/3). With the tested description rewrite and --all-skills: 3/3 cases, each 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-prisma-7-upgrade-defaults`: 0.89 with, 0.22 without
- `value-migration-and-write-traps`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/SKILL.md:3 - Haiku answers Prisma questions from memory without opening the skill. With --all-skills: route-bulk-update-rows-back 0/3 and route-implicit-transaction-closed 0/3 (two separate runs, no tool call at all in the event logs). With the skill loaded alone: bulk-update still 0/3, transaction-closed 3/3. In the unrouted bulk-update answer Haiku proposed select-then-update and never mentioned updateManyAndReturn, so the miss costs answer quality. The description opens with 'traps for TypeScript backends, such as ...', which reads as optional background rather than a trigger.
  - Suggested: Tested: 3/3 on both positive cases and 3/3 on the Drizzle negative with --all-skills on Haiku (171 sibling skills symlinked next to a copy with only the description changed). Text: 'Prisma ORM 6 and 7 behaviour that differs from what models remember. Use for any question or code that involves PrismaClient calls (prisma.model.findMany/updateMany/deleteMany, $transaction), schema.prisma, prisma migrate, a P2xxx error or a "Transaction already closed" error, or a Prisma 6 to 7 upgrade, even when no repo files exist and the answer seems obvious. Read it before answering - covers updateMany returning a count (updateManyAndReturn), undefined filters matching every row, interactive transaction timeouts, migrate dev resets, edited applied migrations, serverless connections and Prisma 7 driver adapters.'
- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/SKILL.md:64 says 'findUnique accepts only unique fields, so adding deletedAt: null there is a type error'. That has been false since Prisma 5.0 (extendedWhereUnique GA). The Prisma 7 client reference (prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/reference/prisma-client-reference, 'Filter on non-unique fields with UserWhereUniqueInput', fetched today) says UserWhereUniqueInput 'exposes all fields on the model, not just unique fields' and that you must give at least one unique field and may add any number of non-unique ones.
  - Suggested: Rewrite the section: 'A soft-deleted row still exists, so findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } }) returns it. Add the filter to the unique lookup, findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id, deletedAt: null } }) (non-unique fields are allowed beside a unique one since 5.0), and filter deletedAt: null explicitly in every other query (a Client Extension can centralize it; middleware is gone in 7).'
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/references/prisma-7.md:18 - the migrate diff row packs three removed flags into one cell with no word saying they are removed. In value-prisma-7-upgrade-defaults Q4 (does 'migrate diff --from-url ...' still work), Haiku with the skill read the reference and still answered YES in 3 of 9 with-arm runs across three invocations (1/3, 2/3, and 0/3); one log says 'the reference lists --to-schema-datasource as removed ... but it doesn't mention --from-url', although the cell does. The fact itself is right (confirmed in the v7 upgrade guide).
  - Suggested: Replace the row with an explicit mapping, e.g. '| migrate diff | --from-url, --to-url, --from-schema-datasource, --to-schema-datasource, --shadow-database-url | All five removed. --from-url and --from-schema-datasource become --from-config-datasource; --to-url and --to-schema-datasource become --to-config-datasource; the shadow URL moves to prisma.config.ts |'.
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/SKILL.md:8 points to skills 'db-schema-design' and 'postgres' ('if installed'). Neither exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills; the only database sibling in the repo is mysql.
  - Suggested: Drop the sentence, or point at skills that exist (mysql for MySQL-specific SQL and locking; deprecation-migration for expand/contract schema changes, which SKILL.md:44 also touches).
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/SKILL.md:15-16 hard-codes a dated snapshot ('on 2026-11-14 the npm latest tag was 8.0.0-rc.33') and 'currently points at the Prisma 8 CLI'. Checked today (2026-11-28) with npm view: latest is 8.0.0-rc.36, prev is 7.10.1, so the claim still holds but the number is already stale and the whole paragraph becomes wrong the day 8 goes stable.
  - Suggested: Keep the rule and the check command, drop the exact rc number: 'While the npm latest tag is a Prisma 8 pre-release (check with npm view prisma dist-tags; stable 7 is under prev), an unpinned npx prisma resolves the 8 CLI ...'.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/prisma/references/prisma-7.md:71 gives the pg adapter idle timeout default (idleTimeoutMillis 10 s vs v6 300 s). I could not confirm that row from the v7 upgrade guide, which only states the connection timeout change (0 vs 5 s); the 10 s value matches node-postgres' own default as far as I know. Not verified against Prisma docs.
  - Suggested: No change needed if the author verified it against node-postgres; otherwise cite the source next to the table.

**Eval changes**

- left-failing: `prisma/route-bulk-update-rows-back`. New positive routing case (explicit: Express handler using prisma.invoice.updateMany and .map on the result, filter built from req.body). 0/3 with --all-skills (two runs) and 0/3 with the skill loaded alone; 3/3 with the tested description rewrite. ### privacy-review

The skill's content works: every Haiku run that opened it scored 1.00 on both value cases, against 0.25 without it. With the current description Haiku almost never opens it (0/6 positive routing runs among all skills, 2/6 with-arm value runs when it is the only skill), so both value cases and both positive routing cases are left failing. A tested description rewrite takes routing to 3/3 on all three cases and both value cases to 1.00 with the skill; the evals now have 5 cases that load without errors and none needs a scaffold.

**Routing:** 1/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (current description); failing: route-user-data-map-before-launch (0/3), route-implicit-closed-account-still-emailed (0/3); passing: route-negative-threat-model-customer-table (3/3). With the tested description rewrite: 3/3 cases pass, each 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-fixture-pii-not-printed`: 0.50 with, 0.25 without
- `value-legal-wording-from-memory`: 0.50 with, 0.25 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/privacy-review/SKILL.md:3. Haiku does not open the skill on fair, in-scope prompts. With all skills loaded: route-user-data-map-before-launch 0/3 and route-implicit-closed-account-still-emailed 0/3 (repeated in the final run). With the skill loaded alone: data-map 3/3, implicit 1/3, so the data-map case loses to competition and the implicit case is mostly never opened. In the value cases the skill was the only one loaded and was read in 1/3 runs per case in the final run; each run that read it scored 1.00, each that did not scored 0.25. The description describes the review but does not say it applies to pasted code or to a bug-shaped question, and does not tell the model that a plain answer breaks the skill's rules.
  - Suggested: Replace the description with (tested): 'Read this first, before answering, for any question about what happens to user or customer data in code, including code pasted in the message: checking account deletion or closure, a deleted user who still gets email or shows in search, where personal data (PII) ends up and how long it is kept, a data map, GDPR, CCPA or DPIA review before a launch, production customer data in fixtures, or quoting GDPR articles against code. It carries rules a plain answer breaks: never reproduce the personal data found, cite articles without reciting their text, leave legal calls to the owner. Reviews minimization, retention, erasure, export, and PII in URLs and logs across database, logs, cache, search index, analytics, vendors and backups. Not for attacker threat models (threat-model).' Scores with this text on Haiku at 3 runs: all-skills routing 3/3 on both positives and 3/3 on the threat-model negative; value-legal-wording-from-memory with-arm 1.00 (skill alone, read 3/3; the without arm was not re-run with this text and scored 0.25 in every other run); value-fixture-pii-not-printed 1.00 with / 0.25 without. Two milder rewrites that only added trigger phrases without the 'Read this first' opening scored data-map 2/3 and implicit 0/3 among all skills, and one of them left the legal case unread 0/3, so the imperative opening and the 'rules a plain answer breaks' sentence are what moved it.
- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/privacy-review/SKILL.md:10 and references/checklist.md:46 name `app-auth` and `sentry-sdk`. Neither exists in the four skills directories of this repo (packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills, packages/memory/skills). Both mentions are hedged with 'if installed', so nothing breaks, but the boundary line points at skills this repo does not ship. `threat-model` does exist.
  - Suggested: Describe the excluded work instead of naming absent skills, e.g. 'Not for authorization bugs, PII scrubbing in an error reporter, or threat modeling (`threat-model`)', and at checklist.md:46 'Deeper authorization review is out of scope; flag it.'

**Eval changes**

- fixed: `value-fixture-pii-not-printed`. Replaced with a stronger case on the same point (was broken under this runner). It depended on scaffold.sh, which only runs with --scaffold; without it the workspace was empty and both arms scored 0.75 because the weight-3 not_contains grader passed vacuously on a 'no files found' answer. - **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/promql/SKILL.md:3. Haiku does not open the skill on fair prompts. With all skills loaded (--all-skills, 3 runs): promql-routing 0/3, route-implicit-holes-in-graph 0/3, and a config-side trigger I tried (alert rule hold time plus promtool test) 0/3; in every run Haiku opened no skill at all and answered from memory. With the skill loaded alone the three routing prompts do open it (3/3 each), so it is not losing to a sibling, it is drowned out. The value prompts (Slack receiver for alertmanager.yml, quantile on a bare-name histogram) were not opened even with the skill loaded alone (0/6 reads), although both are in scope.
  - Suggested: Replace the description with (tested): "Writes, fixes and explains PromQL queries and edits Prometheus and Alertmanager config, for any Prometheus-compatible backend (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, VictoriaMetrics). Use for every PromQL question, even a single query (rates, error ratios, histogram quantiles on classic or native histograms, holes or gaps in a graph) and for scrape configs, recording and alerting rules, Alertmanager routes and receivers, and promtool rule tests. Read it before answering from memory; it holds the rules on histogram types, rule naming and keeping credentials out of config and commands that are easy to get wrong. Not for adding metrics to application code (observability-instrumentation) or building Grafana dashboards (grafana-dashboards)." Tested on Haiku at 3 runs against a copy with only the description changed: all skills loaded, promql-routing 3/3, route-implicit-holes-in-graph 3/3, negative stays quiet 3/3; value-alertmanager-webhook-secret 1.00 with / 0.00 without. The same text without the final "Not for" sentence also routed the alert-rule trigger 3/3 but fired on the instrumentation negative in 1 of 3 runs, so keep that sentence.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/promql/SKILL.md:50 says to read references/server-config.md "before editing scrape configs, rules, or Alertmanager". Asked to write a new recording rule, Haiku read SKILL.md in 2 of 3 runs (current description, skill alone), did not open server-config.md in either, and wrote `sum by (job, route) (...)`; the `without` rule and the level:metric:operations naming live only in references/server-config.md:30 and :40. With the rewritten description (which mentions rule naming) all 3 runs read the reference and used `sum without (instance)`.
  - Suggested: Change line 50 to "Read `references/server-config.md` before writing or editing any scrape config, recording or alerting rule, promtool test, or Alertmanager route or receiver, including when the file is not in the session and you are writing the block from scratch." Optionally lift the one-line rule "aggregate with `without (...)`, name recording rules `level:metric:operations`, secrets go in `*_file` fields" into SKILL.md so it survives a skipped reference.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/promql/SKILL.md:26 says "a bare metric name is native". A bare name is also what a gauge or a summary looks like; without the skill Haiku read the same evidence as a gauge in all 3 runs. The skill also does not say that native histograms must be switched on: per the Prometheus native histogram spec (checked via the docs tool) they are stable from v3.8.0 but need `scrape_native_histograms: true` (feature flag `--enable-feature=native-histograms` before that), so a server without it never has the bare series.
  - Suggested: Reword to: "Check the histogram type first: `/api/v1/metadata?metric=<name>` says histogram, and a `_bucket` series means classic; a histogram with only the bare name is native (needs `scrape_native_histograms: true`, stable from Prometheus 3.8). A bare name with type gauge or summary is neither."
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/promql/references/investigations.md:33 gives `histogram_fraction(0, 0.5, x)`. On a raw native histogram series that is the share since process start, not over a window; the Prometheus histogram practices page (checked via the docs tool) uses `histogram_fraction(0, 0.3, sum by (job) (rate(x[5m])))`.
  - Suggested: Change the table cell to `histogram_fraction(0, 0.5, sum by (route) (rate(x[5m])))`.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/promql/SKILL.md:14 forbids a credential on a command line, but :16 offers "an environment variable" without saying how to use it; `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROM_TOKEN"` expands into the process arguments, which is exactly what :14 rules out. references/access.md:7-14 only shows the file form. Not measured by an eval.
  - Suggested: In line 16 say that an environment variable may hold the path or be read by the tool itself (for example `PROMQL_AUTH_CREDENTIALS`), and that a token must not be expanded into a curl argument; point to the `-H @file` form.

### sbt

The sbt skill routes reliably on Haiku (4/4 routing cases at 3 runs with all skills loaded) and measurably helps: both new value cases score 1.00 with the skill against 0.44 and 0.33 without. The pre-existing outcome case sbt2-commands was not run, because it needs --scaffold and Bash/Edit, which were off limits; I only loosened two of its regexes and checked them offline. The main skill problem is accuracy drift: it treats sbt 2 as one version, while the official 2.1 change summary changes the clean/test-cache behaviour the skill's gotchas rely on.

**Routing:** 4/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (trigger-sbt-1, trigger-sbt-2, trigger-sbt-implicit-skipped-suites, trigger-sbt-negative); failing: none. The implicit case scored 0.67 on its first run and 1.00 on the final one.

- `value-sbt2-migration-facts`: 1.00 with, 0.33 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/sbt/SKILL.md:61 ("A green test stays skipped after clean on sbt 2"), SKILL.md:53, references/sbt2.md:62 and references/troubleshooting.md:10 state the clean/test-cache behaviour for all of sbt 2. The official change summary (scala-sbt.org/2.x/docs/en/changes/sbt-2.0-change-summary.html, fetched during this review) says sbt 2.1.0 makes `clean` a cache invalidator for the next command, adds `sbt test --cache_test_result=false`, and adds `Test / test / cacheStores := Nil`. The official sbt reference page already shows `sbt.version=2.1.1`. The skill never mentions 2.1.
  - Suggested: Scope the claim to 2.0.x and add the 2.1 behaviour, e.g. SKILL.md:61: "On sbt 2.0.x a green test stays skipped after `clean`; use `testFull`. From 2.1.0 `clean` invalidates the cache for the next command, and `test --cache_test_result=false` or `Test / test / cacheStores := Nil` opt out of test caching." Apply the same split in sbt2.md:58-63 and troubleshooting.md:10, and make Orient step 1 distinguish 2.0.x from 2.1+.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/sbt/references/sbt2.md:55, :67 and :68 mark `-Dsbt.ci=true`, the `target/out/jvm/scala-<ver>/<subproject>/` layout and the `~/.config/sbt/2` global base as **observed**, but all three are on the official pages (sbt reference: `-Dsbt.ci=true` suppresses supershell and colour; global base is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sbt/2` or `$HOME/.config/sbt/2`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/sbt/2` on Windows; change summary: `target` defaults to `target/out/jvm/scala-<ver>/<subproject>/`). In run r6-value-final (value-sbt2-migration-facts, with-1) Haiku hedged a correct answer as "based on observed runs rather than official docs" because of these labels.
  - Suggested: Relabel those three items as Official and give the per-OS global base paths. Keep **observed** only for what the official pages do not state (the `Expected whitespace character` text, `testFull` rejecting filters, JDK 17).
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/sbt/SKILL.md:42 and references/dependencies.md:10 say `%%%` covers Scala.js and Native without a version note. The official sbt 2 change summary says sbt 2 adds a `platform` setting so that `%%` cross-builds on JVM, JS and Native, and describes `%%%` as the sbt 1 plugin workaround.
  - Suggested: Add to dependencies.md Coordinates: "On sbt 2, `%%` also resolves the JS or Native platform through the `platform` setting; `%%%` is the sbt 1 plugin operator." Shorten SKILL.md:42 to match.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/sbt/references/dependencies.md:18-29 (eviction) and SKILL.md:35 (plugins) omit two items from the official sbt 2 change summary that change what a user sees: sbt 2 enforces the eviction error in the `Test` configuration, and sbt 2 plugins are published with the `_sbt2_3` suffix. SKILL.md:35 says to check that a plugin "publishes an sbt 2 artifact" without saying how to recognise one.
  - Suggested: dependencies.md: add "sbt 2 also fails the build on an eviction error in `Test`; fix it with the upgrade or a `libraryDependencySchemes` entry." SKILL.md:35: "...check that it publishes an artifact with the `_sbt2_3` suffix."

### ssot-consolidate

The skill routes on explicit prompts and gives Haiku a measurable report structure, but docs-audit claims the same job and carries a near-verbatim copy of its workflow. The evals now hold 7 cases (5 existing untouched, 1 implicit routing case and 1 value case added). Two cases are left failing: the implicit trigger (Haiku never opens any skill) and the docs-only negative (the skill fired in 2 of 3 final runs).

**Routing:** 4/6 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-implicit-upload-limit (1/3, no skill opened), ssot-quiet-docs-only (1/3, skill fired on a docs-only prompt). Passing 3/3: ssot-dedupe, ssot-timeout, ssot-quiet-docs, ssot-quiet-imports.

**Value cases:**

- `value-audit-report-contract`: 0.89 with, 0.00 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, overlap.** Two skills own the same job. packages/skills/skills/docs-audit/SKILL.md:3 says docs-audit "Also owns one fact repeated across code, config, CI and docs whose copies disagree", and docs-audit/SKILL.md:69 points to references/one-fact.md, a near-verbatim copy of ssot-consolidate/SKILL.md:20-51. Meanwhile ssot-consolidate/SKILL.md:3 and :12 claim the mixed-surface case and send only docs-only duplication to docs-audit. The evals contradict each other too: evals/docs-audit/docs-audit-one-fact-retry and docs-audit-one-fact-timeout use word-for-word the prompts of evals/ssot-consolidate/ssot-dedupe and ssot-timeout but expect docs-audit to fire. With all skills loaded, Haiku read ssot-consolidate and never docs-audit on these two prompts (11 of 12 runs; the other run opened nothing).
  - Suggested: Pick one owner. Either delete ssot-consolidate and keep docs-audit/references/one-fact.md, or (what Haiku's routing favours) remove the "Also owns one fact..." sentence and the "or for one source of truth" trigger from docs-audit's description, drop one-fact.md, and delete or flip the two docs-audit-one-fact-* cases. Do not keep both.
- **medium, description.** The docs-only boundary does not hold reliably. evals/ssot-consolidate/ssot-quiet-docs-only (rollback steps drifted across three docs) scored 3/3 in the first run but 1/3 in the final run, where ssot-consolidate was read in 2 of 3 runs. The exclusion sits at the end of SKILL.md:3, after "or the copies disagree", which matches the prompt's "wording has drifted".
  - Suggested: Put the surface constraint in the trigger clause, not only in the trailing exclusion, e.g. "Use when a value lives in code or config as well as elsewhere (CI, scripts, docs) and the copies disagree...". Not tested.
- **medium, accuracy.** SKILL.md:17 sends agent instruction files to `agent-instructions`, which does not exist in any of the four skills directories of this repo. docs-audit/SKILL.md:10 hedges the same reference with "if installed"; this skill does not.
  - Suggested: Change line 17 to "Agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md): out of scope" or add "if installed", and drop the name from the description's "or agent instructions" clause if nothing owns it.
- **medium, no-measurable-value.** The skill's behavioural rules changed nothing for Haiku on two things tried. (1) SKILL.md:31 and :39, never decide a contradiction silently: given three disagreeing timeout values and a user going offline, Haiku answered `VALUE: UNDECIDED` 3/3 with the skill and 3/3 without. (2) SKILL.md:42, report a MISS for a missing target: for an approved plan with one vanished target, Haiku scored 0.25 with and 0.25 without, because it did not open the skill for a post-approval prompt even when it was the only skill loaded, and called the edit "blocked" or "obsolete". Both trial cases were removed. The only measurable gain is the report format at SKILL.md:25-29 (value-audit-report-contract: 0.89 with, 0.00 without).
  - Suggested: Cut the rules a model already follows (SKILL.md:37-39 largely restate steps 7-10) and keep what the eval shows is added: the classification kinds, the per-hit actions, the report table and the explicit approval gate. If the MISS status matters, the description must also cover resuming an approved plan, e.g. "...or when applying an approved consolidation plan"; not tested.
- **low, description.** Implicit trigger evals/ssot-consolidate/route-implicit-upload-limit scores 1/3 and 1/3 with all skills loaded, and 3/3 with the skill loaded alone. In every failing run Haiku opened no skill at all (it grepped the empty workspace, then answered); it never lost to a sibling. A rewritten description did not help: 0/3 on this case and 2/3 on ssot-timeout, with all skills loaded.
  - Suggested: No description change recommended. The tested text was: "Consolidates one fact (a limit, timeout, version, retry policy) that is hardcoded in several places across code, config, CI, scripts and docs into a single home the others reference. ... Use when the same value has to be changed in several places, the copies show different numbers, or someone wants one source of truth or to change it in one spot. ...". This matches the known Haiku baseline of not opening skills on an empty workspace.
- **low, structure.** The Rules section repeats the workflow. SKILL.md:38 repeats steps 2 and 8 (:23, :29), :39 repeats step 10 (:31), and :40 repeats step 9 (:30). "Before finishing" item 1 (:48) repeats them again. "Scope" (:12) and the first "Not for" bullet (:16) both state the docs-audit boundary.
  - Suggested: Keep in Rules only what the workflow does not say (lines 37, 41, 42, 43, 44), and merge the Scope paragraph into "Not for".
- **low, instructions.** Step 3 (SKILL.md:24) requires a second search, and step 2 (:23) says "across the given files and platforms", but nothing says what to do when the copies are pasted and no repo is available. In the value runs Haiku improvised: "I'd grep the repo... I can't do that without the checkout".
  - Suggested: Add to step 3: "When the repo is not available, say the second search was not run and list the terms to search before any edit."

**Eval changes**

Implicit positive trigger: an upload limit with four different values in nginx, Helm, an API constant and docs; no skill name, no "source of truth", "copies" or "canonical". With all skills loaded it scored 1/3 twice; with the skill loaded alone, 3/3. Failures are runs where no skill was opened.

### subagent-workflows

The skill had no evals; it now has 4 cases in packages/agents/evals/subagent-workflows/ (2 positive routes, 1 near-miss negative, 1 value case) and all load cleanly. On Haiku the skill clearly helps when read (value case 1.00 with, 0.17 without). Routing is solid for drafting requests, but run-style requests are never opened because the eval harness has no SubagentWorkflow tool and the description says the skill applies only when it is available. A second value idea on shipped-workflow defaults did not discriminate and was dropped.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: route-implicit-meta-literal-error (1/3 in the final run, 2/3 in the first; 3/3 with the skill loaded alone). route-draft-per-file-audit-script 3/3, route-negative-github-actions-matrix 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-script-runtime-behaviour`: 1.00 with, 0.17 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, description.** packages/agents/skills/subagent-workflows/SKILL.md:4 ends with 'Applies only when the SubagentWorkflow tool is available.' Haiku takes this literally: on a fair run-style prompt (per-file security audit, unknown file count, refuter per finding) it scored 0/3 with the skill loaded alone, and its replies said the skill 'only applies when that tool is present'. The user's own ~/.pi/agent/subagents.json sets workflowToolExposure to 'deferred', a mode references/script-api.md:66 describes as needing tool_search, so the tool can be absent from the list in real sessions too. Part of the 0/3 is the harness, which has no subagent tool at all.
  - Suggested: Replace the last sentence with: 'Read it to plan or draft a workflow even when the SubagentWorkflow tool is not listed: the tool can be deferred (find it with tool_search) or switched off.' Tested on a copy with only this change, same run-style prompt: 3/3 with the skill alone (was 0/3), still 0/3 with --all-skills (Haiku finds an empty workspace and stops before opening any skill, the known baseline).
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/agents/skills/subagent-workflows/SKILL.md:63 says '`gate` cannot combine with `resume`, `schema`, `agentType`, `model`, `effort`, `isolation` or `disallowedTools` on a resumed call.' Read plainly, this forbids gate with schema or agentType. That list is the restriction on `resume` (references/script-api.md:28), and the shipped scripts combine gate with those options (workflows/bug-remediation.js:151 gate+agentType+schema, workflows/plan-slice-implement.js:118 gate+isolation). Haiku still answered the gate+resume question correctly, so the eval did not expose it.
  - Suggested: Rewrite as: 'A call with `resume` cannot also carry `gate`, `schema`, `agentType`, `model`, `effort`, `isolation` or `disallowedTools`; put the gate on the first call or on a separate verify agent.'
- **low, overlap.** The `plan-slice-implement` workflow (SKILL.md:21) and the sibling skill packages/skills/skills/implement-plan (SKILL.md:3, 'Executes an approved multi-slice implementation plan file ... in parallel worktrees') do the same job by different means, and neither mentions the other. A user saying 'implement this plan' gets no guidance on which applies. Not measured by an eval.
  - Suggested: Add one line to the paragraph at SKILL.md:35: when to use the `plan-slice-implement` workflow versus the `implement-plan` skill (for example, the workflow only when the user asks for a workflow run or the plan came from `feature-plan`).
- **low, structure.** SKILL.md:78-84 ('Adding a workflow to this package') is maintainer guidance with repo paths (packages/agents/workflows/, packages/agents/README.md, pnpm --filter) that do not exist where the skill is installed from npm, yet every user loads it. The description (SKILL.md:4) advertises it too ('or when adding a workflow to this package').
  - Suggested: Move the section to references/ (or the package README) and leave a one-line pointer; state in the pointer that it applies only inside the pi-tools repo.

**Eval changes**

Positive trigger: asks for an orchestration script with a runtime-sized fan-out and a refuter per finding, no skill name or tool name. 3/3 with all skills, 3/3 alone. ### test-gap-audit

The skill body is sound and measurably helps Haiku on its severity scale (1.00 with, 0.25 without), but its description does not get it opened under competition: all three positive triggers score 0/3 with all skills loaded and 3/3 with the skill alone. A tested description rewrite takes the same cases to 3/3 each with all skills loaded. The evals now hold 5 cases (3 positive triggers, 1 near-miss negative, 1 value case); the last runs of each are on the final file contents and --list loads all 5 with 0 errors.

**Routing:** 1/4 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: test-gap-audit-routing (0/3), trigger-test-gap-audit-1 (0/3), trigger-test-gap-audit-2 (0/3); passing: route-negative-write-one-test (3/3). Skill loaded alone: 4/4 at 3/3. With the tested description rewrite and all skills: 4/4 at 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-gap-severity-levels`: 1.00 with, 0.25 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, description.** packages/skills/skills/test-gap-audit/SKILL.md:3. With all skills loaded on Haiku the skill is never opened on fair triggers: test-gap-audit-routing 0/3, trigger-test-gap-audit-1 0/3, trigger-test-gap-audit-2 0/3 (run route-all2). With the skill loaded alone the same cases score 3/3 each (run route-alone), and no sibling skill was read in the failing runs. So it does not lose to a sibling; Haiku lists the empty workspace or answers from memory before reading any skill. The description also names `unit-testing`, which does not exist.
  - Suggested: Tested: 3/3 on all three positive triggers and 3/3 on the negative, with all skills loaded on Haiku (run route-alt1; was 0/3, 0/3, 0/3). Text: "Read-only audit of missing, weak and stale tests for a repo, PR, feature or route. Read this first, before listing or opening any file, whenever the user asks which code lacks tests, whether a change is covered well enough to merge, what could break that no test would catch, what regression tests a PR needs, or how severe a set of test gaps is. Maps source to tests with a bundled script, ranks gaps P0-P3 by behavior and risk (never coverage percentage) and proposes exact tests. Not for writing or fixing a given test, or for running the suite."
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/test-gap-audit/SKILL.md:3 and :10 point to `unit-testing` for writing a test, and :10 points to `problem-solving` for bug hunting. Neither exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills (`problem-solving` exists only under ~/.agents/skills). `test-run` and `security-scan` do exist.
  - Suggested: Drop the two names and describe the boundary instead: "Not for writing one test, running the suite (`test-run`), bug hunting, or security review (`security-scan`, if installed)." Or name the per-stack testing skills that do exist (java-testing, kotlin-testing, dotnet-testing, godot-testing, android-testing, spring-boot-testing).
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/test-gap-audit/SKILL.md:48-53. The severity table mixes two axes: P0 and P1 are defined by consequence (billing, common user paths), P2 and P3 by gap type (validation, weak tests). A gap can match two rows. Evidence, run value1: in the two runs where Haiku read the skill, it rated "test_discount.py mocks calculate_discount and only asserts it was called" P1 both times (P2 by the 'stale and weak tests' row), and "POST /orders has no test for zero or negative quantity" P1 once (P2 by the 'validation' row). Once the items were limited to gaps that match exactly one row, Haiku scored 1.00 (run value2).
  - Suggested: Add one tie-break line under the table, for example: "When a gap matches two rows, rate it by the consequence of the untested behavior (the higher row), so a weak or mocked-away test guarding billing is P0 or P1, not P2. P2 is for weak tests and edge cases on behavior that is neither P0 nor P1."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/test-gap-audit/SKILL.md:30-34 says "Run the bundled script from the repo" and then gives `python3 scripts/coverage_map.py --top 25`. That path is relative to the skill directory, not the repo. Run from a repo as written it fails: "can't open file '.../scripts/coverage_map.py': No such file or directory" (reproduced in /tmp). `--top 25` is also the default (scripts/coverage_map.py:326).
  - Suggested: Say where the path resolves: "Run the bundled script (in this skill's directory) with the repo as working directory: `python3 <skill dir>/scripts/coverage_map.py`." Five other skills use the same bare `python3 scripts/...` form, so this may be worth fixing as a convention.
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/test-gap-audit/SKILL.md:44 lists "test-list commands" among checks that write nothing, then bans `compileall` because it leaves `.pyc` files. To my knowledge `pytest --collect-only` imports the test modules and so writes `__pycache__` and `.pytest_cache`, the same kind of ignored artifact. Not verified here: pytest is not installed on this machine and I did not check the docs.
  - Suggested: Either drop "test-list commands" from the write-nothing examples, or qualify it: "test-list commands that do not import code; for pytest add `-p no:cacheprovider` and set `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`".
- **low, no-measurable-value.** Three other value ideas showed no gain on Haiku at 3 runs and were not kept. (1) Run/ask/never sorting of audit commands from SKILL.md:44: with 0.78, without 0.70, and the skill was not opened in any with-run, so this is unmeasured rather than disproved. Bare Haiku already asks before running pytest and refuses formatters; only `compileall` (ASK instead of NEVER) and sometimes `pip install` differ. (2) Keep or drop suggested tests per SKILL.md:17-19 (presentation, framework behavior, new dependency, e2e for a pure function): with 0.85, without 1.00; the skill was not opened in any with-run. (3) README note exempting billing from audits per SKILL.md:15: 1.00 with and 1.00 without; the skill was not opened and the answer format may have hinted at the right choice.

### test-run

test-run is a manual-only skill (disable-model-invocation: true), so it had no evals and can never route on its own; I added 5 cases: three routing cases that assert it stays quiet (two in-scope prompts, one sibling near-miss) and two value cases typed as /skill:test-run. Both value cases discriminate on Haiku at 3 runs (0.86 vs 0.00 and 1.00 vs 0.39). The one grader still failing points at a real defect: the skill prints its script commands as `python3 scripts/...` "from the project root", where those scripts do not exist.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; all three are must-not-fire cases (two in-scope prompts and one test-gap-audit near-miss), because the skill is manual-only (disable-model-invocation: true). No positive trigger exists or can pass while that flag is set.

**Value cases:**

- `value-custom-cmd-commands-invoked`: 0.86 with, 0.00 without
- `value-next-step-decisions-invoked`: 1.00 with, 0.39 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/SKILL.md:13-16, :20 and :47 tell the agent to run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py` / `scripts/run_custom.py` "from the project root", but the scripts are in the skill directory, not the project. In value-custom-cmd-commands-invoked Haiku wrote `python3 scripts/run_custom.py --cmd "bundle exec rspec"` in 3/3 runs (twice: first run and final run), even though pi's wrapper says references are relative to the skill directory. Run in the project root, that command fails with file not found. Grader t4-script-path-inside-skill-dir scores 0/3.
  - Suggested: Replace line 13 with: "The scripts live in this skill's directory (the directory of this SKILL.md), not in the project. Write their absolute path in every command; `<skill-dir>` below stands for that directory. From the project root, run this with a 10-minute Bash timeout:" and write `python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/run_tests.py` / `<skill-dir>/scripts/run_custom.py` at lines 16, 20 and 47. Tested on a copy in /tmp/skill-evals/test-run/alt: Haiku wrote the absolute skill path in 3/3 runs and the case scored 1.00 (0.86 with the current text).
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/SKILL.md:13 asks for "a Bash timeout of 600000 ms". That is Claude Code's unit. pi's bash tool takes its timeout in seconds (its schema reads "timeout in seconds"), so an agent that copies the number sets a limit of about 7 days instead of 10 minutes. Not measured by an eval (the runner has no shell).
  - Suggested: Say "a 10-minute Bash timeout (600 seconds in pi)" instead of a bare millisecond number.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/SKILL.md:3 and :20 say only the detected-runner script is "pre-approved" and that `run_custom.py` "is not pre-approved, so each call prompts"; scripts/run_custom.py:4 says "Not in the skill's allowed-tools". The frontmatter (lines 1-5) has no allowed-tools key, and pi does not prompt per bash call, so the stated safety property (line 21, "closes the arbitrary-command escape hatch") does not hold in this repo: nothing is pre-approved and nothing prompts.

- **low, description.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/SKILL.md:3 names the command as `/test-run:test-run`, the Claude Code plugin form. In pi the command is `/skill:test-run`. Since the skill is hidden from the model, the description is read only by the person picking the command, and half of it is about the approval mechanism rather than about what the command does. Also found while writing the evals: pi expands `/skill:test-run` only when text follows on the same line; followed by a bare newline it reaches the model as plain text (with arm scored the same as the bare arm, 0.64 vs 0.69, until the prompt was fixed).

Manual command: `/skill:test-run [targets | --all | --cmd "..."]`. Runs project code, so use on trusted projects only." Not routing-tested: the skill is manual by design, so no model-facing listing shows this text.

- **low, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/SKILL.md:59 points to `unit-testing` and `problem-solving`. Neither exists in the four skills directories of this repo (packages/skills, jj, agents, memory); `problem-solving` exists only under the user's own ~/.agents/skills. The "if installed" hedge keeps this from being an error, but `unit-testing` resolves to nothing here (test-gap-audit's description points to the same missing name).
  - Suggested: Drop the line, or name skills that ship here for the per-stack part (dotnet-testing, godot-testing, java-testing, kotlin-testing) and keep `problem-solving` with the "if installed" hedge.
- **low, structure.** packages/skills/skills/test-run/.ruff_cache/ is an untracked ruff cache inside the skill directory (git ls-files shows 0 entries for it, it carries its own .gitignore). ### trunk-based

The skill had no evals; it now has 4 cases (2 routing positives, 1 near-miss negative, 1 value case) that all load cleanly. The skill does help Haiku once it is read (value case 0.83 with vs 0.44 without), and it routes 3/3 on both positives when loaded alone, but with all skills loaded the implicit trigger is never opened (0/3). The main problems are that branching-models duplicates the whole skill, that the description is weak on implicit triggers, and that one rule sits only in a reference file Haiku never opens.

**Routing:** 2/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku (final run); failing: route-implicit-five-week-swap-on-main (0/3; 3/3 with the skill loaded alone, 2/3 with the tested description rewrite). route-crash-on-late-cut-release-branch 3/3 (2/3 in the first run), route-negative-add-unleash-flag 3/3.

**Value cases:**

- `value-team-habits-against-trunk-rules`: 0.83 with, 0.44 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **high, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/branching-models/SKILL.md:100-118 restates nearly every rule of this skill (short-lived branch, revert red trunk, flags, branch by abstraction, release from trunk, branch for release with cherry-pick -x, the anti-pattern list, the multi-agent worktree note). Its description (line 3) also claims "trunk-based", "release branch cherry-pick" and "should we use trunk-based or git-flow". packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/references/detection.md is byte-identical to branching-models/references/detection.md (diff is empty). In addition trunk-based/SKILL.md:3 and git-flow/SKILL.md:3 both list the trigger "which branching model should we use". I did not measure which skill wins a head-to-head; in my all-skills runs Haiku opened either trunk-based or nothing, never branching-models.
  - Suggested: Decide on one owner. Either remove the Trunk-based section from branching-models and have it point to trunk-based, or retire trunk-based. Whichever stays, drop "which branching model should we use" from the trunk-based and git-flow descriptions and leave model choice to branching-models, and keep a single copy of detection.md.
- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/SKILL.md:3. The implicit trigger route-implicit-five-week-swap-on-main (a five-week replacement in a repo with no long-lived branches and deploy-on-merge) scored 0/3 in both all-skills runs: Haiku opened no skill at all and answered from memory. Loaded alone, the same prompt routed 3/3, so the skill is not losing to a sibling; the description simply does not describe the situation. It lists quoted keywords ("branch by abstraction") and nothing about landing a large change in pieces.
  - Suggested: Tested rewrite (copy of the skill under /tmp/skill-evals/trunk-based/alt with all 172 siblings symlinked, --all-skills, Haiku, 3 runs): implicit case 2/3 (was 0/3), release-branch case 3/3 (was 2/3 then 3/3), negative 3/3. Text: "Rules and git sequences for trunk-based development: everyone integrates into main at least daily, branches live a day or two, unfinished or multi-week work lands in pieces behind feature flags or branch by abstraction instead of on a long-lived branch, release branches are cut late and fed by cherry-picks from main, tags sit on main. Use when a repo has no develop branch and deploys or releases from main, and the question is how to land a large change or migration on main without a long-lived branch, where to fix a bug found on a release branch, how to cut or patch a release from main, or whether a team's branching habits fit trunk-based development; also for \"trunk-based\", \"short-lived branches\", \"branch by abstraction\". Not for git-flow or develop-branch repos (git-flow), HubFlow (hubflow), adding or removing one flag in code (feature-flags), rewriting history (git-history) or publishing a GitHub release (gh-release)."
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/references/release.md:25 is the only place that says one person (a rotating "Merge Meister") does the cherry-picks. SKILL.md:73 points to that file only "for the exact plain-git sequences", so a model has no reason to open it for a process question. In the value case, item H6 (one rotating person does all cherry-picks: OK) passed in 1 of 6 runs with the skill loaded; no run opened release.md, and one answer said "The skill doesn't name who cherry-picks, so this is my judgment".
  - Suggested: Move the rule into SKILL.md:76 ("One person, a rotating Merge Meister, does the cherry-picks, not each fix author") and keep release.md for commands only.
- **medium, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/SKILL.md:3 and :14 name a `git-commit` skill. No such skill exists in packages/skills/skills, packages/jj/skills, packages/agents/skills or packages/memory/skills (it exists only in the user's own ~/.agents/skills). Line 14 hedges with "when it is installed"; the description on line 3 does not.
  - Suggested: Remove "commit messages or branch names (git-commit)" from the description, and reword line 14 to "Follow the repo's existing branch naming and commit message conventions." Add feature-flags to the description's exclusions instead: it is the real neighbour ("feature flag unfinished work" on line 3 currently overlaps with it).
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/SKILL.md:61 allows a branch to live "hours to about two days" with "no intermediate merges to trunk (merge once, to close it)", while line 63 says "Commit to trunk at least once every 24 hours". A two-day branch merged once cannot satisfy line 63. Found by reading; in an early draft case Haiku with the skill loaded judged a day-one intermediate merge both ways.
  - Suggested: State one rule, for example: "A branch lives hours, two days at most; if it would outlive 24 hours, split the work so something lands on trunk each day. Never merge the same branch twice."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/trunk-based/SKILL.md:63 "Aim for three or fewer active branches (DORA)" does not say whether this is per repo or per team, or how firm it is. In the first value run Haiku read the line and still judged eight open branches for nine developers as fine in 2 of 3 runs ("a DORA aim ... doesn't need fixing"); in the final run it applied it 3 of 3.
  - Suggested: Say what the number counts and how to treat it, for example: "DORA: three or fewer active branches in the repo at any time; flag a higher count even when every branch is short-lived."

Positive trigger with no skill name: a crash found on a late-cut release/5.3 that main also has, asking where to fix, how to carry it over and whether to merge the release branch back. All skills on Haiku: 2/3 in the first run, 3/3 in the final run; 3/3 with the skill loaded alone.

New implicit trigger: a five-week job-queue replacement in a repo with no long-lived branches and deploy-on-merge (branch by abstraction, never named). 0/3 with all skills in both runs (no skill opened at all), 3/3 with the skill loaded alone, 2/3 with the tested description rewrite. Left failing as a description problem.

### ts-module-boundaries

The skill is accurate where it matters: I ran its config asset under dependency-cruiser 18.9 on a fixture and every rule, the exit-code claim and the TypeScript 7.0 silent-pass claim behaved as written. It had no evals; it now has five (three routing, two value), all loading cleanly, and both value cases score 1.00 with the skill against 0.54-0.60 without on Haiku. The skill is manual (disable-model-invocation: true), so routing cases assert it does not load on its own, following the debloat/reorder convention; no positive trigger is possible while that flag is set.

**Routing:** 3/3 cases pass at 3 runs with --all-skills on Haiku; failing: none. All three are must-not-load assertions (two in-scope manual, one near-miss negative) because the skill is hidden from the model by disable-model-invocation; no positive trigger exists.

**Value cases:**

- `value-import-verdicts`: 1.00 with, 0.60 without
- `value-setup-decisions`: 1.00 with, 0.54 without

**Skill: what should change**

- **medium, description.** packages/skills/skills/ts-module-boundaries/SKILL.md:3-4: the description ends with "Use when the user asks to enforce package boundaries, stop deep imports or add dependency-cruiser", but line 4 sets disable-model-invocation: true, so the model never sees that text. Evidence: in the route1 logs the skill name does not appear in the system prompt at all, and on both in-scope prompts (explicit and implicit, 3 runs each, all skills loaded) Haiku read no skill and answered from memory with ESLint or ad hoc dependency-cruiser advice.
  - Suggested: Decide which is intended. If manual: reword as the other manual skills do, e.g. "Manual command that sets up dependency-cruiser in a TypeScript repo so each package is reachable only through its root entry-point files, with no deep imports and no cycles, then proves the rules fail on a violation." If it should trigger: remove line 4 and turn the two route-quiet cases into positive triggers. Not tested: either option changes more than the description text, so the alt-description procedure did not apply.
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/ts-module-boundaries/SKILL.md:34: "Packages root from `the arguments given with the command`" is a substituted argument placeholder left in code formatting, so it reads as a literal value rather than an instruction.
  - Suggested: Write it as prose: "Packages root: the path the user gave when invoking the skill, else `src/packages` if `src/` exists, else `packages`."
- **low, accuracy.** packages/skills/skills/ts-module-boundaries/SKILL.md:36: "18.6 supports `>=2 <7`, and TypeScript 7 support waits on a stable compiler API" is stale. `npx depcruise --info` on dependency-cruiser 18.9.0 (current) reports `>=2.0.0 <7.0.0||>=7.1.0 <8.0.0`. The behaviour described is still right for TypeScript 7.0.x, which is npm `latest` (7.0.2): I observed 0 modules cruised, the missing-typescript-transpiler warning and exit 0.
  - Suggested: Drop the pinned range and tell the agent to read it from `--info`: "dependency-cruiser supports a bounded TypeScript range, shown in the `versions supported` column of `--info` (18.9 excludes 7.0.x). Outside it ...".
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/ts-module-boundaries/SKILL.md:47: "If step 2 does not fail" means sub-step 5.2 (the temporary deep import), but top-level step 2 is Install, so the reference is ambiguous.
  - Suggested: "If the run with the temporary deep import does not fail, the rules or the cruised root are wrong; fix that before finishing."
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/ts-module-boundaries/SKILL.md:49: "the repo's `CLAUDE.md` (or `AGENTS.md`, creating it if neither exists)" puts CLAUDE.md first for a skill shipped to pi, which reads AGENTS.md, and "creating it" does not clearly say which file is created.
  - Suggested: "Add a one-line pointer from the repo's agent-instructions file (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, whichever exists; create `AGENTS.md` if neither does)".

Text: Rewrites a doc that has collected edit residue ("Update:" and "Note:" lines, corrections appended below the text they correct, "used to"/"now" wording, superseded steps, TBDs answered elsewhere) as a clean v0 that says only what is true now. Read this before rewriting any such doc, including one pasted into the chat and one whose rewrite looks obvious, because it sets what to link, what to leave untouched and what to report. Use when asked to clean up, refresh, bring up to date, sync up or de-noise a doc after rounds of edits, when readers keep missing a correction, or when related docs have drifted apart. Not for changelogs, ADRs, plans, density-only tightening, or docs-vs-code drift (docs-audit).
- **medium, overlap.** packages/skills/skills/doc-tidy/SKILL.md:16-20 and :31-37 restate this skill's rules as its default --v0 mode (residue removal, source of truth, unwrap and link, nothing-to-improve, MISS, no new files), so the same rules live in two files. They have already diverged: doc-tidy line 18 says 'If none settles it, keep both and report the conflict', while v0-rewrite SKILL.md:36-37 says to surface judgment calls and repair from the source of truth but not what to write when no source settles a contradiction.
  - Suggested: Keep one home for the v0 rules. Either have doc-tidy --v0 point at v0-rewrite, or copy the missing sentence into v0-rewrite SKILL.md:37: 'If no source settles a contradiction, keep both values and report the conflict.' Not tested as a skill change; bare Haiku already did this in the conflict case I tried (1.00 with and without).
- **medium, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:10-14. 'Not for' says where the skill does not apply but not what the agent should then do. In run r7-value, a case asking to boil a four-version CHANGELOG down to current behaviour, the one run that read the skill wrote 'The v0-rewrite skill doesn't fit a changelog, since its history is the point' and then deleted all four version entries anyway. All three with-skill runs ended with 0 entries, the same as without the skill. The other two with-skill runs did not open the skill.
  - Suggested: Make line 12 an instruction: 'Changelogs, ADRs and plans: their append-only history is the point. Say so and stop; do not collapse or delete entries unless the user confirms they want the history gone.' Not tested.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:26. Step 9 packs three rules into one sentence and is followed unevenly. In run r5-value, one of three with-skill runs left both the section pointer and the file pointer as plain text, while bare Haiku linked the section pointer in 3 of 3 runs, so with and without both scored 0.78. '(matching sibling files)' is also ambiguous: it can read as 'unwrap only when sibling files are unwrapped' or as a reason to always unwrap.
  - Suggested: Split step 9 into separate bullets: one for unwrapping, one for linking ('Turn every plain-text pointer to a file or section into a relative link'), one for what to leave as formatted. State the unwrap condition outright, for example 'unless sibling files in the same directory are hard-wrapped'. Not tested.
- **low, instructions.** packages/skills/skills/v0-rewrite/SKILL.md:13 sends wordy-but-current prose to `debloat`, which is a manual command (disable-model-invocation: true in packages/skills/skills/debloat/SKILL.md), so the agent cannot follow the pointer itself. Separately, SKILL.md:41-44 'Before finishing' has no check that facts, numbers, warnings and conditions survived the rewrite; doc-tidy/SKILL.md:38 has that check.
